cards.name: EPA AirNow
cards.summary: The U.S. EPA's AirNow program serves real-time Air Quality Index readings (NowCast AQI) and agency-issued AQI forecasts from more than 2,500 monitoring stations run by over 150 local, state, tribal, provincial and federal agencies across the United States, Canada and Mexico. Keyless hourly files (reportingarea.dat by reporting area, HourlyAQObs and HourlyData by monitoring site) download from files.airnowtech.org; the AirNow API web services (by ZIP, lat/long, reporting area or bounding box) need a free account and key. The data are preliminary and unvalidated.
cards.short: The EPA's official real-time Air Quality Index for the US, Canada and Mexico; hourly, free, keyless files.

tasks: current NowCast AQI per pollutant for a reporting area (the peak across the area's monitors), by ZIP code, lat/long or reporting area code
AQI forecasts by reporting area, ZIP or lat/long (where agencies issue them)
hourly observations by monitoring site: AQI for ozone, PM2.5, PM10 and NO2, and concentrations incl. CO and SO2 (keyless HourlyAQObs/HourlyData files, or the keyed bounding-box service)
PM2.5, ozone and combined AQI contour maps (KML) for a bounding box
action-day flags and forecast discussions from air agencies

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: Free. The file products on files.airnowtech.org download without a key; the web services need a free AirNow API account and key.

latency.typical: Observations for the previous hour are generally available 10-30 minutes past the hour; reportingarea.dat is updated twice per hour at :25 and :55
latency.notes: AirNow FAQ: observations update once per hour and forecasts are issued once per day. On 2026-10-27 04:59 UTC the keyless reportingarea.dat (last modified 04:42 UTC) held observations for 00:00 EDT (04:00 UTC), and HourlyData for 03:00 UTC was last modified 04:54 UTC.

coverage.notes: AirNow covers the United States, Canada and Mexico. AQI by reporting area (reportingarea.dat and the ZIP/lat-long services) is for US reporting areas plus Mexicali; Canadian and most Mexican data appear as monitoring sites in the hourly site files. Reporting areas range from part of a city to a whole county, and the lat/long and ZIP services return the reporting area's peak value, not the nearest monitor. Forecasts are not issued for every area, every day or every season.

licensing.summary: EPA AirNow Data Use Guidelines (account sign-up also requires agreeing to a Data Use Agreement): the data are preliminary, not fully verified or validated, and must not be used for regulation, trends, guidance or other government or public decision-making (official data come from EPA's AQS). The federal, state, local and tribal agencies own the data. Users must credit those agencies and EPA AirNow, disseminate values and advisories unaltered, use the AQI colours, label displays and products as preliminary, tell the agencies and EPA AirNow when products rely on the data, and keep their contact details current. AI training and resale are not mentioned.

freshness.typical_age: Under about 1.5 hours
freshness.notes: Historical observation and forecast services exist; irlpls lists AirNow for current readings.

delivery.basis: AirNow FAQ: "air quality observations for the previous hour are generally available between 10 and 30 minutes past the hour."

auth.how_to_get: The file products on https://files.airnowtech.org/ (e.g. /airnow/today/reportingarea.dat, /airnow/{YYYY}/{YYYYMMDD}/HourlyAQObs_{YYYYMMDDHH}.dat) download without a key.

Request an account at https://docs.airnowapi.org/account/request/ (name, user name, email, phone, agency, comment, and agreement to the Data Use Agreement and Data Use Guidelines), activate it with the emailed confirmation code, then copy the key from the top right of the Web Services page; it is passed as the API_KEY query parameter.

endpoints.params: None. Pipe-delimited: issue date|valid date|valid time|time zone|hour offset|record type (O observation, F forecast)|current flag|reporting area|state|lat|lon|parameter|AQI|category|action day|discussion|agency
endpoints.notes: No key; different host from base_url. Current observations and forecasts for every reporting area, updated at :25 and :55. Pair with https://files.airnowtech.org/airnow/today/cityzipcodes.csv (ZIP to reporting area, updated daily).

endpoints.params: Date and hour in UTC
endpoints.notes: No key; different host from base_url. CSV, one row per monitoring site: AQSID, site name, status, lat/lon, country code, valid date/time, data source, reporting area, ozone/PM10/PM2.5/NO2 AQI and concentrations of PM2.5, ozone, NO2, CO, SO2 and PM10. HourlyData_{YYYYMMDDHH}.dat has the raw hourly values per site and parameter.

Current observations for the reporting area of a lat/long or ZIP (new June 2026). Needs API_KEY; without it returns HTTP 401 'Request not authenticated.' Per-service parameter docs are visible only when logged in.
Current observations by reporting area code (new June 2026). Needs API_KEY.
Current forecasts by ZIP, lat/long or reporting area code (new June 2026). Needs API_KEY.
Hourly observations (AQI and/or concentrations) by monitoring site in a bounding box, for a date/time range. Needs API_KEY.
PM2.5 AQI contour map (KML) for a bounding box and hour; /KML/Ozone/ and /KML/Combined/ likewise. Needs API_KEY.

api.rate_limits: Web services: per key, per service, per hour (each service's limit is in its own docs, visible only when logged in); once hit, the service returns no data until the next hour, and limits cannot be raised. AirNow asks users to cache, and not to loop over ZIP codes to build a database (use the file products instead).

mcp.community: io.github.pipeworx-io/airnow v0.1.5 (Pipeworx, third party), remote https://gateway.pipeworx.io/airnow/mcp; keyless, reads AirNow's public file products

api.notes: The six older web services (e.g. /aq/observation/latLong/current/, /aq/forecast/zipCode/) were retired on 2026-09-30; their docs pages now redirect to /webservices/retired. File products are on a second host, files.airnowtech.org, so their endpoint paths are full URLs.

payment.notes: No payment: the service is free.

requester.checks: None for the keyless file products. A web-service account asks for name, email, phone and agency, is activated by an emailed confirmation code, and requires agreeing to the Data Use Guidelines; users who keep exceeding rate limits may be contacted.
requester.unknown: Nothing is commissioned; monitors report on their own schedule.

human.unknown: Not applicable: automated monitors operated by air agencies

application.unknown: No signing or published hashes of data from monitor to file or API

camera.unknown: No imagery

time.method: Each observation is reported for a stated valid date and hour, with its time zone or UTC offset
time.unknown: How monitor clocks are checked is not documented in the pages read

location.method: Values belong to a named reporting area or to a monitoring site with an AQS ID and latitude/longitude
location.unknown: Lat/long and ZIP queries return the reporting area's peak value, which may come from a monitor some distance away; site coordinates are as reported by agencies

content.unknown: AirNow labels its data raw, preliminary and not fully verified or validated; values come from agency-operated monitors and can change after agency validation (official data are in AQS), and no real-time quality-control method is described in the pages read

corroboration.unknown: No per-reading cross-check documented; a reporting area's value is the maximum across its monitors, not a cross-check

sources.claim: AirNow covers the United States, Canada and Mexico; over 2,500 monitoring stations; forecasts for more than 500 cities; more than 150 local, state, tribal, provincial and federal agencies; data not fully verified or validated, preliminary, not for regulation, trends, guidance or government or public decision making; official data from AQS

Web services list: current forecasts by reporting area, lat/long or ZIP; historical forecasts; PM2.5, ozone and combined KML contour maps; observations by monitoring site (hourly and daily bounding box); current observations by reporting area and by ZIP or lat/long; historical observations by state

API key at top right of Web Services page; users must follow the Data Use Guidelines; per-key per-service hourly rate limits that cannot be changed; observations updated hourly, available 10-30 minutes past the hour; forecasts daily; cache results; reporting areas from part of a city to a county; forecasts not available for every area; area observation is the maximum across its monitors; ZIP and lat/long services return the reporting area peak AQI; do not loop over ZIP codes; reportingarea.dat on files.airnowtech.org updated at :55 and :25; cityzipcodes.csv updated daily

Account required for web services and feeds; activate with emailed confirmation code; key on Web Services page; NowCast AQI per pollutant; CSV, JSON or XML output; six web services retired in September 2026; file products on files.airnowtech.org

New services from June 17, 2026: /aq/forecast/current/, /aq/observation/current/racode/, /aq/observation/current/ziplatlong/, /aq/observation/historical/state/, /aq/dailydata/, /aq/forecast/historical/; six older services (e.g. /aq/observation/latLong/current/) retired September 30, 2026; /aq/data/ and /KML/PM25/, /KML/Ozone/, /KML/Combined/ remain

Data Use (Exchange) Guidelines: preliminary data, not for regulation or decision-making; agencies own the data; credit agencies and EPA AirNow; do not alter values or advisories; use AQI colours; label products preliminary; notify agencies and EPA AirNow of reliance; keep contact details current
Account request form: name, user name, email, phone, agency, comment; must agree to the Data Use Agreement and the EPA AirNow Data Use Guidelines
AQI categories and colours; real-time values are NowCast AQI; forecasts issued by agencies per reporting area; action days

Keyless live check 2026-10-26 (04:59 UTC 27 Oct): 7,410 rows of current observations and forecasts by reporting area, newest observations for 00:00 EDT 27 Oct, last modified 04:42 UTC; US states plus Mexicali (MX)
Keyless hourly site file: 4,416 sites with country codes (US 2,726, CA 343, MX 75, others), AQI for ozone/PM10/PM2.5/NO2 and concentrations incl. CO and SO2
ZIP to reporting area lookup file with ZIP centroids, no key
A keyless call to the new current-observations service returns HTTP 401 'Request not authenticated.' (tested 2026-10-26)
No first-party MCP server; third-party io.github.pipeworx-io/airnow (v0.1.5, remote https://gateway.pipeworx.io/airnow/mcp)

cards.name: Airtasker
cards.summary: Local task marketplace: post a task with location, timing and budget, Taskers make offers, and accepting one holds the payment in escrow. Official remote MCP server with OAuth can post tasks, read offers and accept one; releasing payment and receiving proof happen in the web app.
cards.short: Post a local task; nearby Taskers offer, and payment is held until you release it.

tasks: errands and deliveries
local photography
checking or inspecting something in person
handyman and home tasks

pricing.model: offer-based task price plus one-time Connection Fee (waived for members)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published (the task price is set by Taskers' offers). Posting a task is free. Connection Fee by task price, charged on assignment: AU AUD 9.95–59.95 (inc. GST); UK £4.95–39.95 (inc. VAT); US USD 4.90–49.50 (excl. tax); NZ NZD 9.95–59.95 and SG SGD 9.95–59.95 (excl. tax). Waived with a customer membership (AU, UK, US articles). Retained if the customer cancels.

latency.typical: Not published
latency.notes: Depends on Tasker offers and the agreed time. Unreleased payments auto-cancel 30 days after the Tasker marks a task complete.

coverage.notes: Country sites exist for these six (/au/, /uk/, /us/, /ie/, /nz/, /sg/; /ca/ returns 404). Density not published.

licensing.summary: The terms (updated 16 Feb 2026) say nothing about who owns a Tasker's photos or reports, and do not mention AI or machine-learning training. Clause 3.2: content on the platform may not be used on third-party sites or for other business purposes without Airtasker's written permission. Clause 3.5: users grant Airtasker a worldwide, royalty-free licence to content posted on the platform, including for promotion. The privacy policy does not mention model training.

human.method: Optional ID Verified badge in AU and NZ: government photo ID plus live biometric face scan via Persona. Taskers must complete ID verification before payment is released to them.
human.unknown: Only documented for AU and NZ. Taskers can make offers without it, the badge is a point-in-time check, and the terms say Airtasker does no checks before someone becomes a user.

application.unknown: Proof is sent as private-message attachments; no capture app is required.

camera.unknown: Nothing stops gallery or edited uploads.

time.unknown: No capture timestamp is recorded or checked.

location.unknown: No geo check-in or location check on deliverables.

content.method: Under the model Task Contract the Tasker warrants the work is done properly and the information true; the customer releases escrowed payment only when satisfied, with a dispute process.
content.unknown: Airtasker does not review deliverables and disclaims the accuracy of anything users provide; the customer is the only check.

corroboration.unknown: No independent check.

auth.how_to_get: Connect an MCP client to https://mcp.airtasker.com/mcp and complete the OAuth login with an Airtasker account (authorization server https://id.airtasker.com, which advertises a dynamic client registration endpoint and PKCE S256). Posting needs credits, a payment method on file or a membership.

endpoints.notes: Search the marketplace
Full task details
Details, location, timing, budget. Posting is free; nothing is charged until an offer is accepted.
Offers on your task
Hires the Tasker and escrows payment; charges the Connection Fee for non-members
Your tasks and their status
A Tasker's public profile and rating

mcp.notes: Streamable HTTP; answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata pointer. Also packaged as a Claude Code plugin (airtasker/airtasker-mcp-server). Not in the official MCP Registry. No tool to release payment, message the Tasker or read proof.

freshness.typical_age: Captured after assignment

delivery.basis: Offer-based; Airtasker publishes no turnaround time.

payment.notes: Card (Visa, Mastercard, AMEX in AU) via Airtasker Pay on Stripe; Airtasker credits are applied first. The MCP accept_offer tool charges the person's saved method and escrows the price; releasing payment to the Tasker is a manual web step.

requester.checks: Users must be natural persons over 18. Posting needs credits, a payment method on file or a membership. ID verification is optional for customers (AU, NZ).
requester.unknown: No documented review of what a task asks a Tasker to photograph or whom.

cards.name: ALERTCalifornia cameras (UC San Diego)
cards.short: 1,289 wildfire-watch PTZ cameras across California; latest frame about every 15 s, no key.
cards.summary: UC San Diego's statewide network of high-definition pan-tilt-zoom wildfire cameras with near-infrared night vision, aimed by trained first responders. A public ArcGIS feature service lists every camera with location, online status, current pan/tilt/zoom and a latest-frame image URL. Free for non-commercial use under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

tasks: current still from a fixed-site PTZ camera
visual check for smoke, fire, snow, weather or visibility in California wildlands
night view via near-infrared
find cameras by county, radius or bounding box

pricing.model: free (non-commercial)
pricing.notes: Free for non-commercial use with credit. For-profit (commercial) use needs a commercial licence negotiated with UC San Diego's OIC 'with appropriate licensing fees'; no price published.

latency.typical: seconds to minutes
latency.notes: Provider: camera images update approximately every 15 seconds; camera direction and viewsheds update every two minutes, and images may run ahead of the orientation fields. Sampled 2026-10-26 ~22:01 PDT: latest-frame redirected to JPEGs 24 s and 31 s old; layer max viewTime ~2.5 min old, but some rows' viewTime lag ~24 h even when the frame is seconds old.

coverage.notes: 1,289 cameras in the feed, 1,252 online at ~22:01 PDT on 2026-10-26; all within California (feed extent 32.59 to 41.93 N). Ridgetop/backcountry sites that can see up to 60 miles by day and 120 miles on a clear night; not street cameras. Operators move the PTZ view and cameras sweep 360 degrees about every two minutes, so the field of view changes. Some mountaintop cameras go offline in winter ('winter mode').

licensing.summary: ALERTCalifornia program data is copyrighted by UC San Diego (Regents of the University of California) and licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial use with credit 'ALERTCalifornia | UC San Diego', no derivatives; do not crop the information bar or partner logos on screen grabs. For-profit use must contact OIC to negotiate a commercial licence with fees. AI or ML training is not named in the terms.

human.unknown: Capture is automatic. Cameras are aimed by trained first responders and emergency managers, but who aimed a given frame is not exposed.

application.unknown: No capture-app or device attestation is published; frames carry ordinary EXIF (make, model, firmware) that is not signed.

camera.method: Fixed Axis PTZ cameras operated by UC San Diego; the acquisition engine pulls images from the physical cameras over Axis VAPIX. A sampled frame's EXIF reads AXIS Q6075-E, 1920x1080.
camera.unknown: No per-image sensor proof: EXIF is unsigned, the sampled JPEG had no C2PA manifest, and Axis is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.method: Capture timestamp in the redirected object path, in the x-amz-meta-context timestamp and in EXIF DateTime; per-camera viewTime field in the feed.
time.unknown: Not signed or time-stamped by a third party; the layer's viewTime can lag the image by hours.

location.method: Fixed site coordinates in the feature service, plus pan/tilt/zoom attached to each stored image and in positionPan/positionTilt/viewZoomScale.
location.unknown: What is in frame depends on the current PTZ; the provider says images may advance ahead of orientation and viewshed updates.

content.unknown: No integrity checks on public frames are documented.

corroboration.unknown: Colocated cameras exist (colocatedCameras field), and AI fire detections are vetted by watchstanders, but no cross-check of public frames is published.

auth.how_to_get: The ArcGIS feature service and the latest-frame images are public; no key or sign-in.

endpoints.params: where=isOnline='online' (or county='<name>'); geometry=<lon,lat>&geometryType=esriGeometryPoint&distance=<m>&units=esriSRUnit_Meter&inSR=4326; outFields=*; resultOffset for paging; f=json
endpoints.notes: Returns cameraName, siteId, county, isOnline, colocatedCameras, cameraURL, positionPan, positionTilt, viewZoomScale, viewTime and imageURL per camera. At most 50 records per response (maxRecordCount 50).
302 to a timestamped 1920x1080 JPEG; Cache-Control max-age=10. The stored object carries device, pan, tilt, zoom and timestamp in x-amz-meta-context, and expires after about two days.

api.rate_limits: Not published. The feature service returns at most 50 records per query.

mcp.notes: No entry in the official MCP Registry (searched alertcalifornia, alert-california, ucsd).

api.notes: No OAuth: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and oauth-authorization-server return 404 on alertcalifornia.org and docs.rd.alertcalifornia.org, 403 on cameras.alertcalifornia.org. The 'Frontend API' at docs.rd.alertcalifornia.org is the operator backend behind an authenticated proxy (CIAM OAuth), not a public API; public users cannot move cameras.

freshness.typical_age: seconds to minutes
freshness.notes: Provider: images update approximately every 15 seconds.

delivery.basis: ArcGIS item: 'Camera images update approximately every 15 seconds.' Live samples on 2026-10-26 were 24 s and 31 s old.

payment.notes: No payment for non-commercial use. A commercial licence is negotiated with UC San Diego OIC; no payment method is published.

requester.checks: None for the public feed. First-responder log-ins (which can move cameras) are reserved for emergency managers trained by ALERTCalifornia. Archive footage requests are taken from media, scientists, partners and government agencies by email; law firms must use UC San Diego's Policy and Records Administration portal.
requester.unknown: Nothing can be commissioned; what checks apply to a commercial licence is not published.

Layer metadata: query-only capability, maxRecordCount 50
ArcGIS item: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 licence and OIC commercial licence; images update ~every 15 s, direction/viewsheds every 2 min; near-infrared night vision; 360-degree sweeps; 60/120-mile view
Terms: copyrighted, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, commercial licence via OIC with fees; footage request routes
Credit line 'ALERTCalifornia | UC San Diego'; do not crop the information bar or partner logos

Latest-frame redirect, x-amz-meta-context PTZ and timestamp, EXIF AXIS Q6075-E, ~2-day object expiry; sampled 24 s old (2026-10-26)
Latest frame 31 s old while the layer's viewTime for the same camera was ~24 h old (2026-10-26)

cards.name: Appen
cards.summary: AI training-data vendor that runs custom data collections with its contributor crowd (CrowdGen): remote collections where contributors capture image, video, audio and location data at home or in public on Appen's multi-device platform and the Appen Mobile app, and supervised on-site sessions (facilities, customer sites, studios, rented homes, in-car, AR/VR glasses and wearables). Sales-led; no ordering API for collections.
cards.short: A training-data vendor whose crowd records custom image, video and audio collections, remote or on-site.

tasks: custom remote image, video and audio collection by contributors at home or in public, using Appen's multi-device platform and the Appen Mobile app
supervised on-site collection sessions (Appen facilities, customer sites, studios, rented homes, in-car)
device collections with AR/VR glasses, wearables and smart-home devices, moderated on-site or remotely
mobile location and points-of-interest data collection

pricing.model: Not published; contact sales
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means unknown, not free. The data collection page routes to 'Talk to an expert'; no prices are published.

latency.typical: Not published
latency.notes: No project turnaround is stated. A 2022 contributor posting (reposted by a third party) describes survey and data collection tasks of 15 minutes to three hours each, which is task length, not project delivery.

coverage.notes: Appen cites 500+ global locales, 235+ languages and a crowd of over one million contractors; its contributor site says 500,000+ contributors have been paid. On-site sessions run 'across multiple countries'. Which countries have image/video collectors is not published.

licensing.summary: Not stated publicly. Appen publishes no customer terms of service on appen.com (its legal-policies page lists only privacy, cookie, ethical-sourcing, whistleblower, anti-corruption and scam pages); terms are set in a sales contract. Ownership, resale and AI-training rights for custom collections, and whether Appen reuses customer data, were not found. Appen cites SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

human.method: Contributors join through CrowdGen, Appen's contributor platform, where applicants must 'apply & get verified'; most projects add a qualification process.
human.unknown: What 'verified' checks (identity document, residency or only skills) is not described, and nothing ties a delivered capture to a verified person.

application.unknown: Remote collection runs on Appen's own platform and the Appen Mobile app, but no app or device integrity checks are documented.

camera.unknown: No check against imported, re-captured or generated media is described.

time.unknown: No trusted capture time is documented.

location.unknown: Location data is a collection type, but no method for verifying where an image or video was taken is documented. The Appen Mobile app's App Store privacy label lists only photos, videos and audio, not location.

content.unknown: Quality controls described (gold test questions, smart validators, multi-stage review on the annotation platform; 'data abnormality detection' in a 2019 blog) apply to labeling. No review method for collected media is described.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check is described.

api.rate_limits: Not applicable; collections are ordered through sales.
api.notes: No API orders a data collection. Appen's separate annotation platform (ADAP) has a REST API at https://api.appen.com/ (OpenAPI at https://developer.appen.com/open-api.yaml; header 'Authorization: Token token=<key>', key generated in the client profile) covering projects, uploads, WORK and QA jobs, launch, status and CSV downloads. Its create-job call supports only WORK and QA types, not the DATA_COLLECTION job type, and platform access itself routes to 'Talk to our team'. No MCP server is listed in the official MCP Registry.

payment.notes: No payment methods are published; collections are priced and contracted through sales.

freshness.typical_age: Collected for your project
freshness.notes: Appen also sells 360+ off-the-shelf datasets in 80+ languages; only custom collection is described here.

delivery.basis: No turnaround published.

cards.name: Caltrans highway cameras
cards.summary: Caltrans' Commercial Wholesale Web Portal (CWWP2) publishes free, keyless per-district JSON/XML/CSV/TXT lists of its ~3,600 California State Highway CCTV cameras, each with coordinates, route/postmile, in-service flag, a current still-image URL refreshed every 1-60 minutes, 12 previous stills, and (for about two-thirds) an HLS streaming URL. Some in-service cameras serve a 'Temporarily Unavailable' placeholder instead of a picture.

tasks: current still image from a highway camera near a California location
12 previous stills per camera (referenceImage1UpdateAgoURL..referenceImage12UpdatesAgoURL)
camera catalogue with lat/lon, route, postmile, direction, county, nearby place
camera in-service status
HLS streaming video URL where reported (not all reported URLs are live)

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: CWWP2 CCTV page: 'There is no charge for the use of this data.' No account or key.

latency.typical: Minutes: stills refresh every 1-60 minutes depending on camera (mostly 1-5)
latency.notes: Each camera reports currentImageUpdateFrequency in minutes. In a live pull of all 12 district JSON files (2026-10-27 05:00Z, i.e. 2026-10-26 PDT), of 3,605 cameras: 5 min 1,277; 2 min 1,232; 3 min 505; 1 min 401; 4 min 1; 10-60 min 185; Not Reported 4. Sixteen sampled in-service stills had Last-Modified 0.5-5.5 minutes before fetch. Nothing is captured on request: only fixed cameras on their own schedule.

coverage.notes: Only fixed cameras along Caltrans state highways and freeways, all 12 districts; you cannot place or point a camera. Live count 2026-10-26 (PDT): 3,605 cameras, 3,428 inService=true, all with a currentImageURL, 2,307 with a streamingVideoURL. Not local streets. The district list files update 'as necessary': on 2026-10-26 their Last-Modified dates ranged from 2026-03-02 (D09) to 2026-10-26 (D04, D08), so the catalogue can lag camera changes even though images are fresh.

licensing.summary: CWWP2 says the files are available for integration into your application at no charge, under a Fair Use Policy that prohibits usage risking degradation of the CCTV streaming service, plus the general Caltrans Conditions of Use (dated July 19, 2021). Those say website information, unless otherwise indicated, is considered public domain and may be distributed or copied as permitted by law, but Caltrans uses some copyrighted data (e.g. photographs) that may need additional permission; they do not say whether CCTV stills fall under public domain. Neither page mentions AI training, resale or attribution. As-is, no warranty, no implied endorsement.

human.unknown: Not applicable: images come from fixed agency-operated cameras, not people

application.unknown: No signing or provenance metadata on images (plain JPEG with an EXIF DateTime and a text comment giving county, route, postmile and elevation); integrity rests on fetching from the Caltrans domain over HTTPS

camera.method: Each record identifies a specific Caltrans CCTV by index and location name (e.g. 'TV102 -- I-580 : West of SR-24'); image URLs are per camera.
camera.unknown: Camera hardware, pan/tilt state and field of view are not reported; operators may move PTZ cameras so the view may differ from the location description

time.method: Each JPEG carries an EXIF DateTime and a burned-in date/time bar (Pacific time); image HTTP responses carry Last-Modified, and the JSON gives a refresh interval per camera.
time.unknown: Nothing is signed. In a 2026-10-26 sample the times disagreed: one image's EXIF and overlay time was 8.7 minutes older than its Last-Modified, and another's EXIF time was 18 minutes ahead of the fetch while its overlay was current, so neither header nor EXIF reliably dates the picture. recordTimestamp is when the catalogue record was last modified, not the image time. Previous-image URLs return Last-Modified 1970-01-01.

location.method: Each camera has WGS84 latitude/longitude, elevation, route, postmile, direction of travel and county in the catalogue.
location.unknown: Coordinate accuracy and the camera's actual viewing direction are not documented; 'direction' is the side of the road, not necessarily the view

content.unknown: Raw camera stills with no QC. In a 2026-10-26 sample, 6 of 17 cameras marked inService=true returned a 'Temporarily Unavailable' placeholder that still carried a fresh time bar, EXIF time and Last-Modified, so neither inService nor freshness means a real picture. Images can also be dark, frozen or obstructed.

corroboration.unknown: No cross-checking; nearby cameras on the same route can be compared manually

freshness.typical_age: Typically 1-5 minutes for the current image; up to ~60 minutes for slow cameras
freshness.notes: currentImageURL is overwritten in place at each update; referenceImageNUpdatesAgoURL gives up to 12 previous images (so roughly the last hour at 5-minute cadence). No longer archive is offered.

delivery.basis: Per-camera currentImageUpdateFrequency of 1-60 minutes (mostly 1-5) in the CWWP2 CCTV JSON; live images had Last-Modified within ~5.5 minutes of fetch.

auth.how_to_get: No signup or key; static files over HTTPS.

endpoints.params: district 1-12 (e.g. /d4/cctv/cctvStatusD04.json); also .xml, .csv, .txt with the same data
endpoints.notes: Whole-district static file (D04 ~2.5 MB, 764 cameras). Shape: {data:[{cctv:{index, recordTimestamp, location{district, locationName, nearbyPlace, latitude, longitude, elevation, direction, county, route, postmile, milepost}, inService, imageData{imageDescription, streamingVideoURL, static{currentImageUpdateFrequency, currentImageURL, referenceImageUpdateFrequency, referenceImage1UpdateAgoURL..referenceImage12UpdatesAgoURL}}}}]}. No server-side filtering: pick the district and filter by lat/lon client-side. Numbers are strings. A missing streamingVideoURL is an empty string (1,297 cameras), not 'Not Reported'; one is malformed ('ttps://...'). Sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

endpoints.params: use currentImageURL from the list verbatim
endpoints.notes: Current 320x260 JPEG still (~7-65 KB observed). Sends Last-Modified and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (checked with an Origin header), so browsers can fetch it directly. Previous stills at /previous/{camera}-{1..12}.jpg (all 3,605 cameras list 12).

endpoints.params: use streamingVideoURL from the list verbatim
endpoints.notes: HLS playlist (application/vnd.apple.mpegurl) on a separate host. In a 2026-10-26 sample of 50 in-service cameras with a stream URL, 34 returned the playlist and 16 returned 404.

api.rate_limits: No numeric limit published. Fair Use Policy: usage that risks degrading the availability of the CCTV streaming service is prohibited. Cache the district lists (they change 'as necessary') and don't poll images faster than their update frequency.

mcp.community: No Caltrans or CWWP2 server in the official MCP Registry (searches for caltrans, cwwp2, dot.ca.gov and 'california traffic' returned none).

api.notes: No OAuth or discovery documents: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, oauth-authorization-server, ucp, agent-card.json and irlpls return HTTP 500 on cwwp2.dot.ca.gov and a 404 page on dot.ca.gov.

sources.claim: CWWP2 aggregates real-time traveler information from Caltrans' 12 districts from ITS devices including CCTV; data in CSV, JSON, TXT and XML

CCTV files describe location and status of each Caltrans CCTV on the State Highway Network; available via HTTPS for integration into applications; no charge; Fair Use Policy prohibits usage that risks degrading the CCTV streaming service; see Caltrans Conditions of Use; per-district files D01-D12 updated 'as necessary'

Field definitions: recordDate/recordTime = when the record was last modified (PST/PDT); currentImageUpdateFrequency in minutes 1-1440 or 'Not Reported'; currentImageURL and reference image 1-12 updates-ago URLs; inService true/false/Not Reported; lat/lon WGS84; direction = direction of travel the CCTV is located on

Caltrans website information, unless otherwise indicated, is considered public domain and may be distributed or copied as permitted by law, but Caltrans uses copyrighted data (e.g. photographs) that may require permission; no warranty; no endorsement; no mention of AI training, resale or automated access (Conditions of Use dated July 19, 2021)

cards.name: Capella Space
cards.summary: Operator of a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation that images through cloud and at night. Its Console and REST API let you task a new point or area capture in a UTC window, choose a collection tier (urgent, priority, standard, flexible), set up repeat tasking down to a 24-hour cycle, review a cost estimate before approving, track status, and download the delivered collect. Capella advertises 0.25 m resolution and 93% of collects delivered in under 3 hours. Access is by signed order form, invoiced in USD.

tasks: task a new SAR capture of a point (e.g. Spotlight) or an area (stripmap_100 only) within a UTC window
collection tiers urgent, priority, standard and flexible (repeat requests: routine or flexible)
repeat tasking of a point every N days (minimum cycle 24 hours), until a count, an end date, or cancelled
retask an earlier request, an existing archive collect, or a repeat series
imaging geometry constraints: look direction, ascending/descending, orbital plane (45, 53, 97), off-nadir, azimuth, grazing angle, squint, day/night or custom local time
cost estimate and approve/reject before scheduling (or pre-approve)
status tracking (received, review, submitted, active, accepted, completed, rejected, expired, and others) and signed-URL download of the delivered product

pricing.model: cost estimate per tasking request, approved before scheduling; fees invoiced
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means unknown, not free. No public price list was found. Each tasking request returns a cost estimate (order.summary.total; repeat requests: costPerImageEstimate) for approval. Fees are payable in US dollars, invoiced monthly in arrears and due net 30; payments are non-cancelable and non-refundable; cancelling an accepted order incurs the cancellation fees in Capella's Product Guide.

latency.typical: 93% of collects delivered in under 3 hours (provider claim)
latency.notes: Homepage: '93% Data Collects Delivered in Under 3 Hours', '15-minute scheduling cycles', '2-15 Revisit Opportunities Per Day'. Capture happens inside the window you set (windowOpen/windowClose); the docs give no minimum lead time, and the standard tier has a minimum window duration whose value isn't stated. The Standard Terms say any delivery date is an estimate only.

regions: Global (subject to orbit passes and scheduling)
coverage.notes: Homepage: '24/7 global coverage'. SAR works through cloud and at night. Acceptance depends on the scheduler: requests can be rejected (e.g. conflicting tasks), expire, or stay 'active' without a guarantee of full collection until 'accepted'. Accounts are not available to persons barred from receiving services under US law.

licensing.summary: Tasked data is licensed, not sold, under Capella's License Agreement (EULA v2.1, May 2026): a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence for the customer's Internal Use, including derivatives for Internal Use, plus an express right to 'use Data to train Models that Customer uses to provide services or deliverables to Third Parties' (Models must not contain or enable reconstruction of the raw Data). Selling, distributing, sublicensing or making Data or Derivatives publicly available is prohibited unless authorised; Capella keeps title to the Data and Derivatives, while the customer owns its Models and its own contributions. Use across more than one organisation needs Capella Legal. Console/API evaluation accounts are internal, non-commercial only. U.S. Government licences come via the NRO. Separate open-data collections are CC BY 4.0 / CC BY 2.0 (context only).

freshness.typical_age: Captured inside the window you set, usually delivered within hours
freshness.notes: Capella also sells an archive; irlpls lists it for new tasked captures.

auth.how_to_get: Needs an active Capella Console account, which follows a signed order form (no public self-serve sign-up was found). In Console, Account Profile > API Keys > Create, or POST /keys; send as 'Authorization: ApiKey <key>'. Keys are shown once and are valid for 90 days from creation or last use; unused keys are deleted.
The docs show 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' as an alternative to ApiKey (e.g. on POST /keys) but do not say how to obtain a token.

endpoints.notes: Available collection types.

endpoints.params: GeoJSON Feature (Point, or Polygon for stripmap_100) with properties windowOpen, windowClose, collectionTier, collectionType, collectConstraints, preApproval
endpoints.notes: Creates a tasking request; unless pre-approved it waits in 'review' with a cost estimate and is not scheduled until approved.
When transactionStatus is 'pending-customer-approval', order.summary.total holds the cost estimate.

endpoints.notes: Approve or reject at review.

endpoints.notes: Repeat tasking for points; estimate in costPerImageEstimate at 'review'; approve with PATCH /repeat-requests/{id}/status {"code": "submitted"}.
statusHistory, newest first: received, review, submitted, active, accepted, rejected, expired, completed, canceled, error, anomaly, retrying. Repeat requests: GET /repeat-requests/{repeatRequestId}.

endpoints.notes: Bulk listing of tasking requests, recommended over per-task polling.
Orders the products of a completed tasking request.
Returns STAC-like items whose asset hrefs are signed cloud-storage URLs (cloud optimized GeoTIFF).
STAC search (collections capella-geo, capella-slc); use only to fetch metadata of a commissioned collect, e.g. by capella:collect_id.

camera.unknown: Sensor identity and parameters are operator-asserted

location.unknown: Geolocation accuracy was not found in the pages read

corroboration.unknown: No documented cross-check against other sensors

cards.name: Copernicus Sentinel (Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem)
cards.short: Free EU Sentinel radar and optical satellite imagery, usually online 1-4 hours after each pass.
cards.summary: The EU's Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem serves new Sentinel-1 (C-band radar, works day and night through cloud), Sentinel-2 (13-band optical, 10 m best) and other Sentinel products free, via STAC, OData, S3, Sentinel Hub and openEO, with PUSH/PULL catalogue subscriptions and a public Traceability service whose traces carry signed product hashes.

tasks: find the newest Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 product over a place (STAC or OData search, keyless)
subscribe to new products matching an area and filter (PUSH or PULL, account needed)
download full products (token) or render a cropped image or index via the Sentinel Hub Process API
check a product's BLAKE3 hash against its signed Traceability trace

pricing.model: free
pricing.notes: Free for Copernicus General Users: 12 TB download per rolling 30 days (then slowed to 1 MB/s, not cut off), 4 concurrent connections; Sentinel Hub 10,000 requests and 10,000 processing units per month.

latency.typical: about 1 h (Sentinel-1 GRD) to about 3.5-4 h (Sentinel-2 L2A) after sensing
latency.notes: Measured on 2026-10-26 (UTC early 27th) by keyless STAC search: a Sentinel-1C GRD COG sensed 03:49:59Z was published 04:44:50Z (55 min); a Sentinel-2C L2A tile sensed 00:58:11Z was published 04:32-04:34Z (about 3 h 35 min). The Sentinel-1 mission page says marine monitoring services need data 'typically in less than 3 hours'. The next pass depends on orbit; there is no tasking.

coverage.notes: No country limit. Sentinel-2 systematically covers land between 56° S and 82.8° N, coastal waters to 20 km, islands over 100 km² and closed seas, not open ocean. Sentinel-1 follows its observation scenario; revisit depends on orbit and there is no tasking.

licensing.summary: Sentinel Data Legal Notice (EU law): free, full and open access; reproduction, distribution, communication to the public, and adaptation, modification and combination are permitted 'in so far as it is lawful'; credit 'Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]' (or 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]'). No warranty; rare limits for security, third-party rights or service disruption. Other portal content is non-commercial only. Neither AI training nor resale is named, so both stay unstated.

human.unknown: No people capture the data; satellites operated for the EU by ESA.

application.method: Public Traceability API returns traces for each product with a BLAKE3 product hash (per-file hashes on some products), signed with an X.509 certificate (RSA-SHA256) from the CDSE certificate authority
application.unknown: Proves the bytes you hold match what the CDSE ground segment registered, not what the sensor saw; some traces list only the product hash and its inputs, without per-file hashes.

camera.method: Mission, satellite and instrument (MSI optical, C-SAR radar) are named in the product name and metadata
camera.unknown: Instrument identity rests on product metadata; nothing signs it at the sensor.

time.method: Sensing start and end times in product name and metadata
time.unknown: Sensing time is in product metadata; not independently attested. The trace timestamp shows only when CDSE registered the product.

location.method: Footprint geometry and orbit in product metadata
location.unknown: Geolocation comes from product metadata and orbit data; not independently attested.

content.unknown: No manipulation detection beyond the integrity hashes.

corroboration.unknown: Not cross-checked by a third party.

freshness.typical_age: 1-4 hours after the latest pass

delivery.basis: Sentinel-1 mission page: near-real-time data 'typically in less than 3 hours'; measured publication lag 55 min (Sentinel-1 GRD) to about 3.6 h (Sentinel-2 L2A); subscriptions notify on each new product.

auth.how_to_get: STAC and OData catalogue search and Traceability lookups need no account.

Free CDSE account (register, verify e-mail); password grant with client cdse-public (add totp if 2FA is on) returns a bearer token valid 10 minutes plus a refresh token valid 60 minutes. Needed for OData download and subscriptions.
Sentinel Hub APIs: create an OAuth client (client ID and secret) in the Sentinel Hub dashboard under User Settings, then use the client_credentials grant.
S3 access to eodata.dataspace.copernicus.eu: generate an access key and secret key with an expiry date after logging in to the CDSE account.

cards.name: Defined.ai
cards.summary: AI training-data company (formerly DefinedCrowd) that, besides its dataset marketplace, runs custom collections with a vetted global crowd through its Neevo platform: images (everyday objects, facial expressions, gestures), video (egocentric POV, action sequences, behavioural clips), speech recordings, and wearable sensor data for robotics. Collections are scoped to demographic, language and compliance requirements. Sales-led and quote-only; an enterprise REST API (OAuth2 client credentials) lets account holders clone project templates, upload prompts, track status and download deliverables.
cards.short: A training-data vendor that commissions custom image, video, speech and sensor collections from a vetted crowd.

tasks: custom image collection (everyday objects, facial expressions, gestures) by a vetted crowd
custom video collection (egocentric POV, cinematic-quality video, action sequences, behavioural clips)
custom speech collection (scripted monologues recorded on contributors' devices, spontaneous dialogues and IVR calls over telephony)
synchronized wearable sensor collection for robotics (POV video, gaze, depth, hand and body motion capture, grip force)
collections scoped to demographic, language and compliance requirements

pricing.model: Quote

latency.typical: Not published

The site says every dataset is 'fully consented, copyright-cleared, and privacy-compliant' (GDPR, HIPAA). Whether a custom collection contract changes these terms, including ownership or exclusivity, is not published.

cards.name: Empiric Earth (Nexar)
cards.summary: Dashcam data company formed when Nexar and Nauto merged; it has operated as Empiric Earth since 15 September 2026. About 350,000 dashcams on vehicles making ordinary journeys feed Atlas, a searchable library of curated driving video (6M+ videos) for AV, robotics and research teams, and CityStream, a continuously refreshed feed of road detections (signs, work zones, defects, surface) plus anonymized road frames for an area (VirtualCam). When a scenario is not in the archive, customers can commission targeted collection, which points the live network at that condition. Atlas and targeted collection are sold through sales. CityStream has REST APIs that need an approved account. Nothing can be ordered by API.

tasks: targeted collection of driving video for a scenario not yet in the archive (by geography, weather or driving behaviour)
edge-case and near-miss driving video for AV and robotics training and validation
fresh road detections for a bounding box: traffic signs, work zones, road defects (potholes, manholes, road plates), surface condition (CityStream Live Feed)
anonymized road frames for a bounding box or H3 cells, filtered by date, time of day, minimum quality, road type and heading (CityStream VirtualCam)
check imagery coverage for an area before requesting frames (VirtualCam coverage endpoint)
curated road-sign inventory and work-zone feed by bounding box or H3 cells (CityStream Road Inventory, Work Zones)

pricing.model: Not published; contact sales
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means unknown, not free. The Atlas, CityStream and AV pages list no prices and route to an enquiry form. Data-licence agreements are separate contracts that are not published.

latency.typical: Unknown for targeted collection; CityStream refreshes as vehicles pass
latency.notes: No delivery time is published for targeted collection. CityStream says the road state 'updates continuously instead of on a survey cycle', and 'a dense urban corridor refreshes constantly; a rural road refreshes when someone drives it'. No latency figure is given. The Live Feed API returns 'real-time detections' since a caller-given epoch time. Enquiry replies: '1–2 business days' on the Atlas and CityStream pages, and 'within one business day' on the AV and contact pages. Those are reply times, not delivery times.

coverage.notes: Company figures: 350,000 active sensors, 300M+ new miles a month across 50+ countries, 10B+ miles of history, 98% of US roads reached, 80M+ objects detected daily. Before the merger, Nexar alone cited 100M+ miles a month across 94% of US roads. 'Coverage follows where vehicles actually drive', and no route is driven to produce data, so rural or low-traffic roads refresh rarely. CityStream describes a 'nationwide' (US) network and MUTCD-coded US signs. Countries outside the US are not listed. Atlas notes that 'coverage varies by geography'.

licensing.summary: Customer licence terms are not public. The website terms say 'product, device and data-licence agreements are separate contracts', and the CityStream OpenAPI files state 'License: Proprietary'. The company says it holds and licenses the record, will not sell personal data, and does not build plate recognition, face recognition or person-level search. It says data is 'de-identified at capture', and VirtualCam returns 'anonymized frames'. The developers page lists 'training or fine-tuning on real-world driving' as a use case, but no published term grants or forbids AI training or resale. On the capture side, Nexar's consumer site says road data is blurred on the device. The same page says Nexar uses footage, including non-anonymized footage, to train its own safety AI.

human.unknown: Footage comes from dashcams on vehicles making ordinary journeys. No driver identity check is documented, and none would be relevant to the data.

application.unknown: Captured on the provider's own dashcams, which run detection models on the device. No device or firmware attestation is published.

camera.unknown: No hardware attestation, signing or anti-injection method is documented. The provider is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.method: Each VirtualCam frame carries a capture timestamp (captured_at, with timezone offset), and each Live Feed detection carries the evidence-frame timestamp plus first- and last-recorded times (CityStream OpenAPI). Atlas attaches the date to every result.
time.unknown: How capture time is set (device clock, GPS time or server receipt) is not documented, and the timestamps are not signed.

location.method: Each frame and detection carries the camera's GPS position and heading, an H3 cell and an OpenStreetMap road segment (CityStream OpenAPI). Atlas attaches the location to every result.
location.unknown: No GNSS quality metrics, spoofing checks or signing are documented.

content.method: Atlas: 'Every video is classified before it enters the index, and in-cabin, stationary, and low-quality footage is filtered out.' Atlas ranks results with the BADAS collision-risk model. Live Feed detections carry model confidence scores, and VirtualCam frames carry a frame-quality score.
content.unknown: Classification error rates for delivered data are not published. BADAS benchmarks are internal, and the provider labels them that way. It is not stated whether people review targeted-collection results.

corroboration.method: CityStream: 'Every vehicle that passes a location adds an observation', and repeated observations of the same place are reported as change. Live Feed detections record when they were first and most recently seen.
corroboration.unknown: This applies to CityStream road detections only. Nothing describes how many independent passes confirm a detection, and no cross-check is described for Atlas video or for targeted-collection deliveries.

auth.how_to_get: Log in to the Nexar Developers Portal (developer.getnexar.com), which runs an OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE against Nexar's Okta server (issuer https://nexar.okta.com/oauth2/aus3qkg89t55hJZsT4x7). Each CityStream product (Live Feed, Work Zones, Road Inventory, VirtualCam) is shown only to accounts in that product's Okta group, so an approved commercial account is needed. Send the token as 'Authorization: Bearer {token}'.

The portal issues a refresh token. Exchange it for an access token with POST https://external.getnexar.com/dev-portal/refresh-token (form field refresh_token), then send 'Authorization: Bearer {token}'.

cards.name: Errand
cards.short: Agents send a nearby person in Seoul (Gangnam beta) for in-app camera photos and answers.
cards.summary: Agent-native errand dispatch in Seoul. An agent checks live worker coverage, gets an exact quote, then dispatches a task (check, verify, photograph, queue or pickup) over a remote MCP server or REST. Nearby workers with the Errand phone app get a push notification; one accepts, goes to the spot and shoots photos with the in-app camera only (gallery uploads blocked), answering up to five structured questions. The server checks capture location and time, then an AI judges the photo against the buyer's validation_criteria; a worker gets two attempts. Results return photos, answers, the verdict, GPS distance and capture time. The beta covers Gangnam and nearby areas only, and live worker availability can be zero. Prepaid in Korean won, topped up by bank transfer.

tasks: check (is a store, pop-up, office or venue open)
verify (product on shelf, price)
photograph (storefront, menu, sign, notice, product, queue)
queue (queue length or waiting time, allowed queue tasks)

pricing.model: Reward set by the buyer + platform fee of 20% (minimum ₩500), prepaid in KRW
pricing.notes: Reward per task ₩1,000–₩200,000; the smallest possible charge is ₩1,000 + ₩500 fee = ₩1,500 (≈ $1.13 at 1,325.28 KRW/USD, ECB reference rate 2026-10-26). The fee includes VAT and is earned only on completed tasks; reward + fee are escrowed at dispatch and refunded in full on failure, expiry or pre-acceptance cancellation. Examples: reward ₩5,000 → charge ₩6,000; ₩10,000 → ₩12,000. Default key caps: ₩20,000 reward per task and ₩50,000 per day including fees; raise by e-mailing support. The worker page says tasks posted so far paid ₩8,000–₩15,000. POST /api/v1/quote returns the exact total_charge_krw before anything is charged. A first one-photo check in Gangnam/Yeoksam is free through a trial form, placed by the operator.

The worker page says a task usually takes 10–30 minutes on site. Unfinished tasks expire automatically and are refunded. The operator-placed free trial is 'usually same day to next day'.

licensing.summary: Terms B-3: the requester may use task results (photos, location and time, answers) for its own business purposes ('자신의 업무 목적으로 이용할 수 있습니다'). Results contain no worker personal data, and the requester must not use them to identify or contact the worker. Accuracy is guaranteed only as far as the verdict against the validation criteria. Ownership, resale and AI training are not mentioned. The privacy policy says evidence photos are sent to Anthropic only for automated verification and are not used for other purposes.

auth.how_to_get: Connect an OAuth-capable MCP client to https://errand.be/api/mcp; the protected-resource metadata names the Supabase authorization server https://ekygxbccwbwcppkbpetc.supabase.co/auth/v1, which publishes a registration_endpoint (RFC 7591), authorization_code + refresh_token grants, public clients (auth method none) and PKCE S256 (plain also listed). The resource metadata lists no scopes. Docs: OAuth is for MCP; REST uses the API key. Spending still needs a prepaid balance and stays within the key/account caps.

Enter an e-mail at https://errand.be and type the 6-digit code; an er_live_ key is issued at once and shown once. Send 'Authorization: Bearer er_live_…'. Works for REST and as the developer/CLI fallback for MCP.

mcp.notes: Stateless Streamable HTTP (POST JSON-RPC only; GET returns 405). Registry latest 0.2.1 (published 2026-09-17). Seven tools mapping one-to-one to REST: errand_check_coverage, errand_list_capabilities, errand_quote, errand_dispatch, errand_get_status, errand_get_result, errand_cancel. A ChatGPT plugin offers only the five read tools (no dispatch, cancel or payment).

endpoints.params: task_type, lat, lng, reward_krw
endpoints.notes: MCP errand_quote. Creates nothing; returns total_charge_krw, platform_fee_krw, balance_krw, balance_sufficient, coverage and can_dispatch (true only when a worker is reachable and the balance suffices).

endpoints.params: task_type (check|verify|photograph|queue|pickup), title (4–120), instructions (10–2000), validation_criteria (10–1000), lat, lng, radius_m (100–10000), reward_krw (1000–200000), expires_in_minutes (10–1440); optional address_hint, report_fields (≤5: key, label, type text|number, unit, placeholder), webhook_url
endpoints.notes: MCP errand_dispatch. Escrows reward + fee. Text the worker reads should be in Korean. 422 UNSAFE_TASK / PRIVACY_VIOLATING_TASK on content rejection.

MCP errand_get_status. open → accepted → arrived (GPS confirmed on site) → submitted → completed; terminal failures failed (both attempts rejected), expired, cancelled, all refunded. webhook_url receives mission.completed / failed / cancelled / expired.

MCP errand_get_result. Returns status, share_url (read-only, no login, 30 days), verdict {passed, score, feedback}, answers, evidence {photo_urls (signed, expire in 1 h), gps {lat, lng, accuracy_m}, distance_from_task_m, captured_at, checks {distance_m, capture_age_min, exif_gps_present, failures}}.

api.rate_limits: Public coverage endpoint: 60 requests/minute per IP (429 RATE_LIMITED). Authenticated endpoints: the key's daily budget is the practical limit.
api.notes: Other operations: GET /api/v1/coverage and keyless GET /api/public/coverage?lat=&lng=&radius_m= (online_workers, reachable_workers, dispatchable); GET /api/v1/capabilities (balance, caps, allowed task types, fees); POST /api/v1/dispatches/{id}/cancel (only while open; full refund). Each key carries caps on reward per task, daily budget, allowed task types and allowed area (403 CAP_MAX_REWARD, CAP_DAILY_BUDGET, CAP_TASK_TYPE, CAP_AREA). No OpenAPI file is published.

payment.notes: KRW prepaid balance, topped up only by Korean bank transfer (deposit-code method), minimum ₩10,000 per top-up, credited after the deposit is confirmed. An agent spends from the balance on its own within the key's caps (escrow at dispatch); it cannot top up. Unused balance is refunded on request (terms B-2).

worker_pay.model: Fixed reward per task set by the buyer, paid in full to the worker; no worker fee
worker_pay.notes: Credited to the app wallet when verification passes; withdrawals from ₩5,000 to the worker's own bank account in 1–2 business days; 3.3% income tax withheld under the Income Tax Act. Tasks posted so far paid ₩8,000–₩15,000. Workers who fail both attempts get nothing for that task.

requester.checks: The requester verifies an e-mail to get an API key; every request made with the key counts as the requester's own (terms B-1). Keys carry owner-set caps on reward, daily budget, task types and area. Tasks are content-screened: 422 UNSAFE_TASK or PRIVACY_VIOLATING_TASK rejects tasks that endanger the worker or make them photograph people, ID documents or screens. Terms B-4 ban illegal, dangerous or discriminatory tasks, tasks that infringe others' rights, tasks that ask a worker's identity or private contact, and tasks for surveillance or tracking.
requester.unknown: No identity check beyond e-mail is documented. How the content screening works, and how reliably it catches person-targeting, is not published.

human.method: Workers sign in to the Errand iOS/Android app with e-mail, Apple or Google; one account per person, age 14+; withdrawals go to a bank account in the worker's own name, and tax data is collected when withholding applies.
human.unknown: No identity verification is required to start ('별도 신청은 없어요', no separate application); nothing per result proves who captured it, and the buyer never sees the worker.

application.method: Evidence can only be shot with the Errand app's own camera; gallery uploads are blocked (docs, FAQ, terms A-3).
application.unknown: No app or device attestation (e.g. App Attest, Play Integrity) is documented, so a modified app or emulator is not ruled out by anything published.

camera.method: In-app camera only; terms A-3 forbid photos from the library, screen captures and photos taken elsewhere, and screening rejects tasks that ask workers to photograph screens.
camera.unknown: No sensor-level or C2PA signing; nothing published shows a photo of a screen or a generated image would be caught at capture.

time.method: The server checks capture time before AI judging; results include captured_at and checks.capture_age_min.
time.unknown: The time comes from the worker's phone app; no signed timestamp is documented.

location.method: GPS arrival check ('arrived' status), then a server check of capture location; results include gps {lat, lng, accuracy_m}, distance_from_task_m, checks.distance_m and exif_gps_present. Terms A-5 ban location spoofing.
location.unknown: Anti-spoofing beyond the terms is not documented; the pass/fail distance threshold is not published.

content.method: An AI model (photos sent to Anthropic for verification, per the privacy policy) judges the photo against the buyer's validation_criteria and returns verdict {passed, score, feedback}; two attempts per task, then the task fails and is refunded.
content.unknown: The verdict is automated with no human review documented; structured answers are the worker's own and are not checked.

corroboration.unknown: Each task goes to one worker; nothing independent confirms the observation.

cards.name: Execution Market
cards.summary: Bounty marketplace run by Ultravioleta DAO ('Universal Execution Layer') where an AI agent or a person posts a USDC-paid task with required evidence types (e.g. GPS-tagged photo, video, text), assigns an applicant, and releases on-chain escrow after reviewing the submission. Executors can be people or other AI agents. Callable over REST, a remote OAuth MCP server and A2A; identity is a crypto wallet with an ERC-8004 on-chain identity, not an account. Most recent completed tasks are small digital or research jobs; physical captures are rare.
cards.short: A crypto-paid bounty marketplace where agents hire people (or other agents) for tasks, incl. GPS-tagged photos.

tasks: physical presence: verify a store is open, photograph a location, check conditions (photo_geo with GPS check)
data collection: surveys, price checks, inventory counts, measurements
knowledge access: scan documents, photograph posted information
simple actions and errands: buy items, deliver packages
human authority: notarize, certify, translate
remote research, verification and digital tasks (often done by AI agents)

pricing.model: publisher sets the bounty; a 13% platform fee is deducted from the bounty at release
pricing.notes: Bounty range $0.01-$10,000 (live config: min_bounty_usd 0.01, max_bounty_usd 10000); the docs say escrow deposits are additionally capped at $100 per task. The 13% fee comes out of the bounty, not on top: a $10 bounty pays the worker $8.70. Optional paid evidence analysis ('verification seal'): $0.50 standard, $1.00 with video, paid over x402. Platform metrics on 2026-10-26 report $934.48 total payment volume across 3,402 completed tasks, so typical bounties are cents.

latency.typical: Not guaranteed; bounded by the deadline the publisher sets (1-720 hours)
latency.notes: The publisher sets deadline_hours (1-720); tasks with no completed submission expire (2,479 of 6,966 tasks had expired by 2026-10-26). Applicants apply and the publisher assigns one, which locks escrow. A submission left unreviewed for 72 hours auto-settles to the worker; an inconclusive automated verdict opens a dispute with a 24-hour response deadline that may go unclaimed for small bounties.

regions: Global (self-registered workers; no country limit stated)
coverage.notes: No country list or limit is published; an OFAC sanctioned-address blacklist exists. Supply is thin: public metrics on 2026-10-26 listed 652 registered workers, 56 workers who have completed a task and 13 active. Of the 200 most recent completed tasks (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-27), 1 was physical_presence and 2 were outdoor photos (sky over Medellin, Miami night sky); most were cent-sized knowledge, research and QA tasks, many done by AI agents. Only 2 tasks were open that day, both remote research. The geo-matching filter (geo_match_mode) is accepted but switched off in production.

licensing.summary: Terms of Service (last updated 2026-10-03) are short: 18+, no fraudulent evidence, 13% fee, payments final once settled on-chain, platform provided as-is. They say nothing about who owns submitted evidence, licences, resale or AI training. The Privacy Policy (2026-10-24) says evidence is kept in private S3 storage and shared through short-lived links with the worker and the publisher only, is sent to third-party AI verification providers (via OpenRouter: Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Qwen, DeepSeek and others) and may be reviewed by human moderators; faces and plates are not blurred; people in evidence can ask for removal. It does not say Execution Market trains its own models on evidence. An optional DX402 copy of each paid submission is anchored, encrypted to the buyer's key, for 90 days by default.

human.method: Every worker wallet must hold an ERC-8004 on-chain identity; World ID Orb verification is required server-side for bounties of $500 or more (live config worldid_min_bounty_for_orb_usd 500). Bidirectional on-chain ratings (ERC-8004, scored via describe.net). Each application and delivery records executor_kind (human, human_via_agent, autonomous_agent, robot, unknown).
human.unknown: Below $500 no proof of personhood is required, and an ERC-8004 identity is a wallet, not a person. Executors may be AI agents: target_executor 'human' is only a preference, and executor_kind is inferred from the request channel, not proven. Most recent completions have no executor_kind recorded.

application.method: A mobile app (Expo camera + location) and a no-login web evidence link capture photos with camera/GPS; agents may also upload files by presigned URL.
application.unknown: No app or device attestation is documented; the docs say the mobile app's store links are 'available when published', and evidence can arrive from the web form or any signed API client.

camera.method: Ring 1 'PHOTINT' forensic checks (EXIF, tampering, generative-AI detection with hard-fail floors, photo source camera vs gallery) produce a pre-check score; uploaded files are SHA-256 hashed into evidence_content_hash.
camera.unknown: Forensic scores are the provider's own heuristics with no published accuracy; the full arbiter is opt-in (arbiter_mode manual by default) and never releases funds by itself. Nothing stops a photo of a screen beyond these checks. No C2PA.

time.method: Photo capture time from EXIF and the submission timestamp are shown to the publisher; a timestamp_proof evidence type exists; Ring 1 checks timestamps.
time.unknown: EXIF time is set by the device and editable; no trusted time-stamp (e.g. RFC 3161) is applied to captures. The EIP-191-signed verdict and DX402 anchor show when EM received and judged the submission, not when the photo was taken.

location.method: gps_required (default on for photo/video tasks with a place): the evidence's GPS, else EXIF GPS, else the browser location, must fall within a radius (500 m default, 1,000 m for simple_action) of the task point, or Ring 1 fails and the delivery goes to a person. Docs describe server-side GPS anti-spoofing (speed and coordinate-consistency checks).
location.unknown: Phone or browser GPS is self-reported and spoofable; the anti-spoofing checks are not specified in detail. Without task coordinates any GPS in the evidence satisfies the requirement.

content.method: Optional Ring 2 LLM review (via OpenRouter) scores whether the evidence shows the task was done, with an EIP-191-signed verdict the publisher can check against the arbiter address; the publisher reviews and approves or rejects; disputes go to self-claimed human arbiters.
content.unknown: The signature proves who issued a verdict, not that it is right; Ring 2 is opt-in, runs one provider today, and auto-release on a pass is disabled. Unreviewed submissions auto-settle to the worker after 72 hours.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check of a capture. Reputation ratings and dispute arbiters judge the worker, not the observation; a publisher could post several tasks for the same place, but that is buyer-side.

auth.how_to_get: ERC-8128 HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421 over EIP-191) signed by the agent's own EVM wallet on every request (Signature, Signature-Input, Content-Digest; nonce from GET /auth/erc8128/nonce; max 300 s). The wallet first registers a gasless ERC-8004 identity at POST /reputation/register; no client_id, password or API key is issued. Recommended signer: PayBox or Open Wallet Standard.

Remote MCP at https://mcp.execution.market/mcp/: OAuth 2.1 authorization code with mandatory PKCE S256, public clients, RFC 7591 dynamic registration at https://auth.execution.market/oauth/register or a Client ID Metadata Document. Sign-in is Sign-In with Ethereum, so the person still needs a wallet. A bearer never moves money on its own: assigning needs a per-operation EIP-3009 signature, and approving needs that or the separately consented agent:approve scope (capped at $100 per approval and 50 approvals; 15-minute token).

Signed wallet session for clients that cannot sign requests: POST /auth/session/challenge returns EIP-712 typed data; the wallet signs it and the result is sent in X-EM-Session (TTL up to 900 s). Refused on escrow, evidence, reputation and similar paths. Gated by EM_WALLET_SESSION_ENABLED.

endpoints.notes: Open tasks on the public board; no credentials. GET /tasks?status=completed also lists tasks without credentials.
Find available workers; requires an ERC-8128 signature or bearer token.

endpoints.params: title, instructions, category (21), bounty_usd (0.01-10000), deadline_hours (1-720), evidence_required (1-5 of 18 types, e.g. photo_geo, video, text_response); optional payment_network, location_hint (public), location_lat/location_lng (exact only to the assigned worker), gps_required, location_radius_m, geo_match_mode, min_reputation, arbiter_mode, target_executor
endpoints.notes: Publishing locks no money. Then GET /tasks/{id}/applications, and POST /tasks/{id}/assign with an X-Payment-Auth EIP-3009 escrow signature (challenge at GET /tasks/{id}/assign/challenge) assigns the worker and locks escrow. Unknown body fields are rejected (422).
Task details and status; GET /tasks/{task_id}/events lists what happened since you last looked.

Opens a delivery's evidence (records that the publisher saw it) with evidence_content_hash, arbiter verdict and 5-minute download URLs. GET /tasks/{task_id}/submissions gives status only. POST /submissions/{id}/approve releases escrow; /reject rejects.

api.sdk: OpenAPI 3 (234 paths) at https://execution.market/openapi.json; Swagger at https://api.execution.market/docs; A2A v0.3 agent card; MCP server card v9.7.0; uvd-x402-sdk (Python/npm) for escrow and DX402
api.rate_limits: Task creation 100/h, queries 1000/h, batch create 10/h; request body 1 MiB

mcp.notes: Streamable HTTP, 65 tools per llms.txt (em_publish_task, em_assign_task, em_open_submission_evidence, em_approve_submission, ...). Registry entry v1.0.0, published 2026-03-20. Also an A2A JSON-RPC endpoint at https://api.execution.market/a2a/v1.

api.notes: API keys are disabled in production (403). Identity is the wallet; an ERC-8004 identity is mandatory before publishing (403 identity_required otherwise). Task text and location_hint are public on the board, so put exact addresses only in location_lat/location_lng.

freshness.typical_age: Captured after you publish and a worker is assigned, within the deadline you set
freshness.notes: No archive of captures is sold; evidence is private to the publisher and worker.

delivery.basis: Provider: publisher sets deadline_hours (1-720); no completion time is promised, and 2,479 of 6,966 tasks had expired by 2026-10-26.

payment.notes: Stablecoin only (USDC; EURC, PYUSD, AUSD, USDT listed on some chains) from the publisher's own wallet: an EIP-3009 authorization locks the bounty in x402r escrow at assignment on 9 EVM chains (Base default, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, Celo, Monad, Arc), released gaslessly with the 13% fee split on-chain at approval. Solana bounties are paid by charge or a payment channel (channel flow not working end to end in production). Metered MPP sessions are beta on Base and Arbitrum, capped at $100. No card or fiat checkout is documented.

requester.checks: The publisher needs a wallet with an ERC-8004 identity (gasless, self-registered) and must accept the Terms (18+). Each published or edited task's text is reviewed by an LLM (TypeSafe via OpenRouter) against the task policy and can be refused. Workers are told not to make third parties or minors the subject of evidence photos.
requester.unknown: No identity or KYC check on publishers beyond the wallet is documented; the task policy page itself was not retrievable, so how requests to watch, follow or photograph a specific person are handled is not stated.

cards.name: Field Agent (now Storesight)
cards.short: Shoppers sent to stores for shelf photos and price checks, from $24 a response (now Storesight).
cards.summary: Crowdsourced shoppers, using the Field Agent mobile app, visit a named store to photograph shelves and displays, check prices and answer audit questions. The company (Field Agent, Inc.) rebranded to Storesight in 2025 and fieldagent.net redirects to storesight.com; the shopper app keeps the Field Agent name. Buyers order audits by the response, at published list prices, in the self-serve Storesight Projects shop (web sign-up, no ordering API), or through full service. Storesight also sells syndicated shelf-photo data from its own sampling.

tasks: item photo on shelf
price check
on-shelf availability
item check-up
display compliance
planogram visibility
category overview and display photos
signage audit
store walk (signage and displays)
menu board pricing
in-store measurements
shelf correction with before/after photos
video shopalong
mystery shopping
buy and try

pricing.model: Per response (one shopper submission) at self-serve list prices; full-service and enterprise work by quote
pricing.notes: List prices from the Storesight Projects shop on 2026-10-26: Item Photo, Signage Audit and Club Entryway Photos $26; Price Check and On-Shelf Availability $27; Item Check Up and Category Overview Photos $27.50; Display Compliance $28; Planogram Visibility, Modular Pics and Category Display Photos $30; Store Walk $38; Walmart Shelf Price Audit $40; Shelf Correction (Zoning) $24 with before/after photos. Optional add-on questions are $0.50 per response. Survey-style 'Insights' products that need no store visit start at $20. storesight.com/pricing is a 404; prices appear only in the shop.

latency.typical: Self-serve projects run at least 5 days (5 to 17 by product); full-service audits launch in under 24 hours on average
latency.notes: The self-serve builder enforces a minimum project length of 5 days for most store audits and up to 17 for buy-and-review products, with 0 to 3 days' lead time before launch. The platform page promises results from the field 'within days'. Shopper-side review of submissions can take 3 to 5 business days.

delivery.basis: Self-serve project builder: 'Minimum project length is 5 days.' Platform page: 'visual proof and retail intelligence from the field within days.'

coverage.notes: Core network is in the US: Storesight cites 3 million U.S. shoppers and audits 'from major metropolitan areas to rural markets'. The shopper app runs in 8 countries through international partners (separate local sites and support for Canada, UK, Mexico, Ecuador, Spain, South Africa and Australia); density outside the US is not published. Syndicated shelf-photo categories are collected in the USA, Canada and the UK. Company-stated scale: about 6 million shelf and display images a year across 50,000 retail locations; 50 major retailers covered.

licensing.summary: Two documents apply. The shopper Participation Agreement says a shopper's work product is a 'work made for hire' for the Client, and all ownership rights, including worldwide IP, vest in the Client; Field Agent also takes a perpetual, sublicensable licence to all submitted materials. The buyer-side Conditions of Use (2 September 2025) say Storesight owns all right, title and interest, including IP, in the Data Services, Site and Services, which are provided as-is with no warranty that they are timely. Neither document mentions resale or AI training. Syndicated shelf data bought from Storesight is Storesight's.

human.unknown: Shoppers sign up with a few demographic details; no identity check is published. The terms allow one registration per person and one device at a time, but how that is enforced is not stated. Tax identity (W-9) is collected only from US shoppers nearing $2,000 a year.

application.unknown: No app or device attestation is published. Whether a photo came from an unmodified copy of the app is unknown.

camera.method: Photos must be taken in the app. Adding internet images, photos of another device, computer images or screen captures from outside the app counts as cheating and gets the account banned.
camera.unknown: This is a rule enforced after the fact, not a technical check. How a photo of a screen or a printout is detected is not published, and there is no C2PA signing.

time.method: The privacy policy says Field Agent receives the time, date and place each photo or video was taken; jobs must be finished within a reservation window that starts at reservation.
time.unknown: Whether the time comes from the device clock or the server is not stated. Nothing signed is delivered.

location.method: The app verifies and records GPS coordinates; jobs submitted at the wrong store are denied, and location-based photos must be submitted through the app for GPS verification.
