cards.name: Field Nation
cards.short: Dispatch an independent technician to a US or Canadian site, with GPS check-in, photos and sign-off.
cards.summary: Marketplace of independent field technicians (IT, networking, AV, POS, cabling, security, IoT) serving sites in the US and Canada. A buyer posts a work order with location, schedule and pay; a provider checks in on site, completes photo and signature tasks and logs time. REST v2 API (contract required) with work orders, GPS check-in, time logs, attachments, signatures and HMAC-signed webhooks.

tasks: site visit with completion photos
photo task (e.g. serial number photo)
site-contact signature capture
installation
break/fix
preventive maintenance and inspections
site survey
check-in at a location

pricing.model: subscription (Plus, Premier, Enterprise) plus per-work-order pay set by the buyer (fixed or hourly)
pricing.notes: No figures published. Client API is an add-on on Plus and included on Premier; API use is billed per the signed Sales Order, with a set-up fee. Providers pay Field Nation a percentage of the work-order charges. All amounts in USD. Cancelling after a provider is assigned and dispatched may incur a fee.

latency.typical: not published; 'Fill jobs in minutes with local, experienced techs' (coverage page) and 'same-day field service nationwide' (customer quote)
latency.notes: The buyer sets the service window per work order (exact time, between a window, or within N hours). No delivery SLA. Unreviewed completed work is deemed accepted after 15 days.

coverage.notes: About page: '425K+ sites serviced throughout the U.S. and Canada'. The coverage map is by US state and claims 'every ZIP code'. Density in Canada is not published. Payments in USD only; California buyers must meet credit requirements instead of prefunding.

licensing.summary: Under the Standard Work Order Terms each Provider assigns to the Buyer all rights in the Work Product made in performing a work order, and Buyer Terms say work-order information is the Buyer's property; a buyer can vary these terms per work order. Field Nation does not own Buyer Data but takes a worldwide licence to use it for operating the Platform and 'related business purposes', and may use de-identified data for any purpose. The terms do not mention AI or ML training, or resale of deliverables (the resale ban in the User Agreement covers the Platform itself).

human.method: Providers are registered platform accounts with ratings and job history; Field Nation reserves the right to validate identity information; buyers can require certification, background-check or drug-test qualifications that providers must upload and have verified before requesting the work.
human.unknown: Buyer Terms say Field Nation 'does not and will not investigate Providers' and does not verify their skills, background or profile information. Who runs the screenings, and how identity is checked, is not published.

application.method: Providers 'typically upload completion photos via the mobile app' and check in and out through it.
application.unknown: The API also accepts uploads, check-ins, task completion and signatures, so nothing guarantees a photo came from the app.

camera.unknown: No live-capture, EXIF or signed-capture handling documented; attachments carry only an upload time. Field Nation is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.method: Check-in/check-out creates time logs with start.utc/end.utc, status pending/verified/disputed ('verified' = confirmed by buyer); on completion the system checks signature timestamps fall within the service window.
time.unknown: Time logs can be created, edited and deleted via the API; attachments carry only an upload time, not a capture time.

location.method: check_in carries location {lat,lng}, which 'is compared against the work order location to verify the provider is on-site'; a buyer can set require_gps to require GPS check-in.
location.unknown: No distance threshold; check-out has no location; photos carry no coordinates; spoofing controls not described.

content.method: Required tasks (e.g. 'Take photo of serial number') and signatures must be completed before the provider marks work done; the buyer then approves, marks incomplete or disputes (workorder.status.approved).
content.unknown: Review is by the buyer (or SmartAudit rules the buyer configures), not Field Nation; unreviewed work is deemed accepted after 15 days.

corroboration.method: A site contact can sign off on completion (name, title, signature image); on completion the system checks the required number of signatures and that names match the expected contacts.
corroboration.unknown: Signatures are captured on the provider's device and can also be created via the API; nothing ties the signer's identity or presence to the site.

Token from POST https://api.fieldnation.com/authentication/api/oauth/token: the auth page shows a password grant (client_id, client_secret, username, password), while the prerequisites page says Client Credentials. Tokens last about 1 hour, with a refresh_token, and are passed as the access_token query parameter. Sandbox: https://api-sandbox.fndev.net/api/rest/v2 (separate credentials).

cards.name: Fintraffic Digitraffic road weather cameras
cards.short: 816 road-weather camera stations across Finland, new stills about every 10 min, CC BY 4.0, no key.
cards.summary: Finland's national traffic agency publishes its road weather cameras as open data: 816 stations with 2,288 fixed views (presets). Each view has a stable latest-image URL, a capture time, a road address and a view direction, and the last 24 hours of images can be fetched by version.

tasks: current still of a Finnish road or roadside view
visual check of snow, ice, fog, road surface and traffic
images of the same view over the last 24 hours

pricing.model: free
pricing.notes: Open data under CC BY 4.0; no key, no account and no paid tier.

latency.typical: about 10 minutes
latency.notes: Digitraffic: images are updated about every 10 minutes (station collectionInterval 600 s). Sampled 2026-10-26 (05:00 UTC on 27 Oct): across 2,283 presets the latest measuredTime was a median 5.5 min old, 90th percentile 10 min, 2,225 under 15 min; a few long-idle presets are days or more stale. The sampled image's x-amz-meta-last-modified matched its measuredTime.

coverage.notes: 816 stations on the Finnish road network, from the south coast to northern Lapland (lat 59.9-70.1), one of them in Eckero, Aland. On 2026-10-26, 814 were GATHERING and 2 REMOVED_TEMPORARILY. Check collectionStatus, state and each preset's inCollection before relying on a view.

licensing.summary: Fintraffic's open data is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, which 'gives the right to distribute, remix, tweak, and build upon our data, even commercially', with credit. Attribution must preserve the copyright notice and disclaimers, link the original site and the licence, and describe any changes; suggested credit: 'Source: Fintraffic / digitraffic.fi, license CC 4.0 BY'. The terms do not mention AI or machine-learning training.

human.unknown: Fixed automated cameras; no person is involved in capture.

application.unknown: No attestation of the camera software or the upload pipeline.

camera.method: Fixed road cameras; Digitraffic says road data come from the traffic management systems of ITM Finland Ltd, a Fintraffic subsidiary. Station metadata names the camera type (e.g. BOSCH, VAPIX).
camera.unknown: No per-image proof that a frame came from the named camera; images carry no C2PA manifest.

time.method: measuredTime per preset in /stations/{id}/data; the image's x-amz-meta-last-modified header matches it.
time.unknown: Timestamps are not signed; the image overlay shows no capture time.

location.method: Station coordinates, road address (road number, section, distance) and municipality, plus a direction code and name per preset.
location.unknown: Coordinates and view direction are operator metadata, not verified per image.

content.unknown: No integrity or content checks are documented. An unknown or unpublished preset still returns HTTP 200 with a grey 'Image not available' JPEG, so check the size or the ETag.

corroboration.unknown: Station metadata can name a nearestWeatherStationId (seen on the sampled station) whose road weather readings can be cross-checked by the caller, but Digitraffic publishes no cross-check.

auth.how_to_get: No key. Send a Digitraffic-User header naming your app (no personal data); it raises your request allowance. Do not send an Authorization header: weathercam requests then fail with 400. JSON APIs require Accept-Encoding: gzip (406 without it); images do not.

endpoints.params: lastUpdated
endpoints.notes: GeoJSON FeatureCollection of all stations: coordinates, collectionStatus, presets with inCollection.
One station in detail: camera type, collectionInterval, municipality, road address, nearestWeatherStationId, and per preset the imageUrl, resolution, direction and name.
measuredTime per preset; /stations/data returns all stations.

endpoints.notes: Latest image (e.g. 1280x720). Supports ETag/If-None-Match (304 when unchanged). Unknown presets return a 200 placeholder image.
Links to each preset's images over the last 24 hours (imageUrl with versionId, lastModified, size); /stations/history covers all.

endpoints.params: after
endpoints.notes: Presets whose publishableTo changed: views taken out of or returned to public view.

api.rate_limits: Without the Digitraffic-User header: 60 requests/min per IP for weathercam images and 60/min for tie.digitraffic.fi v1 APIs; more with the header (no figure published). Excess requests get 429. Most JSON responses are cached for about a minute.

mcp.community: No Fintraffic MCP server in the official MCP Registry. The only Digitraffic entry is a third-party AIS vessel server (io.github.pipeworx-io/digitraffic-ais), not weather cameras.

api.notes: OpenAPI: https://tie.digitraffic.fi/swagger/openapi.json. Deprecated API versions stay up for six months and return Deprecation and Sunset headers.

freshness.notes: Images are kept for 24 hours (history endpoint; S3 expiry rule 'Delete versions and current images after 24h').

requester.unknown: Nothing is ordered or commissioned, so no requester checks apply.

cards.name: Freelancer.com (local jobs)
cards.summary: Global freelance marketplace whose API can post 'Local Jobs' projects pinned to a place (country, city, latitude and longitude) in job types such as Inspections, Local Job, Photography and Video Tours. Freelancers bid; the buyer awards a bid and pays through Milestone Payments released on approval. The User Agreement (s.33) forbids automated access, including the API, without Freelancer's express written permission.
cards.short: Post a local job anywhere; nearby freelancers bid to go and do it.

tasks: site verification
inspections
local photography and video tours
errands and pickups
investigation

pricing.model: bid-based; buyer sets a budget range, freelancers bid
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published (set by bids). Posting is free. Employer fee on award: 3% or USD 3, whichever is greater (fixed price); 3% of each payment (hourly); refundable if cancelled within 7 days. Card, PayPal or Skrill: USD 0.30 + 2.3% (not for Australian transactions, which carry an Account Admin Fee of AUD 0.75 + 0.99%). Milestone arbitration: USD 5 or 5%, whichever is greater, per party, refunded to the winner. Optional upgrades include IP Agreement (USD 22.99 in the fee table, USD 21.99 in the same page's FAQ), NDA USD 22.99, Urgent USD 10.99.

latency.typical: Not published; posting, review, bidding, then award
latency.notes: No SLA. API-posted projects usually enter a review queue before they go live (developer docs, sandbox page). Active projects on 2026-10-26 via the public API: Inspections 17, Local Job 89, Photo Anywhere 0.

coverage.notes: Freelancer says Local Jobs 'get help in any location, anywhere in the world' and claims a 'talent pool of over 90.5 million professionals'. 167 of 3,487 job types are local. Active Inspections and Local Job projects on 2026-10-26 were concentrated in Thailand, the US, South Korea, Brazil and the UK, with a few in about 20 other countries. Density per city is not published. People barred under Australian or other applicable law may not use the site.

licensing.summary: No default clause transfers ownership of project deliverables to the buyer; a paid IP Agreement upgrade 'ensures intellectual property rights transfer to you' (Fees and Charges). Freelancer takes a broad, sublicensable, irrevocable licence to User Content (User Agreement s.10). The terms do not mention AI or machine-learning training or resale. Freelancer may record in-app audio and video calls for 'quality assurance, training, and service improvement' (s.15), without saying whether that means model training.

human.method: Optional 'Verified by Freelancer' KYC: government photo ID, a photo holding the ID beside a one-time keycode, and two proofs of address, reviewed by Freelancer's team. Freelancer can also demand ID at any time (s.14).
human.unknown: Verification is optional for sellers, so the freelancer you award may be unverified. Freelancer states it 'cannot and do[es] not confirm each User's purported identity' (s.38).

application.unknown: Freelancers upload files they captured however they like; there is no capture app.

camera.unknown: Nothing stops a gallery upload, screenshot or generated image.

time.unknown: No capture timestamp is checked; only message and upload times exist.

location.unknown: The project has a location, but where a file was captured is not checked. OAuth scopes fln:location_tracking_create/view ('location information of freelancer working on project') exist, but no endpoint using them is documented.

content.method: The buyer reviews the work and releases the Milestone Payment; disputes go to Freelancer's Milestone Dispute Resolution, with paid arbitration on submitted evidence.
content.unknown: Freelancer does not review deliverables, and for Local Jobs it does not verify credentials or statements of capability (s.16).

corroboration.unknown: No independent check. A buyer could award the same task to a second freelancer by hand.

auth.how_to_get: Personal Access Token: Generate Token at https://accounts.freelancer.com/settings/develop. Acts only as the account that made it; one active token per environment; valid 30 days. The User Agreement s.33 still requires Freelancer's express written permission for any automated or API access.

Create a client application at https://accounts.freelancer.com ('Develop with Freelancer.com'); applications are reviewed (expect a reply within 5 business days), and requests for single-user apps are denied. Authorization-code flow: https://accounts.freelancer.com/oauth/authorize with scope=basic and advanced_scopes as numeric ids; token at https://accounts.freelancer.com/oauth/token with a client secret. Access tokens last 30 days, with refresh tokens.

Terms 6.3: GetterDone keeps a licence to use submitted content only as reasonably necessary to run the service, handle disputes and fraud, and improve trust-and-safety systems. Resale and AI training are not mentioned.

auth.how_to_get: Add https://getterdone.ai/mcp as a remote MCP server; the client registers itself (POST /oauth/register, RFC 7591) and the owner signs in once on the consent page. authorization_code + PKCE S256 (required); a token minted with resource=https://getterdone.ai/mcp works only at /mcp. Paid task creation still needs the owner's one-time identity check, card and funding token.

Owner registers the agent at https://getterdone.ai/register-agent (Stripe Identity KYC + card) and gets an API key gd_<clientId>:<clientSecret>; POST /api/auth/agent/token (client_credentials, scope agent:full) returns a Bearer token valid 1 h. Developer path: GET /api/auth/agent/challenge then POST /api/auth/agent/register (proof-of-work).

mcp.notes: Stateless JSON-RPC over POST. Tools include quote_task, create_task, get_task, list_tasks, get_pending_reviews, approve_task, dispute_task, cancel_task, events_poll, get_funding_status. Also a stdio package, @getterdone/mcp-server on npm (API key). Not in the official MCP Registry (search 'getterdone' returned 0 on 2026-10-26).

Agents spend under a funding token (single-use by default, or recurring) within owner-set per-task and daily caps. No prepaid balance: fund_account is a deprecated no-op.

Tasks pass content moderation (keyword blocklist, AI classifier) and can be suspended when workers flag them. The Acceptable Use Policy bans following, photographing or recording a specific individual without documented consent, and tasks inside private residences.
requester.unknown: How moderation detects person-targeting tasks in practice is not documented; Starter owners can post before their identity is verified.

human.method: Workers must complete Stripe Connect identity verification and bank setup before they can claim a task; worker trust scores gate claims.

camera.unknown: Metadata can be stripped, so its absence proves nothing; no C2PA or signed capture.

time.unknown: EXIF can be stripped or edited and carries no timezone; the check is informational only.

location.method: Device-GPS proximity check at submit, plus photo EXIF GPS vs the task location (within_radius / out_of_range / no_gps, exifDistanceKm).
location.unknown: GPS spoofing is not addressed; the radius is not published; EXIF GPS can be stripped.

content.unknown: The automated check cannot judge meaning; whether a photo shows the right thing is up to the buyer.

tasks: new drone capture of a polygon
raw photos (JPEG, DNG)

thermal

Final price in a per-order quote (finalPrice, currency, expiryDate); permit and non-standard costs can be added.

Globhe's use of data the client marks in writing as critical needs express consent. Operators assign all IP in uploaded content to Globhe. Data Library purchases carry no IP transfer. No AI-training or resale clause.

cards.name: Hire a Human
cards.summary: Small freelance marketplace (operated by Design 3D Solutions Ltd, founder Tom Carr) for physical and digital tasks, where people and AI agents post tasks with a budget and Veriff-verified freelancers bid on them. Agents post through a REST API with a scoped x-api-key, issued only after the operator passes Veriff KYC; an MCP server is advertised but its URL is not published. Payment is held in escrow and released when the client confirms the work. Published headline numbers conflict (142 vs 56+ countries; 3,275+ vs 1,200+ tasks completed).
cards.short: A freelance marketplace where AI agents post tasks by API and Veriff-verified people bid to do them.

tasks: on-site inspections
mystery shopping and inventory checks
photography
event attendance and real-time reporting
deliveries, errands and sample collection
field research
quality checks
phone calls

pricing.model: client sets a budget and freelancers bid their own rate; no client fee; 10% deducted from the freelancer on completion
pricing.unit: hour (typical physical-task rate, not a minimum)
pricing.notes: Provider: freelancers 'typically $15–$30/hr for physical tasks and $30–$100+ for digital work'; 'Clients: No fees — you pay the agreed task price, nothing extra'; no minimums. Listed freelancer profiles show rates as low as $5/hr, so $15 is the stated typical floor, not a minimum.

latency.typical: Not published
latency.notes: FAQ: 'physical tasks in active areas are often filled within hours' with an urgent deadline and a fair budget. That is time to find a freelancer, not to deliver. Escrow releases 24–48 hours after the client approves; disputes are reviewed within 48 hours.

coverage.notes: Coverage claims conflict: the home page shows 142 countries, 2,847+ verified humans and 3,275+ tasks completed (fixed numbers in the site's code, not live counts); the FAQ says '56+ countries' and 'over 1,200 completed tasks', as does llms.txt. The View Tasks page's '150 Active Tasks' and '$1.2M Total Value' and its task list are sample data built into the page. The Browse Humans directory shows real-looking profiles (first ones in Pakistan, Kenya and Nigeria), each showing 0 completed tasks. No country list is published.

licensing.summary: The Terms (Design 3D Solutions Ltd, effective 2026-02-20, Delaware law) are a generic AI-service template: users own their 'inputs (prompts)' and the 'AI Outputs generated specifically for you', and grant the operator a perpetual, worldwide licence to use them to provide and improve the Services, 'including anonymized/aggregated use for AI/ML development'; opt-out of non-essential use by email to privacy@design3dsolutions.com. Users may not 'Train competing AI models with our outputs or prompts' or scrape content. Nothing addresses who owns a freelancer's deliverables (photos, reports), resale, or the buyer's right to train AI on them.

human.method: Veriff KYC for every freelancer (government ID photo plus selfie video liveness check, automated review) before the profile goes live; agent operators must pass KYC before generating API keys
human.unknown: Whether the verified account holder is the person who actually does the task; no per-task identity check is described.

application.unknown: No capture app: the FAQ says there is no mobile app yet, and proof of work is uploaded through the website.

camera.unknown: No live-capture requirement is described; uploaded proof could be any file, including an old or edited photo.

time.unknown: No capture-time check on proof is described; only platform timestamps on job status.

location.unknown: No GPS, check-in or location check on the freelancer or the proof is described.

content.method: The freelancer uploads proof of work and marks the job complete; the client reviews it and releases escrow; support reviews disputes within 48 hours
content.unknown: The platform does not say it checks proof itself; whether the proof shows what was asked rests on the client's own review.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check of deliverables is offered.

auth.how_to_get: Sign up as 'AI Agent / MCP', pass Veriff KYC (ID plus selfie, usually under 10 minutes), then generate a key (prefix hah_) in the AI Agent Dashboard. Keys are scoped (dashboard: read, write, financial, profile; the developer guide says read, write, full), expire (30 days by default) and are shown once.

Lists tasks.

No endpoint for task status, applicants or deliverables is published (the guide also lists POST /api-task-apply, which is for applying to a task). The provider says it runs an MCP server endpoint, but publishes no URL, and none is in the MCP Registry (quest.hireahuman/quest is a different service, hireahuman.quest). No OAuth metadata is served.

delivery.basis: No delivery time is published. FAQ: 'physical tasks in active areas are often filled within hours' (time to hire, not to deliver).

payment.notes: The agreed price is deposited into escrow before work begins and released on the client's confirmation (minus the freelancer's 10%). FAQ: clients pay by credit/debit card, PayPal or bank transfer, through Stripe; the agent dashboard also offers escrow deposits in USDT, and the safety post calls crypto 'an additional option' with admin-verified escrow. A 'financial' API key scope covers 'Load funds, view balance & transactions', but how an agent funds a task over the API is not documented.

requester.checks: Every agent account must be backed by a person or organisation that passes Veriff KYC before it can generate API keys or post tasks. Task posts go through automated screening (said to catch about 17% of problematic listings), user reports and daily admin review; the terms prohibit illegal, harmful or deceptive tasks, and violators are suspended.

Agent flow: authenticate by API key, POST /api-tasks with title, description, offered rate, deadline and target type (ai, human or both); freelancers apply; escrow in fiat or crypto
Safety post (2026-02-26): no anonymous agents, task screening layers, crypto payments through admin-verified escrow with Stripe as the primary method

cards.name: Bee Maps (Hivemapper)
cards.summary: Dashcam street-level imagery network run by Hivemapper, Inc. (dba Bee Maps). Contributors drive with Bee cameras and, since August 2026, are paid by default in USDC funded by Bee Maps. Data is sold through the Bee Maps Data API: imagery, ML-detected road features, AI event videos, and on-demand collection (Burst and video requests) for a chosen location.
cards.short: A dashcam network that can be asked for fresh imagery or video of a specific street.

tasks: street-level imagery by polygon (latest, or a specific week)
road feature detections (speed limit and stop signs, fire hydrants, traffic lights, parking and turn restrictions, crosswalks)
AI event videos (harsh braking, aggressive acceleration, swerving, high speed, high g-force, stop sign violation) with GPS traces and IMU data
on-demand imagery collection (Burst) for a point and radius
on-demand video request for a polygon or a driven line within a time window

pricing.model: consumption-based, prepaid balance, no upfront commitment
pricing.notes: Public rate card: imagery $0.005 per image; AI event videos $6 per video; road detections $3 per 1,000 detections; Burst $1 per location, paid only when the location is mapped. The price of a /requestVideo order is not published. Bee Edge AI is priced separately ($15/device/month own devices; $0.02/km network devices). Prepaid API balance; add funds $5 to $1,000 through Stripe checkout; new accounts get $20 free credits with no card required. Price increases take effect 14 days after posting.

latency.typical: Archive imagery days to weeks old; Burst results within hours in urban areas, days in rural areas
latency.notes: Per the Data API guide. No SLA or measured latency is published, and Burst timing is described qualitatively. A Burst location stays active for a validity window (the reference example is 30 days); a /requestVideo order expires if no qualifying video is recorded before validUntil.

regions: Burst: global, depends on local driver density
coverage.notes: Provider states 754M total km mapped, 22M unique km and 37% of world roads (beemaps.com counters, self-reported; the API reference says 36%). Density per region is not published in the pages read. Max query area 5 sq km per request.

licensing.summary: The Data Products Terms of Service (Q4 2025) grant a non-exclusive, non-sublicensable, non-transferable right to use the Bee Maps Data Products only in connection with the customer's own Implementations (products that interoperate with the APIs). The customer may not transfer, distribute, resell, lease or (sub)license the Services or Data Products, use them to build a competing product or for benchmarking, and must protect them from scraping. Bee Maps and its licensors exclusively own all rights in the Data Products. The terms do not mention AI or ML training; the docs market AI event videos and imagery for model training, and the Data API guide advertises 'flexible licensing: build derived datasets from imagery', but neither is licence text.

human.unknown: Capture is passive dashcam recording. Contributors get random three-word usernames and sign in by email; no identity or uniqueness check of contributors is documented.

application.method: Only approved Open Camera devices (such as the Bee) contribute. Each new device starts with low trust and builds credibility by passing visual challenges and agreeing with other devices' detections (Hivemapper Network docs).
application.unknown: No device or firmware attestation is documented. These are Hivemapper Network reward checks; whether they still apply after Bee Maps ended its services agreement with the Hivemapper Foundation (July 2026), and whether API data is filtered by them, is not stated.

camera.method: Imagery comes from Bee Maps' own dashcam hardware; the network's vision-based consensus is described as defending against AI-generated imagery and replay attacks.
camera.unknown: No hardware-level signing or attestation is published, and Bee Maps is not on the C2PA conforming products list. Whether a single unverified device's imagery can reach API results is unknown.

time.method: Each frame and video carries a device timestamp; network consensus treats observations as valid when independent devices agree at the same location and time window.
time.unknown: The clock source and any trusted time-stamping are not documented.

location.method: Dual-band (L1/L5) GNSS module with embedded security; frames return GNSS quality metrics (gdop, hdop, pdop, eph, cno) and IMU data; contributions are checked at the H3 hex level against other devices.
location.unknown: Resistance to GNSS spoofing and how the accuracy metrics are derived are not documented. The Helium-hotspot location check described in older Hivemapper posts could not be fetched and is not relied on.

content.method: Road features are ML detections returned with confidence scores, detection counts and first/last-seen dates; faces, bodies, vehicles and licence plates are blurred on the device.
content.unknown: Confidence calibration, error rates, and any human review of detections are not published.

corroboration.method: Vision-based consensus: observations from multiple independent devices at the same hex and time window are cross-referenced, with device-diversity weighting and de-duplication of devices in the same vehicle.
corroboration.unknown: In low-traffic areas there may be too little overlap for consensus. Whether imagery sold through the API, especially a fresh Burst or video request with a single contributor, is corroborated is not stated.

auth.how_to_get: Sign in at beemaps.com, then Developers > API Key > Get API Key. Sent as 'Authorization: Basic <API_KEY>' (the key itself; the docs do not mention base64 encoding).
Same key as ?apiKey=<API_KEY>. Works on all authenticated endpoints; the OpenAPI spec lists it as the scheme for /burst/create. The MCP server also takes it (https://beemaps.com/api/mcp?apiKey=...).
Accepted by the MCP endpoint per its 401 response. No OAuth: no protected-resource or authorization-server metadata is served.

endpoints.notes: Detected road features within a polygon.

endpoints.notes: On-demand imagery collection. Goes live in the Bee App at once and drivers in range get a push notification. $1 per location, paid only when mapped. Returns id, status, validFrom, validUntil. Rate limit 10 creations per minute.

cards.name: Hover

cards.summary: Hover sends a capture request (a link by SMS or email) to a homeowner, adjuster or other person at the property, who scans it with the Hover phone app. Hover turns the photos into a 3D model with roof, exterior or interior measurements (PDF, JSON, XLSX, ESX and more). The user owns the photos it submits (User Data) but grants Hover a perpetual, transferable licence to them, including for training Hover's models, and assigns Hover any Hover Data derived from them.

human.unknown: The capture is done by whoever accepts the link and signs up with the invited email; the job records that account's email (capture_by), but no identity check is documented.

application.method: Captures must be made in the Hover mobile app on a phone.
application.unknown: No app-integrity or attestation method is published; the Terms only disclaim liability for rooted or jailbroken devices.

camera.unknown: No capture signing (C2PA or other) documented; Hover is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.unknown: The API reports capture records with created_at times, but no capture-time attestation is documented.

location.unknown: Hover collects image metadata and the location where each image was taken to build the model, but documents no check that the capture was made at the requested address, and the API exposes only the job address coordinates.

content.unknown: Measurements are computed by Hover from the photos; the Terms provide Hover Data as is, with no warranty of accuracy.

corroboration.unknown: No independent confirmation offered.

cards.name: Human Archive
cards.short: First-person video, depth, motion and touch data of real work for robot labs, from head-worn rigs and a phone app.

tasks: egocentric video of people doing their jobs in real workplaces (factories, restaurants, laundries, salons, warehouses, construction sites, hotels) and homes, recorded on Human Archive's head-worn multi-camera rigs
rigs with a global-shutter stereo pair and hardware-synchronised IMU; tactile gloves, full-body motion-capture suits and wrist cameras synchronised with RGB-D
first-person video tasks recorded by paid contributors in the Human Archive iOS app (video plus IMU and, where the phone has it, LiDAR depth; no audio)
Voice Exchange: solo and two-party voice recordings (audio only), licensed as separate datasets

pricing.model: Quote
pricing.notes: No prices are published. Buyers use a contact form ('we'll send over our researcher dashboard and samples'), book a call, or email raj@humanarchive.ai.

latency.typical: Not published
latency.notes: No turnaround is stated for new collection. In the app, contributors pick posted tasks and payouts follow approval.

freshness.typical_age: Ongoing collection; catalogue data is existing footage
freshness.notes: Human Archive sells from an 'OTS catalog' (its HARD-2 benchmark used 100 hours from it) and says it works 'alongside leading AI labs to scale human video/sensor data'. It publishes no order flow for collection to a buyer's spec, so how much of a buyer's data is captured after the order is not stated.

coverage.notes: Press reports put most collection in India, through 120+ partner businesses (hotels, restaurants, home services, quick commerce), with expansion to Southeast Asia and early US pilots (TechCrunch, Inc42, May 2026). Wing VC describes a network across homes, factories and warehouses in 'the U.S., India, and beyond'. The contributor app is on the US App Store; its terms exclude residents of Illinois, Texas, Washington and Oregon. Human Archive's own site lists no countries.

licensing.summary: App contributors keep ownership of their clips and grant Human Archive a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, sublicensable licence to use them 'to develop, train, evaluate, and improve machine-learning and robotics models' and to include them 'in datasets Human Archive licenses to its customers for those purposes'. Customers receive data 'under a written agreement' that restricts use to the agreed purposes, prohibits re-identifying contributors and requires confidentiality (privacy policy). The buyer licence is not public; resale, buyer ownership and Human Archive's reuse of a buyer's data are not stated. Terms for footage collected through partner businesses' workers are not published. The Ego500 release is described as open-source, but no licence is shown on its page.

human.method: App contributors hold accounts, confirm they are 18 or over, and pass identity checks run by the payout providers (Stripe, Circle) where required; Human Archive receives only the verification status. Workplace footage comes from workers at partner businesses.
human.unknown: No identity method is published for partner-business workers, and no per-recording identity record is public.

application.method: Workplace capture uses Human Archive's own head-worn rig; app tasks are recorded in the Human Archive app, and nothing is uploaded until the contributor taps Submit.
application.unknown: No device or app attestation is documented.

camera.method: Global-shutter stereo cameras with a hardware-synchronised IMU on the rig; phone camera, IMU and LiDAR in the app. Contributors confirm each recording is genuine and not altered with generative-AI or post-production tools.
camera.unknown: No signed capture; Human Archive is not on the C2PA conforming products list. Screen or generated footage is excluded only by contributor confirmation and review.

time.method: Session metadata records when a recording was collected; rig video and IMU share a hardware clock.
time.unknown: The hardware clock aligns streams to each other; no signed or independently time-stamped capture time is documented.

location.method: Collection metadata includes the environment and location; the app uses device location only if the contributor grants permission.
location.unknown: No location proof is documented, and app location is optional.

content.method: App clips: on-device hand-visibility check, about one frame a minute sent to Google's Gemini API to confirm the assigned task, human review of flagged clips and random audits. Workplace footage: a QA model cuts and filters sessions, then annotators verify clips and labels and an independent reviewer approves them (100+ annotators; 0.763 inter-annotator agreement on boundaries).
content.unknown: Acceptance rates and per-dataset QA results are not published beyond Ego500's agreement figure.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms individual captures. HARD-1 and HARD-2 are Human Archive's own robot benchmarks of data usefulness, not checks of provenance.

delivery.basis: Human Archive says it is 'working alongside leading AI labs to scale human video/sensor data' and offers an 'OTS catalog'; it publishes no turnaround for new collection.

auth.how_to_get: Fill in the contact form at humanarchive.ai/contact.html (name, email, notes), book a call through the cal.com link on the home page, or email team@humanarchive.ai or raj@humanarchive.ai.

mcp.notes: No Human Archive server in the official MCP Registry (searched 'human-archive' and 'humanarchive', 2026-10-26).

api.notes: No public API or API docs. Buyers are offered a 'researcher dashboard and samples' after contact. humanarchive.ai returns 404 for /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

payment.notes: No buyer payment method is published; terms are set in a written customer agreement.

consent.method: Published for the contributor app only: contributors accept a consent confirmation before each recording session, which is logged with the task and session metadata; Voice Exchange adds a one-time voice consent and a per-call consent from both parties. Video tasks must show only the contributor's own hands and task, never other people or children; recording at work needs the employer's written permission and must not capture customers. Contributors can delete their account, but approved clips are de-identified and kept in datasets.
consent.unknown: Human Archive publishes nothing on how workers at partner businesses, who wear its head-mounted rigs at work, are told about or consent to recording. Its co-founder told Inc42 that partner contracts require partners to obtain informed consent and that it is 'the partner companies' responsibility to educate their employees'; TechCrunch wrote that 'it is not clear what information Human Archive gives workers about how their footage is used'. For home-service visits, press reports say customers choose a discounted recorded visit or a full-price unrecorded one; that flow is not published by Human Archive.

Voice contributors who join through a distributor network are paid by that network.

requester.unknown: Human Archive publishes no check of who a buyer is or what the data is for, beyond the written customer agreement described in its privacy policy.

cards.name: Human For AI
cards.short: One pseudonymous human operator who takes agent tasks by API or MCP, free during a pilot. Signed text receipts.
cards.summary: A one-person human-in-the-loop service ("Operator 001", pseudonymous) that AI agents call over a keyless REST API or a remote MCP server. Tasks include real-world verification with photo or text evidence and local physical-world errands (visit, photograph, check, measure, observe) in the operator's undisclosed local service area, plus remote testing, review and judgment work. Every task is reviewed by the operator before acceptance; everything is free during a proof-of-concept pilot. Each delivered task carries an Ed25519-signed JWS receipt over the sha256 of the delivered text and the task's lifecycle timestamps, checkable offline against a published key set.

tasks: real-world verification with photo or text evidence (place, product, price, business, claim)
local physical-world tasks in the operator's service area: visit, photograph, deliver, check, measure, observe
on-site photos and observation of a location at a specific time
counts and documentation on site (dimensions, quantities, queue lengths, foot traffic, posted notices)
manual data collection, labeling and research
remote work: product/app testing, AI output review, human judgment, decision escalation

pricing.model: free proof-of-concept pilot
pricing.notes: Every service is $0 per task during the pilot (the only tier); budget_usd is accepted and ignored. No payment step exists, and tasks accepted during the pilot are never billed retroactively. Paid tiers may come later and would be announced on /pricing and in /agent.json first.

latency.typical: First response within 12 hours; typical response about 4 hours
latency.notes: Response targets are 'honest targets, not a contractual SLA'. Working hours every day 19:00-00:00 operator local time; urgent tasks by prior arrangement only. Physical errands are scheduled after acceptance, so delivery time is not stated. human.json also lists working_days Sunday-Thursday, which conflicts with 'any day of the week' elsewhere.

delivery.basis: Provider: 'First response comes within 12 hours, any day of the week; the errand itself is scheduled after acceptance.' No delivery time is stated.

freshness.typical_age: Captured after the operator accepts the task
freshness.notes: No archive. Deliverables state what was observed, what was inferred and the operator's confidence.

coverage.notes: One person. The exact service area is not published ('confirmed at task review to protect operator privacy'); wider coverage 'by arrangement'. Out-of-reach locations are declined or counter-proposed at review. English only. Remote tasks (testing, review, research) have no stated place limit but are not physical capture.

licensing.summary: Terms (effective 2026-07-19): once delivered, the deliverable is the requester's, who 'receives all rights to use, modify, and republish it, for any lawful purpose'. The operator keeps internal records but does not publish task content. Resale and AI training are not named. Privacy policy (effective 2026-07-06): task data is 'never sold, shared with advertisers, or used to train AI models'.

human.method: The service is one human operator, known only as Operator 001, who reviews and performs every task; the trust page marks 'Real, single human operator' and 'Contactable identity' as true
human.unknown: The operator is deliberately pseudonymous. Third-party identity verification (government ID through an independent provider) is listed as pending, so 'verified human' is the service's own word.

application.unknown: No capture app or device attestation is described.

camera.unknown: No live-capture rule, camera attestation or C2PA signing is described. Signed receipts cover the delivered text only, not photos or files (media hashing is an open roadmap item).

time.method: Physical-task reports come with 'timestamped photos'; each delivered task's receipt signs the task's lifecycle timestamps (submitted, accepted, delivered), verifiable against https://humanforai.dev/.well-known/jwks.json
time.unknown: The provider states the receipt timestamps are 'our own assertion, signed. Nobody outside this service witnessed them'; external anchoring is not built. How photo timestamps are produced is not stated, and the lifecycle times are not the capture time.

location.unknown: No GPS stamp, check-in or location check is described; where a photo was taken rests on the operator's report.

content.method: The operator who does the work writes the deliverable with a confidence block separating what was observed from what was inferred; the signed receipt binds the sha256 of the delivered text so later alteration is detectable
content.unknown: The receipt proves the text is unaltered and came from humanforai.dev, not that it is true; the terms call deliverables 'assistance, not guaranteed truth'. Photos and files are not covered by the receipt.

corroboration.unknown: One operator; no independent second capture or cross-check is offered.

auth.how_to_get: No keys, OAuth or accounts. The protected-resource metadata states authentication_not_required: true and no authorization server exists. A task needs a real return channel: a contact_email whose domain is MX-checked, or delivery: 'status_poll' (deliverable returned as text in operator_notes; 1 such task per client per day).

endpoints.params: limit (1-50), cursor
endpoints.notes: Service catalog (11 task types; the catalog is examples, not limits).

endpoints.params: task_type, description (10-5000 chars) required; location_required, location_detail, deadline (ISO 8601), output_format, contact_email (required unless delivery is status_poll), delivery (email|status_poll), requester; optional Idempotency-Key header
endpoints.notes: Returns 202 with task_id and status_url. Submission is not acceptance: the operator accepts or rejects each task. Duplicates within 24 h return 409.
submitted -> accepted -> delivered, or rejected with a reason; status_history, seen_by_operator_at and an operator-set eta. Anyone holding the task_id can read its public status.

Once delivered: operator_notes (the deliverable text for status_poll tasks), receipt (compact JWS, EdDSA), deliverable_sha256 and receipt_issued_at. Email-delivery deliverables also go to contact_email.

api.sdk: npm humanforai 0.1.4 (stdio MCP proxy); PyPI humanforai 0.1.0 (client and CLI with verify-receipt); Go module github.com/humanforai/humanforai-go
api.rate_limits: Per-client hourly and daily submission caps plus a global daily pilot capacity (429 with Retry-After, resets 00:00 UTC); RateLimit headers on responses; repeat abusers blocked (403). One small test task is welcome; bulk synthetic submissions get the client blocked.

mcp.notes: Streamable HTTP, stateless, no auth. Tools: get_human_services, submit_human_task, check_task_status, message_human_operator. Registry latest is v0.1.4 with the remote URL and the npm stdio package.

api.notes: Messages to the operator: POST /api/v1/messages (reply_to email or an https webhook URL; replies signed with HMAC-SHA256) and a pollable thread with a one-time access token. Receipts are issued only for tasks delivered from 2026-07-20, and are re-issued if the operator edits a deliverable. The receipt is a compact JWS over deliverable_sha256 and lifecycle timestamps, not the detached RFC 8785 receipt of the irlpls standard.

payment.notes: Nothing to pay during the pilot: no payment step, invoice or card. The service says it never asks for payment, credentials or accounts, and that any such request is not from it.

requester.checks: No account or identity check. Each task needs a working return channel (MX-checked email, or the status-poll path capped at one task per client per day). The operator reviews every task before acceptance and rejects illegal, deceptive, unsafe and privacy-invasive work, explicitly including surveillance of individuals, stalking and doxxing. Rate limits, duplicate detection and a blocklist (on a salted hash of the caller's network address) handle abuse. The terms bind an agent's principal to what the agent submits.
requester.unknown: Who the requester is is not checked beyond the return channel; screening rests on one person's review of the task description.

cards.name: ICEYE
cards.summary: ICEYE runs a large synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation that images through cloud and at night. Its Tasking API v2 is for customers with a contract. They can get a price, check feasibility and task a new capture centred on a point. The capture window is at least 24 hours wide and ends within 14 days. The customer picks the imaging mode (Strip, Scan, Spot, Dwell and their variants), the priority, and how soon products are available after acquisition: 8, 3 or 1 hour.

tasks: task a new SAR capture centred on a point (or anywhere covering an AOI circle, with aoiRadiusMeters) in an acquisition window at least 24 h wide, ending within 14 days
imaging modes: STRIPMAP, SCAN, SCAN_WIDE, SPOTLIGHT, SPOTLIGHT_EXTENDED_AREA, SPOTLIGHT_FINE, SPOTLIGHT_EXTENDED_DWELL (and _FINE, _PRECISE), as allowed by contract
price a task before ordering (amount and currency, minor units), on contracts with a pricing plan
feasibility check for a list of candidate tasks (FEASIBLE / INFEASIBLE, and budget fit where priced)
priority BACKGROUND or COMMERCIAL (stated >90% statistical reliability)
product availability SLA: 8 h (default), 3 h, or 1 h in certain regions after acquisition
product types GRD, GRD-COG, SLC, SLC-COG, QLK, SICD, SIDD, CSI, VID as the contract and mode allow
Detect & Classify derivative DC-ATR (aircraft, vessels, vehicles) on Dwell modes and SPOTLIGHT_FINE, where enabled
planned and actual imaging time and footprint via the task scene endpoint
delivery to SFTP or S3 locations, and webhook notifications on task changes

pricing.model: per task, set by contract (region, priority, imaging mode, SLA, exclusivity, EULA)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published, not free. Each contract has a fixed pricing model, and the same task can cost different amounts under different contracts. GET /tasking/v2/price returns the price in minor currency units, but only on contracts with a pricing plan (hasPricingPlan). The docs' example of 529199 USD minor units (about $5,292) is only an example. Cancelling is free within 1 hour of submission or more than 72 h before the window. After that it costs 10% of the order value at 72-48 h, 20% at 48-24 h and 100% under 24 h, and a task cannot be cancelled once the window has started.

latency.typical: Products available 8 h after acquisition by default, 3 h or 1 h with a faster SLA; acquisition happens somewhere in a window of at least 24 h that cannot start immediately
latency.notes: The minimum lead time before collection is 12 h for COMMERCIAL priority and 24 h for BACKGROUND (Product Specification, Table 3-2). The scheduler decides ACTIVE or REJECTED within 20 minutes of submission. The SLA counts from the end of acquisition and leaves out download or delivery time. Non-SLA products usually follow within about an hour, with no guarantee.

regions: Global (subject to orbit passes, contract and scheduling)
coverage.notes: SAR works through cloud and at night. Prices vary by region with demand. The contract decides which regions, imaging modes, priorities and exclusivity you may use, and the 1-hour SLA applies only in certain regions.

licensing.summary: Each task picks a STANDARD or GOVERNMENT EULA, and the full terms are in the customer's contract. ICEYE US publishes its EULA (updated 2 December 2025). It grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence for the End User's internal use only. It forbids distributing, sublicensing, selling, publishing or making products public, and forbids commercial use. ICEYE keeps all title to products and to the parts of them inside the customer's derivatives. 'Data Derivatives' are outputs that keep no SAR pixels or sensor or ephemeris data and cannot be reversed back to them. The customer owns these outright and may use them for any purpose, credited 'Powered by ICEYE'. AI or ML training is not mentioned. Exclusivity: PUBLIC images go into ICEYE's public catalog 14 days after acquisition, where other customers can buy them. PRIVATE images are withheld from that catalog. The Product Specification says permanently, and the API docs say for the contract's agreed period.

freshness.typical_age: Captured in your window, available hours after acquisition
freshness.notes: ICEYE also sells past images from its archive catalog, where new images appear at least 14 days after acquisition. irlpls lists ICEYE only for new tasked captures.

auth.how_to_get: ICEYE issues a TOKEN_URL, CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET during onboarding on a contract. To start onboarding, fill in the SAR data contact form at https://www.iceye.com/contact/sar-data. POST grant_type=client_credentials to the TOKEN_URL with HTTP Basic auth (client id and secret) to get a bearer token that lasts 3600 s. v2 does not support the older username and password flow.

endpoints.notes: Your contracts: allowed imaging modes, priorities, SLAs, exclusivity, delivery locations, start/end dates, and hasPricingPlan.
Budget: consolidatedSpent, onHold, optional spendLimit (minor units). Only for contracts with a pricing plan; available funds = spendLimit - consolidatedSpent - onHold.

endpoints.params: contractID, pointOfInterest[lat], pointOfInterest[lon], imagingMode; optional acquisitionWindow, exclusivity, priority, sla, eula, incidenceAngle, lookSide, passDirection, reference
endpoints.notes: Returns {amount, currency}, amount in minor units; 403 if the parameters are not allowed by the contract or the contract has no pricing plan.

endpoints.params: array of tasks with the createTask fields (all with the same priority)
endpoints.notes: Returns FEASIBLE / INFEASIBLE per task; also checks budget when the contract has a pricing plan.

endpoints.params: contractID, pointOfInterest {lat, lon}, acquisitionWindow {start, end}, imagingMode; optional reference, priority, sla, exclusivity, eula, incidenceAngle, lookSide, passDirection, aoiRadiusMeters, productTypes, derivativeProductTypes, deliveries, notifications
endpoints.notes: Returns 201 with status RECEIVED; the scheduler sets ACTIVE or REJECTED within 20 minutes. 400 ERR_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS if the contract budget is too low. No idempotency key is documented; the free-text reference field can tag tasks.
Status RECEIVED, ACTIVE, FULFILLED (SLA products ready), DONE (all products), or terminal REJECTED, CANCELED, FAILED.
Planned (ACTIVE) or actual (FULFILLED/DONE) imaging time, incidence angle, look side, pass direction and footprint.

endpoints.params: limit, cursor, contractID, createdAfter, createdBefore and filters
endpoints.notes: Your tasks.

endpoints.params: cursor
endpoints.notes: STAC-like items with signed download URLs that expire after 1 hour; available once the task is FULFILLED or DONE. /products/{productType} returns one type.
STAC items; use only to fetch metadata for your own tasked captures (collections incl. private/tasking), not as an archive route.

api.rate_limits: Not published in the pages read.
api.notes: To cancel, PATCH /tasking/v2/tasks/{taskID} with {"status": "CANCELED"} while the task is RECEIVED or ACTIVE (charges in pricing.notes). Webhooks are registered with the Notifications API. Delivery to SFTP or S3 uses config IDs set up by ICEYE. Every tasking request needs a contractID. The API docs show paths without the /api prefix, which is part of base_url. ICEYE publishes an open-source demo app on GitHub (github.com/iceye-ltd), but no official SDK was found.

mcp.notes: No ICEYE MCP server is in the official MCP Registry (search 'iceye' returned 0 servers, 2026-10-26).

human.unknown: ICEYE satellites capture the images, not people. Whether a person reviews a capture before delivery is not stated.

application.unknown: No public signing or checksum scheme for delivered products was found. Download URLs are signed for access only, not to prove where the content came from.

camera.method: Products come from ICEYE's own SAR satellites in a stated imaging mode, with sensor and orbit metadata
camera.unknown: Which satellite and sensor took the image is ICEYE's word. No cryptographic provenance is published.

time.method: The task scene reports the actual imaging start and end, and product items carry start_datetime and end_datetime inside the requested window
time.unknown: No independent or signed timestamp. How acquisition times are validated is not documented.

location.method: Tasks target a WGS 84 point. Products are geolocated using refined orbits and calibrated against ground-surveyed corner-reflector sites. ICEYE gives a fleet worst-case RMSE of 6 m, and its June-November 2025 campaign at Rosamond (521 images) found mean errors under 0.4 m.
location.unknown: The accuracy figures are ICEYE's own statistics, not proof for a single delivered image, and the campaign's raw data are not public. Error grows with terrain-model uncertainty.

content.unknown: No public method for detecting manipulated SAR imagery or proving what a product shows. Within 14 days you can report that a product does not meet the spec.

corroboration.unknown: No documented cross-check of a delivered capture against other sensors

delivery.basis: From the Create Task and Product Specification docs: products are available SLA_8H (default), SLA_3H or SLA_1H after acquisition. The window must start at least 12 h ahead (COMMERCIAL) or 24 h ahead (BACKGROUND), be at least 24 h wide and end within 14 days, so the time from order to product is usually more than a day.

payment.notes: The contract has a spend limit, and a task fails with ERR_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS if it would go over. Under the ICEYE US direct-sales terms (v1.0, April 2021), fees are invoiced every two weeks and due within 30 days, in euros unless the order says otherwise. ICEYE has a separate invoicing process, and no card or agent payment rail was found.

requester.checks: Customers are onboarded by ICEYE's COSP team and contract with ICEYE, and contracts set what each customer may task. Under the US direct-sales terms, ICEYE may accept or reject any order at its sole discretion. Orders may be subject to government regulatory review, and ICEYE can modify or terminate an order to comply. Customers must follow export controls and must not distribute products to sanctioned parties. The EULA choice (STANDARD or GOVERNMENT) depends on the type of end user.
requester.unknown: What due diligence ICEYE runs on new customers during onboarding (KYC, end-use or target screening) is not published.

cards.name: Kled AI
cards.short: A consumer app whose ID-checked contributors capture photos, video and audio to a lab's spec, claimed in under 72 hours.

tasks: custom capture to a spec built from 108 task templates (camera, microphone, screen recording, touch, keyboard)
egocentric hand-task video (e.g. reorganizing a room, two-handed repair)
multi-view object photos (the same object from every angle)
native conversational speech in rare languages

pricing.model: Quote
pricing.notes: Not published. The dataset request form asks for a budget band (under $10K, $10K-50K, $50K-250K, $250K+).

latency.typical: Under 72 hours to build and deploy a task to contributors; Kled also says any consumer dataset can be collected in under 72 hours (provider claim)
latency.notes: Kled V3 post, 30 Sep 2026; no SLA. The request form lets the buyer set the date the data is needed by.

freshness.typical_age: Task captures are recorded after the task is deployed
freshness.notes: The catalogue also sells 'Existing files' from contributors' camera rolls; only 'Task capture' (made to order) is a commission.

coverage.notes: Kled says its contributors are 'across the US, Southeast Asia and Europe'. Its Trace ledger, by receipt volume, shows Southeast Asia 74.5%, Sub-Saharan Africa 22.7%, North America 2%, EU 0.4%, MENA 0.3%, Latin America 0.1%. Catalogue task-capture datasets list '100+ countries'. Kled can route contributors to a region (e.g. 'egocentric video from Southeast Asia this week').

licensing.summary: Contributors grant Kled a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence, sublicensable through multiple tiers and exclusive to Kled for AI and ML training. Buyers receive 'a license written for model training'; catalogue datasets carry a 'non-exclusive commercial training license' ('train and ship commercial models'), and exclusivity and term are negotiable. The buyer licence text itself is not public; resale, buyer ownership and Kled's own reuse of delivered data are not stated.

human.method: Government ID matched via Didit at onboarding; active liveness challenge at every contribution session; each Trace receipt carries the contributor's KYC status (99.9% of receipts from verified contributors).
human.unknown: ID results are not public; only an opaque per-app ID reaches the ledger, and the KYC status on a receipt is Kled's own assertion.

application.method: Task captures are recorded in the Kled app ('Capture Tool: Phone camera (in app)'); the Camera-Original Phone Photos set is 'never imported from a camera roll'.
application.unknown: No device or app attestation is published, and the catalogue also contains camera-roll uploads.

camera.method: Camera-original files with EXIF kept; terms ban AI-generated content; the FD 1.0 fraud model screens every upload for AI-generated, internet-sourced, edited and duplicate files.
camera.unknown: FD 1.0 results are from Kled's internal evaluations only; no C2PA signing and no per-file detector result is published.

time.method: Each accepted file gets a Trace receipt within seconds; anyone can look up a file's fingerprint at trace.datafdn.org/verify.
time.unknown: A receipt shows when the file was registered, not when it was captured; which chain anchors Trace is not documented.

location.method: GPS and EXIF are kept in Kled's systems; receipts carry only the contributor's region and GPS existence flags.
location.unknown: GPS values are never public; ledger resolution is 'never finer than country / state'.

content.method: Every submission is scored for task relevance and quality before acceptance, plus consent checks and masking of faces and personal details; task templates include examples of accepted and rejected submissions.
content.unknown: Review criteria and per-dataset rejection data are not published beyond headline QA pass rates.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms individual captures; Trace is run by The Data Foundation, which invested $3M in Kled.

delivery.basis: 'Any consumer dataset that can exist, can now be collected from physical reality in under 72 hours' and 'deployed to 500,000+ contributors within 72 hours' (Kled V3 post, 30 Sep 2026).

auth.how_to_get: Submit a dataset request at kled.ai/datasets or contact sales; customers sign in at the Enterprise Portal (enterprise.kled.ai). Kled says self-serve task design is coming 'soon'.

mcp.notes: No Kled server in the official MCP Registry (searched 'kled', 2026-10-26).

api.notes: No public API docs. Dataset pages offer a 'Copy .md' button that exports specs and licence terms for an AI assistant.

payment.notes: No buyer payment method is published; terms are set with sales.

requester.checks: The dataset request form verifies the requester's email with a one-time code and a CAPTCHA.
requester.unknown: Kled publishes no check of who a buyer is or what a commission is for.

attestations.scope: security and privacy audit of Kled
attestations.result: Completed May 2026 (stated on Kled's audit portal; no report published by Trail of Bits)

cards.summary: A consumer app whose 500,000+ opt-in contributors (company figure) capture photos, video and audio to a buyer's spec, built from 108 task templates and claimed in under 72 hours. Contributors are ID-checked via Didit and pass a liveness check each session; uploads are screened by Kled's fraud model, and each accepted file gets a public receipt on the Trace audit ledger (consent version, KYC status, payout). Buyers get a model-training licence. Ordering is through sales; self-serve is announced as coming.

sources.claim: 500,000+ opt-in contributors across the US, SEA and Europe; 108 templates; collection and deployment in under 72 hours; self-serve 'soon'; FD 1.0 fraud model; relevance and quality scoring; regional routing

Custom order flow (spec, contributors capture, QA, consent checks, face masking); delivery with consent records and a licence for model training; request form fields (budget bands, licence type, email verification)
Task-capture dataset: in-app phone camera, non-exclusive commercial training licence, exclusivity negotiable, 100+ countries

Submitted content is licensed or sold to third parties to train AI; KYC uses government ID and biometric data

cards.name: LXT (clickworker)
cards.summary: AI data company LXT, which agreed to buy the German crowd platform clickworker in December 2024 and now issues clickworker's North American terms. Its crowd photographs and films to a brief: custom image and video datasets (people, pets, products, scenes, documents) shot at home, at a nearby location with the clickworker smartphone app, or in a studio; and store checks, where workers visit listed shops, photograph shelves and displays with geo data and fill in checklists. Projects are run by LXT's managed service. The clickworker Marketplace API v2 (HTTP Basic auth, access through support) can create tasks, track them, fetch results and accept or reject them; its standard products are surveys, sentiment and iFrame tasks, and photo work is set up as a custom product.

tasks: custom image collection: people and poses, pets and animals, products and objects, scenes and environments, documents and screens
custom video collection: human activity, pets, object interaction, indoor and outdoor scenes, facial and body movement
three settings: remote (at home by PC or phone app), mobile on-site (a nearby location, by smartphone app), in-person (studio, client premises or LXT data collection centre, with a moderator)
store checks and display audits: workers visit listed stores and photograph shelves, displays and promotions with the clickworker app, uploading with geo position, store name and address
on-site mystery checks with photo, video or written documentation
API: create tasks from templates (Survey, Sentiment, ExternalForm/iFrame; custom products set up by clickworker Operations), track status, fetch results, accept or reject, count workers near a point

pricing.model: Custom quote (managed); per-task worker payment you set (API/self-service)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means unknown, not free. LXT quotes image collection by number and type of images, contributor requirements, regions and metadata, and video by scope and turnaround. clickworker's FAQ says managed costs depend on time and quality requirements, with an individual offer per project. Through the API you set the worker payment per task in cents (e.g. external_form_payment); clickworker adds a basic payment surcharge (rate not published) and typically a 40% surcharge on bonuses. Self-service fees are shown on the platform when the order is submitted.

latency.typical: Store checks: 'often within hours'. Datasets: not published.
latency.notes: clickworker's store-check page says 'Results often within hours, not days'. LXT's dataset projects run briefing, setup, pilot, then full-scale capture, and LXT only says 'high throughput rates with managed service and direct app upload'. The API docs say completion 'will take some time, depending on the complexity of the work and availability of workers'.

coverage.notes: LXT cites image and video collection in 150+ countries and 1,000+ locales with 10M+ contributors; clickworker's homepage says its workforce is in 136 countries. A published store-check case study ran in DE, FR, UK, IT, ES, TR and RU with 300 to 800 stores per country. The API targets tasks by ISO country code and can count workers within a radius (minimum 10 km) or bounding box, so density near an address can be checked before ordering, with an account.

licensing.summary: clickworker's North American self-service terms (LXT AI Inc., effective 30 March 2026, §8) give the client, upon full payment, 'a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual license to use task results for its internal business purposes'; they do not mention AI training, resale of results, or LXT using client data for its own models. The rest-of-world client terms (clickworker Germany GmbH, 2012) say nothing about rights in results; managed projects run under an individual contract. Workers grant clickworker unlimited rights of use in what they produce (worker GTC §7). LXT offers mutual NDAs and markets its collected images as 'fully consented'.

human.method: Workers must be 18+, give truthful personal data and hold one account each (no alter egos); clickworker may require evidence that the data is correct before activating an account. LXT says contributors are 'vetted' and selected to the project's requirements.
human.unknown: Whether an identity document is checked for every worker is not stated; the terms only reserve the right to ask for evidence.

application.method: On-site work uses the clickworker app for Android and iOS.
application.unknown: No check that the app or device is genuine or unmodified is documented.

camera.unknown: Camera type can be included as metadata, but no check against imported, screen-captured or generated media is described.

time.unknown: A timestamp 'can be included' as metadata; how it is set and whether it can be trusted is not documented.

location.method: In the store-check case study, workers photograph the store front 'with geo data' and upload shelf pictures 'with geo position, the business address and the store name'.
location.unknown: How the geo position is captured and whether it is checked against the store is not described; geolocation is not mentioned for dataset collection.

content.method: LXT: multi-layer QA with programmatic checks, gold tasks, peer review, human review and compliance validation. Store checks: optional clickworker internal verification of the pictures. API: optional review jobs, then the customer accepts or rejects each result (buyoff).
content.unknown: Review criteria and error rates are not published.

corroboration.method: Peer review of submissions by other contributors; on the API, a separate content-review job can precede the customer's buyoff.
corroboration.unknown: Whether peer review applies to every capture project and what it checks is not described.

auth.how_to_get: HTTP Basic auth with your clickworker customer email and password. Ask clickworker support for API access (https://www.clickworker.com/contact-for-customers/, helpdesk@clickworker.com). Sandbox: https://api-sandbox.clickworker.com.
The OpenAPI file declares an access_token query parameter for Asset Library endpoints only; how to obtain one is not documented.

endpoints.notes: Products available to your account (standard: Survey, Sentiment, ExternalForm/iFrame).

endpoints.notes: Counts workers in an area before launching location-based tasks.
Creates a task from a task template (POST /customer/task_templates first). Optional notification callback URL for TASK_COMPLETED, TASK_TIMEDOUT and CUSTOMER_INPUT_REQUIRED.
States: created, queued, running, finished, timedout, cancelled, feedback (awaiting buyoff).

endpoints.notes: Results inline. Accept or reject with PUT /customer/tasks/{taskId}/accept or /reject.
Orders group tasks for billing.
