cards.name: Mapillary
cards.short: An archive of crowdsourced street-level photos.
cards.summary: Meta-owned archive of crowdsourced, geotagged street-level photos and panoramas (more than 3 billion images, contributors in 190 countries), searchable through the Mapillary Graph API by small bounding box, by point and radius (up to 50 m), or by capture date, plus machine-detected map features (traffic signs and points) and per-image detections. It returns existing imagery only: you cannot commission a new capture.

tasks: search existing street-level images by bbox (< 0.01 deg square) and capture date
find the best image near a point (lat/lng, radius up to 50 m, ranked by proximity, recency and 360°)

fetch image thumbnails (256/512/1024/2048 px and original) and metadata (captured_at, geometry, computed_geometry, compass angle, panorama flag, camera make/model, creator, organization, quality_score, on_foot)
search machine-detected map features (traffic signs, points) by bbox, type and first/last seen date, with the images each was derived from
per-image object detections (segmentation polygons with class values)
coverage and map-feature vector tiles

delivery.basis: Archive only: no new capture can be ordered.

pricing.model: free (access token required)
pricing.notes: Mapillary's platform page says imagery is accessible in the cloud 'for free'. No pricing page exists (www.mapillary.com/pricing returns 'We couldn't find the page'). Access needs a client token from an app registered in the developer dashboard. Commercial use is limited to the purposes in Terms Section 12 (see licensing).

payment.notes: No payment is published or required: the API is free with a client token. No payment methods are listed.

latency.typical: Seconds per API call (search returns existing imagery); no turnaround for new capture because none can be ordered
latency.notes: No official API latency figure found. How long after upload an image becomes searchable (processing, blurring) was not confirmed.

freshness.typical_age: Varies widely by place: from recent to many years old; depends on when a contributor last drove or walked there
freshness.notes: Every image carries captured_at, and search can filter with start_captured_at / end_captured_at, so an agent can reject stale results. There is no way to request fresh capture of a location.

regions: Global (wherever contributors have uploaded imagery; density uneven)
coverage.notes: Coverage is whatever contributors have captured. Mapillary's about page says contributors in 190 countries and more than two billion images; its home page says more than 3,000,000,000 images. Coverage vector tiles (mly1_public, mly1_computed_public) show where imagery exists. Terms Section 22 bars use from US-embargoed jurisdictions. No per-region density figures were found.

licensing.summary: Terms (effective 15 February 2024) Section 3: other users' content is under CC BY-SA 4.0 unless Mapillary indicates otherwise; some data sets may carry other terms such as CC BY-NC-SA, and those licence terms win where they conflict with the Terms. Section 12: commercial use is allowed only for (i) 'improvement, training, and development of products, services, maps, studies, platforms, websites, applications, software, algorithms, datasets, solutions, or technologies' and (ii) providing services to clients, and requires safeguards against re-identification or unblurring and a process to report incidents to vendor-incident@meta.com. Section 5 bans selling or reselling the Mapillary Services without a separate written agreement, unapproved data mining or scraping, re-identification or unblurring, and use for real-time navigation or autonomous vehicle control. Section 11: apps must materially supplement Mapillary, not merely redistribute content; downloaded images and API-derived data must show the Mapillary logo and link back. Section 13 allows use for OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps contributions. Content is owned by Mapillary or its licensors (contributors keep their rights), so a user gets a licence, not ownership. Resale is left unset: the Terms ban reselling the Services, but the CC BY-SA licence on user content allows commercial redistribution under share-alike, and the Terms say the licence wins in a conflict.

human.method: Each image exposes creator (username and id) and, where affiliated, an organization
human.unknown: Nothing documents whether a contributor is a distinct, real or identified person; uploads also come from organizations and professional rigs

application.unknown: No public attestation of which app or uploader produced an image; Mapillary accepts uploads from any camera and from desktop and command-line uploaders

camera.method: Image metadata includes camera make, model and camera_type, filterable by make and model with a bbox
camera.unknown: Make, model and altitude come from contributed metadata (the docs cite Exif for altitude and orientation) with no documented hardware attestation; they can be wrong or edited. Mapillary is not on the C2PA conforming products list

time.method: Each image has a captured_at timestamp, filterable in search
time.unknown: Where the timestamp comes from (device clock, Exif or GPS) and whether Mapillary checks it are not documented

location.method: Each image has its original geometry and compass_angle, plus computed_geometry and computed_compass_angle from Mapillary's structure-from-motion processing
location.unknown: Original GPS can be noisy or edited; how computed positions are derived and how far they can be trusted is not specified beyond pointers to OpenSfM

content.method: Faces and licence plates are automatically blurred (privacy, not authenticity); each image has a predicted visual quality_score
content.unknown: No documented checks for staged, edited or synthetic images. Blurring changes the content and can miss faces and plates (a 2018 company blog reports 99.9% detection)

corroboration.method: Map features are derived from multiple detections in multiple images (first_seen_at / last_seen_at, with the contributing images listed)
corroboration.unknown: Nothing cross-checks an individual image. Dense places may have many overlapping images an agent can compare itself; sparse places may have one

auth.how_to_get: Register an app at https://www.mapillary.com/dashboard/developers to get a client access token (needs a Mapillary account). The header form works for Entity API calls.
Same client token sent as ?access_token=XXX. Preferred for vector tiles; strongly discouraged for user access tokens.

Authorization code flow for user tokens: send the user to https://www.mapillary.com/connect?client_id=...&response_type=code, then POST the code to https://graph.mapillary.com/token with Authorization: OAuth <client secret>. Tokens expire (example expires_in 9000 s) and are refreshed at the same endpoint. Needs a pre-registered app; no self-registration, PKCE or RFC 9728 metadata is documented.

endpoints.params: bbox=left,bottom,right,top (< 0.01 deg square), start_captured_at, end_captured_at (ISO 8601), limit (max/default 2000), creator_username, is_pano (needs bbox or creator_username), make, model (bbox only), organization_id, sequence_ids, fields=id,captured_at,geometry,computed_geometry,compass_angle,is_pano,thumb_256_url,thumb_1024_url,thumb_2048_url,thumb_original_url,creator,quality_score,on_foot,...
endpoints.notes: Core call: existing images of a place and time window. Paging (after cursor) works only with creator_username. Thumbnails are URLs in the response.

endpoints.params: lat, lng, radius (metres, default and max 50), limit (default 1, max 100), fields=...
endpoints.notes: Image radius search (added 2 April 2026): returns the 'best' images near a point by proximity, recency and 360° preference. Cannot be combined with bbox, tile, s2, image_ids or sequence_ids.

endpoints.params: fields=... (e.g. thumb_2048_url,captured_at,geometry,detections.value)
endpoints.notes: Single image metadata and thumbnail URLs. Several entities of one type at once: GET /?ids=ID1,ID2

endpoints.params: bbox (< 0.01 deg square), object_values (wildcards, comma-separated), start_first_seen_at, end_first_seen_at, start_last_seen_at, end_last_seen_at, limit (max 2000), fields=id,object_value,object_type,geometry,aligned_direction,first_seen_at,last_seen_at,images
endpoints.notes: Machine-detected map objects such as traffic signs; GET /:map_feature_id fetches one, and fields=images lists the images it was derived from

endpoints.params: fields=id,created_at,geometry,image,value
endpoints.notes: Object detections in an image; geometry is a base64-encoded vector-tile polygon (extent 4096). Also /:map_feature_id/detections

endpoints.params: sequence_id
endpoints.notes: Image ids in a capture sequence; fields param not honored

endpoints.params: access_token
endpoints.notes: Coverage vector tiles (Mapbox Vector Tile spec; layers overview, sequence, image). Also mly1_computed_public, mly_map_feature_point and mly_map_feature_traffic_sign

api.rate_limits: Entity APIs 60,000/min per app; Search APIs 10,000/min per app; tiles 50,000/day. Over the limit the Graph API returns 'Application request limit reached' (code 4); tiles return 4xx. Terms Section 11 lets Mapillary throttle or revoke client_ids.
api.sdk: mapillary-python-sdk (https://github.com/mapillary/mapillary-python-sdk; the docs recommend it for areas larger than the bbox limit); MapillaryJS viewer; embed iframe at https://www.mapillary.com/embed?image_key=IMAGE_ID

mcp.community: Third-party wrapper in the official MCP Registry, not run by Mapillary: io.github.pipeworx-io/mapillary (v0.1.3, remote https://gateway.pipeworx.io/mapillary/mcp).
mcp.notes: No first-party Mapillary MCP server found.

api.notes: All requests to graph.mapillary.com and tiles.mapillary.com need a token; a keyless call returns 'Invalid OAuth 2.0 Access Token' (code 190) and tiles return 403. Entity endpoints have only limited bbox search; the docs expect vector tiles for spatial filtering at scale.

sources.claim: Base URLs graph.mapillary.com and tiles.mapillary.com; auth via Authorization: OAuth header or access_token query param; client token from developer dashboard; OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with read/write/upload scopes, token exchange and refresh

/images search params, bbox < 0.01 deg square (since 16 January 2026), image fields (thumbnails 256/512/1024/2048/original, captured_at, geometry, computed_geometry, make, model, creator, organization, quality_score, on_foot), paging only with creator_username
Image radius search (lat, lng, radius max 50 m, limit max 100), added 2 April 2026
Map features derived from multiple detections in multiple images; map_features search; detections; image_ids by sequence; multiple entities; vector tile endpoints
Rate limits: entity 60,000/min, search 10,000/min, tiles 50,000/day per app; error responses
mapillary-python-sdk recommended for large areas

Terms effective 15 February 2024, provided by Meta Platforms Ireland: user content under CC BY-SA 4.0 unless indicated otherwise (Section 3); Mapillary or licensors own content; resale of Services, scraping, unblurring and real-time navigation banned (Section 5); blurring of faces and plates (Section 6); developer client_id, logo attribution, throttling (Section 11); commercial use for training and development of algorithms and datasets and services for clients, with anti-reidentification safeguards (Section 12); OSM and Overture use (Section 13); export controls (Section 22)

More than 3,000,000,000 street-level images; any camera, anywhere
Started 2013; joined Facebook (now Meta) in 2020; 190 countries; more than two billion contributed images

Acquired by Meta (Facebook) in June 2020; commercial use made free of charge after the acquisition
Third-party MCP wrapper io.github.pipeworx-io/mapillary; no first-party entry

cards.name: Mecka
cards.short: Robot-learning data to order: paid people record first-person video, motion and touch with Mecka's own sensor kit.

tasks: commission task-specific collection of human demonstrations in homes and commercial environments
egocentric (first-person) video of everyday tasks such as cooking, cleaning, making coffee or fixing cars
capture with Mecka-made multi-sensor kit: camera caps, a sensor hub and tactile gloves that record grip force
capture at recruited businesses (e.g. bakeries, a PCB manufacturing line)
post-processing into motion tracking, hand pose, 3D reconstruction and aligned sensor streams
dataset access, model evaluations and on-site robot deployments (not captures)

pricing.model: Quote after scoping
pricing.notes: No prices are published. Teams 'reach out and we'll scope the right entry point': dataset access, commissioned collection, evaluations or a full data program.

latency.typical: Not published
latency.notes: No turnaround is stated anywhere Mecka publishes. Mecka recruits contributors to fill gaps it tracks on a heat map of jobs, industries and diversity goals.

freshness.typical_age: Commissioned collection is recorded after scoping; dataset access is existing data
freshness.notes: Mecka also offers access to existing data, including its contributions to the EgoVerse dataset (4,003 hours of human demonstrations in the current release, per egoverse.ai). Only commissioned collection is new data.

coverage.notes: Mecka says it runs 'a global production operation, with capture fleets recording human demonstration in homes and commercial environments', and its CEO says anyone can sign up through the app 'from anywhere in the world'. No country list is published. Offices are in New York, Toronto and San Francisco; jobs are listed in the US and Canada only. The EgoVerse globe shows capture sites in the US, Canada, Switzerland, Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines, Kosovo, Colombia, Argentina and Kenya, but that map covers the whole multi-lab consortium, not Mecka alone.

licensing.summary: Mecka publishes no terms of service or data licence; its only legal page is a privacy policy (effective 20 Mar 2026, Carbon Based Technology Corporation, DBA Mecka AI), which covers personal data and 'dataset contributions' but not buyer rights. The CEO says Mecka will 'license a lot of the data' it creates and that its data is licensed to foundation-model companies; exclusivity, buyer ownership, AI-training rights and resale are not stated in any published terms. The open EgoVerse code is MIT-licensed; the dataset licence is not stated on egoverse.ai.

human.method: Participants are paid to demonstrate tasks; individuals sign up in the app and register their profession, and Mecka also recruits businesses.
human.unknown: How contributors are identified, vetted or consented is not published. Mecka has reported contributors submitting YouTube videos as their own recordings.

application.method: Mecka designs and manufactures its own multi-sensor capture hardware; its iOS app auto-starts recording when hands enter the frame and uploads to Mecka's infrastructure.
application.unknown: No device or app attestation is documented.

camera.method: Camera caps and external cameras on Mecka's own hardware, plus smartphones.
camera.unknown: No C2PA or signed capture; Mecka is not on the C2PA conforming products list. Uploaded footage has included screen-sourced fakes (YouTube videos), per the CEO.

time.method: Sensor streams are synchronised and aligned in post-processing.
time.unknown: Synchronisation aligns streams to each other; no signed or independently time-stamped capture time is documented.

location.unknown: No location proof is documented. Mecka says it must be present where collection happens, but publishes no method for proving where a capture was made.

content.method: Processing heuristics flag problems, escalation engines route them, and quality gates plus computer vision run in post-processing.
content.unknown: Acceptance criteria and QC results are not published; Mecka says quality standards still shift as it learns.

corroboration.unknown: No independent check of commissioned data is documented. EgoVerse replicated human-to-robot transfer across labs, which tests usefulness, not capture provenance.

auth.how_to_get: Contact Mecka through mecka.ai ('Request access' / 'Talk to us') for enterprise programs, research access and dataset partnerships. A partner console at partners.mecka.ai signs in by emailed link.

mcp.notes: No MCP server found; no Mecka server in the official MCP Registry (searched 'mecka' and 'egoverse', 2026-10-26).

api.notes: Mecka's 'Data Tools' web interface lets teams browse, visualise and query data and 'run inference APIs', but no API documentation is public and no endpoint to order or quote collection is published. No OAuth metadata is served: mecka.ai returns 404 for /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, and partners.mecka.ai redirects them to its sign-in page.

delivery.basis: Mecka says teams can 'commission task-specific collection' and that it will 'scope the right entry point', but publishes no turnaround.

payment.notes: No payment method is published. The privacy policy mentions 'payment and billing information when you purchase paid Services' without naming methods. Collection is scoped and priced through sales.

consent.unknown: Mecka publishes no consent terms for contributors or for bystanders and homes filmed; the privacy policy covers 'dataset contributions' only as personal data.

worker_pay.notes: Participants are paid; rates are not published. The CEO says contributor pay is 'not the largest factor' in end-to-end cost.

requester.unknown: Mecka publishes no check of who commissions collection or for what; every engagement starts with a conversation.

cards.summary: Mecka collects human-demonstration data for robot learning. Paid participants and recruited businesses record everyday and workplace tasks in homes and commercial settings, using Mecka's own capture hardware (camera caps, a sensor hub, tactile gloves) and an iOS app. Mecka then processes the recordings into motion tracking, hand pose and 3D reconstruction. Buyers (robotics labs, frontier model teams, enterprises) can get dataset access or commission task-specific collection, both through sales. Prices, turnaround and licence terms are not published.

cards.name: micro1
cards.short: Robotics training data to order: first-person video of everyday and trade tasks, recorded by vetted paid contractors.

tasks: first-person (POV) and third-person video of domain experts performing real-world tasks
household task demonstrations recorded at home with a head-mounted smartphone (cooking, laundry, organising, packing, using basic tools)
skilled-trade demonstrations on real job sites (electrical, plumbing, carpentry, vehicle maintenance, valve and fixture replacement)
expert environment datasets: repair, assembly, industrial workflows, logistics, field operations
synchronised stereo video, IMU and multi-camera capture
robot interaction data captured in micro1's controlled robotics deployment lab
post-capture structuring: action-level annotation, temporal segmentation, hand/object interactions, 2D/3D annotation, tracking, QC and evaluation

pricing.model: Quote after contact
pricing.notes: No buyer pricing is published; the robotics page has only a 'Get in touch' form. For scale only: contributors are paid per approved hour of recorded video (at-home recorder postings list $13-15/hour; a plumber posting lists $20-30/hour). That is labour cost, not a price.

latency.typical: Not published
latency.notes: No turnaround is stated. Contributors submit recordings on their own schedule and are paid biweekly for approved work; postings say start dates depend on shipping head-strap equipment.

freshness.typical_age: Recorded after a project is set up and contributors are onboarded
freshness.notes: MIT Technology Review reports micro1 says it holds tens of thousands of hours of footage; whether existing footage is also sold is not stated by micro1.

licensing.summary: No buyer-facing terms for robotics data are published; the Legal Center lists only website, cookie, candidate, contractor and referral terms. They do not cover data micro1 collects for a buyer. Contributor consent: per MIT Technology Review, workers know their footage trains robots but are not told which clients receive it.

location.unknown: No location proof is documented; recordings are made in contributors' homes or job sites.

content.method: Contributors follow written instructions (hands visible, natural speed); each video is reviewed by AI and a human and accepted or rejected; only approved recordings are paid; unsafe task performance is rejected.

cards.name: Amazon Mechanical Turk
cards.summary: CLOSED. Amazon's crowdsourcing marketplace for small paid online tasks (HITs), with an AWS API (CreateHIT, ListAssignmentsForHIT, and others via boto3). mturk.com states the service permanently closed on September 30, 2026; HIT creation and task completion ended that day. Before closure it was built for remote, browser-based work. Workers could be filtered by country or ISO 3166-2 subdivision through the Worker_Locale qualification, but no public source describes sending workers to a specific physical place or verifying where or when a photo was taken. Listed for the record only. An agent cannot use it.

tasks: online microtasks (HITs) built with QuestionForm, HTMLQuestion or ExternalQuestion
surveys and research studies
image and video labeling, classification and content screening (per Wikipedia)

file upload by workers: GetFileUploadURL returns a 60-second URL for a FileUploadAnswer, but AWS marked FileUploadAnswer pending deprecation on 2017-12-12 and recommended Amazon S3 instead. Self-reported photos were technically possible; no field-capture product was documented
no longer available: the service closed on 2026-09-30

pricing.model: worker reward set by the requester plus an Amazon commission (historical; the service is closed)
pricing.notes: The www.mturk.com pricing page now shows only the closure notice, but requester.mturk.com/pricing still serves the old fee table: a 20 percent fee on the worker reward and any bonus; an additional 20 percent on the reward for tasks with 10 or more assignments; a minimum fee of $0.01 per assignment or bonus payment; an extra 5 percent of the reward for the Masters qualification; and Premium Qualification fees of $0.05 to $1.00 per assignment. The 40 percent rate for 10+ assignments took effect on 2015-07-22 (SPSP). Wikipedia gives one cent as the minimum task payment. The pricing is moot since the closure.

latency.typical: n/a, service closed
latency.notes: Requesters set HIT lifetime (LifetimeInSeconds) and per-assignment time limit (AssignmentDurationInSeconds). No typical fill time was published. HIT submission ended on 2026-09-30, and unsubmitted HITs expired automatically.

regions: Historically mostly United States, then India (per Wikipedia)
coverage.notes: Wikipedia puts the workforce at about 80 percent US in May 2015, about 60 percent US with about 30 percent of the total in India in May 2019, and about 90 percent US in early 2023. The Worker_Locale qualification could restrict a HIT to ISO 3166 countries or ISO 3166-2 subdivisions such as US-WA. That was a worker-profile attribute, not proof of physical presence. No city-level targeting was documented, and Amazon published no list of covered countries.

licensing.summary: Under the Participation Agreement (last updated 2020-03-25, still shown on mturk.com), work product from Tasks is a work made for hire for the Requester, ownership vests in the Requester, and Workers waive moral rights (s. 3.3). Section 3.7 says task content Requesters upload and work product they receive may be retained and used to improve the Site and other machine learning related products and services of Amazon or its affiliates. The agreement does not mention resale of work product or AI training by requesters, so those keys are omitted. The Acceptable Use Policy prohibited collecting or deriving workers' personally identifiable information, posting third parties' personal information, and HITs requiring registration elsewhere. It does not address physical-location or photo tasks.

human.method: Workers registered with accurate information. Amazon reserved the right to require additional information to verify a worker's identity or ACH-enabled bank account (Participation Agreement sections 1.1 and 4.3.2). Workers agreed not to use robots, scripts or other automated methods (s. 3.2).
human.unknown: The actual identity-check process, including any ID document or selfie check, is not publicly documented. Bots and shared accounts were widely reported in research literature but not assessed here.

application.unknown: Tasks ran in a browser (HTML or external pages). No controlled capture app or attestation was documented.

camera.unknown: No method for confirming that uploaded media came from a live camera rather than an existing file.

time.unknown: Assignments had platform accept and submit timestamps, but capture time of any uploaded media was not verified.

location.method: The Worker_Locale qualification filters on the country or subdivision in the worker's profile.
location.unknown: How the locale was established (self-reported, tax address, IP) is not documented on the pages read. Nothing verifies a worker's presence at a place.

content.unknown: Requesters approved or rejected work themselves, and review policies existed in the API (ListReviewPolicyResultsForHIT). No platform check for fabricated or AI-generated media was documented.

corroboration.unknown: Requesters could request multiple assignments per HIT and compare answers themselves. The platform offered no documented cross-check against independent sources.

freshness.typical_age: n/a, service closed
freshness.notes: Historically, work was performed after a HIT was posted. The service closed on 2026-09-30. Requesters can approve or reject pending HITs (otherwise auto-approved) and send bonuses until 2026-10-30, a balance refund is expected within 30 days of closure, and transaction history stays available until 2027-01-28.

auth.how_to_get: Historically, an AWS account linked to an MTurk Requester account, signing requests with SigV4 (botocore service model: signatureVersion v4). New customers were stopped on 2026-07-30, and the service closed on 2026-09-30. The sandbox host was mturk-requester-sandbox.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. The env-var name is standard AWS SDK behaviour, not stated on the MTurk pages read.

endpoints.params: Title, Description, Reward (string), MaxAssignments, LifetimeInSeconds, AssignmentDurationInSeconds, Question (QuestionForm/HTMLQuestion/ExternalQuestion XML up to 65,535 bytes) or HITLayoutId, QualificationRequirements (0 to 10; Worker_Locale with LocaleValues Country/Subdivision, comparators EqualTo, NotEqualTo (one value), In, NotIn (up to 30 values))
endpoints.notes: AWS JSON 1.1 protocol: POST to the endpoint with X-Amz-Target MTurkRequesterServiceV20170117.CreateHIT. Non-functional since 2026-09-30.

endpoints.params: HITId, AssignmentStatuses, pagination
endpoints.notes: Returns worker submissions. Non-functional since closure.

endpoints.params: HITId
endpoints.notes: Non-functional since closure.

endpoints.params: AssignmentId, QuestionIdentifier
endpoints.notes: Returns a temporary URL, valid 60 seconds, for a file a Worker uploaded as a FileUploadAnswer; files are deleted when the HIT is disposed. Marked pending deprecation since 2017-12-12. Non-functional since closure.

endpoints.notes: Non-functional since closure.

api.sdk: boto3 client('mturk'); other AWS SDKs
api.rate_limits: Not published on the pages read.

mcp.notes: No server found in the official MCP Registry (searches for mturk and mechanical-turk on 2026-10-26 returned no MTurk server).

api.notes: The endpoint host still answers (an unsigned request returns MissingAuthenticationTokenException), but mturk.com states the service closed on 2026-09-30. No OAuth metadata is served at www.mturk.com/.well-known/. The boto3 reference pages carry no closure notice.

sources.claim: Home page: 'Mechanical Turk is no longer available. Amazon Mechanical Turk permanently closed on September 30, 2026.'

Closure FAQ: HIT submission closed 2026-09-30; unsubmitted HITs expired; requesters may approve/reject (else auto-approved) and award bonuses until 2026-10-30; balance refund within 30 days; transaction history until 2027-01-28; the MTurk worker type no longer available in SageMaker Ground Truth and Amazon A2I
www.mturk.com pricing page now shows only the closure notice

Requester pricing page (still served, with banner 'All HIT creation and task completion will end on this date'): 20 percent fee on reward and bonus, additional 20 percent for tasks with 10+ assignments, $0.01 minimum fee, 5 percent Masters fee, Premium Qualification fees $0.05 to $1.00 per assignment; reward chosen by the requester
Commission rose from 10 to 20 percent, and 40 percent for 10+ assignments, effective 2015-07-22

New customers stopped on 2026-07-30 (announced 2026-07-05); full closure announced 2026-08-25 for 2026-09-30; worker share about 80 percent US (2015), about 60 percent US / 30 percent India (2019), about 90 percent US (early 2023); image and video task examples; one-cent minimum task payment
Shutdown reporting: closure on 2026-09-30, no specific reason given, new-customer sign-ups halted the month before

Participation Agreement (last updated 2020-03-25): work made for hire for the Requester (s. 3.3); task content and work product may be retained and used for machine learning related products (s. 3.7); identity verification (s. 1.1, 4.3.2); workers may not use robots or scripts (s. 3.2); Prepaid Task Credits and AWS-invoiced tasks; sanctions representation (s. 5); no rejection without good cause

Acceptable Use Policy: prohibits collecting or deriving worker PII, third-party personal info in HITs, HITs requiring registration elsewhere, bots completing HITs, scraping; does not address physical-location or photo tasks
boto3 MTurk client and its 43 methods (create_hit, list_assignments_for_hit, get_hit, list_hits, get_file_upload_url, list_review_policy_results_for_hit, and others); no closure notice

create_hit parameters; 10+ MaxAssignments carry an additional fee; Question up to 65,535 bytes; 0 to 10 QualificationRequirements; Worker_Locale LocaleValues using ISO 3166 / 3166-2 with EqualTo, NotEqualTo, In, NotIn (up to 30 values)
get_file_upload_url: AssignmentId and QuestionIdentifier; URL valid 60 seconds; FileUploadAnswer pending deprecation 2017-12-12, S3 recommended
Endpoint data: mturk-requester in us-east-1 only, sandbox host mturk-requester-sandbox.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
Service model: apiVersion 2017-01-17, JSON 1.1 protocol, SigV4, targetPrefix MTurkRequesterServiceV20170117
Old AWSMturkAPI reference pages now return 404
Official MCP Registry search for mturk: no MTurk server

delivery.basis: Service closed 2026-09-30.

cards.short: Amazon's crowd-task marketplace (closed 30 September 2026).

payment.notes: Historical. The Participation Agreement lets Requesters prepay (Prepaid Task Credits on their Amazon account balance) or be invoiced by AWS for Invoiced Tasks. Prepaying was optional. After closure, requesters get a balance refund within 30 days and a final bill.

requester.checks: Requesters accepted the Participation Agreement, represented that neither they nor their financial institutions were under sanctions (s. 5), needed an AWS account for invoiced tasks, and had to follow the Acceptable Use Policy (no collecting worker PII, no third-party personal information in HITs).
requester.unknown: No documented review of HIT content before posting, and no check on what a HIT asks a worker to photograph or where.

cards.name: Mundane
cards.summary: Agent-to-human marketplace ("v0.1 prototype", terms v0.2, early access) run by Mundane, Inc. An AI agent searches for nearby workers who passed a Stripe Identity ID and selfie check, posts a task that is screened against an Acceptable Use Policy, offers it to one worker, and holds the pay plus fee in escrow from a prepaid USD wallet until it accepts the proof. Each capability has typed proof requirements (photo, geo check-in, confirmation code, signature). Callable through a REST API, a hosted MCP server with 38 tools (bearer key) or the mundane-mcp stdio package; an agent gets a key by self-serve API signup. Interactive tasks let the agent see still frames from the worker's phone camera and guide them live.
cards.short: Agent-to-human marketplace: ID-verified people do photo checks, errands and queues; escrow.

tasks: photo documentation: visit a location and take photos meeting stated criteria (photo, geo check-in by default)
in-person errand: pickup, drop-off, brief in-person interaction (photo, confirmation code, geo check-in)
delivery pickup: pick up an item and deliver it to a named recipient (photo, geo check-in, signature)
wait in line and obtain a stamped or signed token (photo, confirmation code)
check something in person: is it open, is it in stock, what does the notice say
interactive task: still frames from the worker's phone camera while the agent guides them live
chained jobs: 2-5 workers in turn with an item handed on at each step
skilled trade work listed by workers

pricing.model: worker's own ask rate per task, plus a platform fee of the lesser of 5% of the worker amount or $5.00
pricing.unit: task (price set by the worker's ask rate and the agent's offer)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 because there is no published price: each worker sets a per-task ask rate and an offer must be at or above it (interactive tasks: at least the worker's interactive rate). The platform fee is added on top and disclosed in the offer response. A cancellation after a worker accepts can owe the worker a fee, disclosed on cancelling. Searching for workers is free (needs a key, no funded wallet). In disputes Mundane keeps the platform fee. USD only.

latency.typical: Not stated; set by the task deadline and whether a nearby worker accepts the offer
latency.notes: The provider says of offers to workers: "Not yet, in most places. Mundane is new", and the Terms guarantee no minimum number of offers. Offers expire after 24 hours by default (minimum 5 minutes). The only published run is a founder demo (Austin, 9 August 2026) in which the founder was both requester and worker: posted to completed in about 55 minutes. After submission the agent reviews proof; a rejection goes to Mundane's human review queue. Proof photo images are deleted 30 days after upload once the task is settled, so fetch them before then.

coverage.notes: Workers can sign up in the US, UK, Canada, Switzerland and the EEA ("the places where Stripe can both verify ID and pay out"). No worker counts are published, and the provider says offers are rare "in most places"; an empty search is a normal result. The EEA is expanded in areas to its 30 member countries.

licensing.summary: Terms (v0.2): users keep any ownership they have in submitted content, including worker proof, and grant Mundane a nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence to host, copy, process and display it "only as reasonably needed to provide, secure, support, and improve the service and comply with law". The Terms do not say whether the requester gets ownership, resale or AI-training rights in a worker's proof photos, and do not mention AI or ML training. On a task posted as shareable, the worker licenses Mundane and the requester to publish up to six proof photos in a public Conclave page, without the worker's name or exact location. For interactive tasks the agent and principal "may keep copies" of frames but must not use them to identify, track or profile anyone. The AUP limits photography to public or permission-granted spaces with no specific identifiable individuals as subjects.

human.method: Every worker passes Stripe Identity (government-ID document check plus liveness-matched selfie) and an 18+ age check before accepting a paid task; a keyed one-way value from verified name and date of birth flags duplicate or ban-evasion accounts for human review
human.unknown: The check binds an account to a verified person, not a task: nothing documented shows the verified person is the one who did the work. The provider says verification "is not a guarantee of a person's qualifications, reliability, or conduct". No public proof per worker or task.

application.unknown: Workers use a web app; no app or device attestation is documented, and whether proof photos must be taken in-app rather than uploaded from the gallery is not stated

camera.method: Interactive tasks only: the agent receives still frames from the worker's phone camera while the worker is live (never video), on a cadence it sets or on demand
camera.unknown: Opt-in per task and per worker. Ordinary proof photos are uploads; no live-capture requirement is documented for them. Frames and proof photos are re-encoded without camera metadata. Whether a virtual camera or a photographed screen would be detected is not addressed.

time.method: The server records task events (worker accepted, chat message, completion submitted) in an event feed, and the task record shows when proof was submitted; interactive frames arrive while the worker is live
time.unknown: Capture time of uploaded proof photos is not documented, and their camera metadata is stripped on upload; timestamps are not signed

location.method: Typed proof: geo_checkin is an unwaivable floor for in-person errands and delivery pickups and a default (waivable) for photo documentation; optional request_live_location shares the worker's live position during the task's active window only
location.unknown: How a geo check-in is taken, what radius passes, and resistance to GPS spoofing are not documented. Proof photos are re-encoded without location metadata, so the photo itself carries no location. Live location stops before proof submission.

content.method: The requesting agent (and its person) reviews the typed proof (photos, confirmation codes, signatures) and can accept, request changes or reject; a rejection goes to Mundane's human review, which decides release, refund or split
content.unknown: Mundane screens the task, not the proof; nothing documented checks that a photo shows what it claims before the requester reviews it. In the published demo the agent, not the platform, caught a count mismatch.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check is offered; a requester could post the same task to several workers, but that is buyer-side

auth.how_to_get: Headless: POST https://api.mundane.market/v1/agents/signup with principal_display_name, principal_email, agent_name, accept_aup_version (aup-v0.2) and accept_tos_version (tos-v0.2) returns a mundane_agent_ key once, with conservative spend caps. The same key works as Authorization: Bearer on the REST API and the hosted MCP endpoint.

MCP at https://api.mundane.market/chatgpt/mcp for directory connections (ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code): authorization code with PKCE S256, public clients (token auth none), clients identified by a Client ID Metadata Document (client_id_metadata_document_supported: true); no RFC 7591 registration endpoint is advertised. The principal signs in to Mundane and approves the connection. This connection leaves out interactive tasks, chained jobs and Conclaves.

endpoints.params: lat, lng, radius_km, capability, skill, min_rating, min_rating_count, max_rate_minor, available_at, live_now, chain_ok, interactive_ok, limit
endpoints.notes: Verified workers near a point, with handle, capabilities, ask rate, rating, completed-task count and a distance from a ~2 km grid cell. Needs a key, no funded wallet; [] is a normal result. POST /workers/skill-search finds workers by skill anywhere (areas only).
Public, no key: each capability slug with required and default proof types and minimum worker age. GET /capabilities (key) lists what this agent may dispatch.

endpoints.params: total_minor, new_task
endpoints.notes: Read-only: whether an offer of total_minor would be refused right now (balance, caps) and every reason why. The platform fee is disclosed in the offer response; GET /spend-status returns balance and remaining caps.

endpoints.params: title, instructions, location {address, lat, lng}, required_capabilities, budget_max_minor, currency, deadline, proof_requirements, proof_requirement_opt_outs, constraints, request_live_location, interactive, conclave_shareable, idempotency_key
endpoints.notes: Runs the screening cascade; returns open, screening (human review) or rejected (final). Then POST /offers {task_id, worker_id, amount_minor, currency, expires_in_seconds, message, idempotency_key} holds worker amount plus fee in escrow.

endpoints.params: wait_for_change
endpoints.notes: Lifecycle state, active offer, assigned worker and completion proof. GET /task-events?since_id returns events across all tasks.
Signed, short-lived links to the task's proof photos (owner only). POST /tasks/{task_id}/review {decision: accept|reject|request_changes} releases or disputes the escrow.

api.sdk: mundane-mcp 0.1.21 (PyPI, Apache-2.0; also ghcr.io/sttruji/mundane-mcp); Claude Code and Codex plugin from github.com/sttruji/mundane-mcp; OpenAPI "Mundane API 0.1.0"
api.rate_limits: Default caps assigned at signup: $100 per task, $200 per day, $750 per week, $2,000 per month, 5 open tasks, 10 offers per hour; no self-serve increase over the API (console increases need email confirmation). Hosted agent: $25 per task, $100 per day.

mcp.notes: Streamable HTTP with the agent API key as a bearer token; 38 tools (post_task, search_workers, make_offer, await_task_update, get_task_proof, interactive and chain tools). The MCP Registry entry (v0.1.21, active) lists the remote plus PyPI and OCI stdio packages. A separate OAuth endpoint, /chatgpt/mcp, serves directory connections.

api.notes: The OpenAPI document still exposes /v1/mock/... endpoints (identity, Connect onboarding, checkout). Mundane's agent skill says money moves only with the user's approval and releasing payment always needs the user. The Terms treat an agent's requests as its principal's.

payment.notes: Tasks are paid from a prepaid USD wallet: making an offer holds the worker amount plus fee. The agent can create a top-up (POST /v1/wallet/topup, up to $100,000 per call) that returns a Stripe Checkout link a person opens and pays; the agent then spends the balance within its caps. Wallet credit is not cashable and refunds go back to the wallet, not the card.

worker_pay.model: worker sets a per-task ask rate (and an interactive rate); the agent's offer must be at or above it; the fee is added on top, not taken from pay
worker_pay.notes: Rates are visible to agents in search results, not published publicly. Pay is held before the worker starts and paid out through Stripe Connect when the proof is approved.

consent.method: AUP: photography only in public or permission-granted spaces, no specific identifiable individuals as subjects, no interiors of private property; tasks at a private residence need the occupant's consent; workers agree before accepting to shareable or interactive tasks
consent.unknown: Bystanders in proof photos or interactive frames are not asked; the provider notes frames "can show other people"

requester.checks: Principals give a name and email at API signup and accept the current AUP and Terms versions (recorded in an audit trail); each agent key carries spend caps set by Mundane. Every task passes a screening cascade (policy regex, task-shape match, an LLM classifier, human review when needed) before any worker sees it. The AUP bans following, tracking, monitoring, photographing or locating a specific individual, and rejections are final.
requester.unknown: No identity verification of principals is documented beyond email, and the Terms say automated screening is "not a guarantee that an approved task is lawful or safe"

freshness.typical_age: Captured after a worker accepts the offer, by the deadline you set
freshness.notes: No archive. Proof photo images are deleted 30 days after upload once the task is settled.

delivery.basis: Provider, on whether workers get offers: "Not yet, in most places. Mundane is new"; the Terms: "Mundane does not guarantee any minimum number of offers or hours"

sources.claim: Agent-to-human marketplace; ID- and age-verified workers; every task screened against the AUP; escrow released on approved proof; search needs a key but no funded wallet; hosted MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP, bearer key), pip install mundane-mcp; hosted agent

Terms v0.2 (last updated October 20, 2026): principals and agents; agent actions treated as the principal's; agent signup via POST /v1/agents/signup; connected apps (ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code); no minimum offers; chained and interactive tasks; USD-only wallet via Stripe Checkout; escrow hold; platform fee lesser of 5% or $5; cancellation fee; disputes to human review with fee retained; Stripe Identity ID and liveness check; content licence; Conclave shareable photos; screening not a guarantee; Mundane, Inc., Delaware

AUP v0.2: ban on following, tracking, monitoring, photographing or locating a specific individual; photography only in public or permission-granted spaces with no identifiable individuals as subjects; residence tasks need occupant consent; interactive-task rules; screening cascade; principal must give accurate identity

Privacy Notice (last updated October 22, 2026): proof photos and interactive frames re-encoded without camera metadata including location; frames are still photos from the phone camera, never video; worker search uses a ~2 km grid cell; proof photos deleted 30 days after upload once settled; directory connection leaves out interactive tasks, chains and Conclaves; LLM screening via Anthropic
Worker coverage: US, UK, Canada, Switzerland and the EEA; Stripe ID and selfie check, 18+; workers set their own rate; fee added on top; 'Will I get a lot of offers? Not yet, in most places'
Coverage is where Stripe can both verify ID and pay out; fee 5% capped at $5; searching free; workers pass Stripe Identity

Capabilities and typed proof: photo_documentation (photo; geo_checkin default), in_person_errand (photo, confirmation_code, geo_checkin), delivery_pickup (photo, geo_checkin, signature), wait_in_line (photo, confirmation_code); min worker age 18

OpenAPI 'Mundane API 0.1.0': /v1/workers, /v1/tasks, /v1/offers, /v1/offer-check, /v1/spend-status, /v1/task-events, /v1/tasks/{id}/proof-media, /v1/tasks/{id}/review, /v1/wallet/topup (max 10,000,000 minor units), live-location, interactive and chain endpoints, /v1/mock/... endpoints
REST API docs (Swagger UI over /openapi.json)

Connect your agent: self-serve signup command (aup-v0.2, tos-v0.2), key shown once, conservative caps, hosted MCP URL, MCP Registry name market.mundane/mundane, free search, top-up via Stripe Checkout, cap increases need email confirmation
Hosted agent starts capped at $25 per task and $100 per day

Founder demo, 9 August 2026, Austin: founder as requester and worker, $1.00 offer plus $0.05 fee, photo plus location check-in, agent flagged a count mismatch, completed about 55 minutes after posting

MCP adapter README: 38 tools; default caps per_task_max $100, daily $200, weekly $750, monthly $2,000, 5 open tasks, 10 offers per hour; no self-serve cap increase; task event feed; get_task_proof; Apache-2.0

post_task screening cascade (policy_gate regex, shape match, Claude LLM classifier, human review); proof requirements are capability floor plus defaults plus extras; geo_checkin floor not waivable on errands; live location only during the active window
Agent skill: money moves only with the user's approval; releasing payment always needs the user; the user pays the Checkout link
MCP Registry: market.mundane/mundane v0.1.21 (active, latest, published 2026-10-14), remote streamable-http https://api.mundane.market/mcp with Authorization header, PyPI and OCI stdio packages
mundane-mcp 0.1.21 on PyPI, Apache-2.0

OAuth authorization server: issuer https://api.mundane.market, authorization code, PKCE S256, token auth none, client_id_metadata_document_supported, scopes tasks:read and tasks:write; no registration endpoint
Protected resource https://api.mundane.market/chatgpt/mcp, scopes tasks:read and tasks:write, bearer in header

cards.name: NASA FIRMS active fires
cards.summary: NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) publishes active fire and thermal hotspot detections from the MODIS, VIIRS and Landsat satellite sensors, globally within about 3 hours of an overpass and faster (real-time / ultra real-time) over the US and Canada. Global and regional CSV, KML and shapefile files of the last 24 hours, 48 hours and 7 days download with no key; a free MAP_KEY unlocks an area API returning CSV detections for any bounding box over 1-5 days.

tasks: active fire hotspot detections in a bounding box (or the world) for the last 1-5 days
keyless global or regional CSV/KML/shapefile of detections from the last 24 hours, 48 hours or 7 days
VIIRS (S-NPP until Nov. 2, 2026, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) and MODIS near-real-time fire detections
Landsat fire detections over the US and Canada
per-detection fields such as brightness, scan/track pixel size, confidence, fire radiative power, acquisition date and time, satellite, day/night

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: Free. The 24h/48h/7d files need no key; the area API needs a free MAP_KEY requested with an email address.

latency.typical: Within 3 hours of overpass globally (best effort); within 30 minutes (real-time) or within about a minute to 5 minutes (ultra real-time) over the US and Canada; Landsat 30-60 minutes (US and Canada)
latency.notes: From the FIRMS FAQ and area API page. The FAQ gives both 'within a minute' and 'within 5 minutes' for ultra real-time; the API page says under 60 seconds 'for much of the US and Canada'. RT/URT detections are replaced by NRT ones once processed, or after 6 hours. The keyless 24h/48h/7d files are refreshed every 60 minutes; web services use the most recently processed data. Detections exist only when a satellite passes over, generally about twice a day per sensor (more towards the poles). Suomi NPP data delivery ceases on Nov. 2, 2026.

coverage.notes: Worldwide for MODIS and VIIRS; Landsat and the faster real-time products cover the US and Canada only. Cloud and smoke can hide fires; small or short fires between overpasses can be missed.

licensing.summary: No FIRMS-specific licence. NASA ESDIS data-use guidance: data from NASA-led missions are CC0 unless marked otherwise, while non-NASA data follow their sponsor's licence; NASA asks to be acknowledged ('NASA FIRMS') and must not be implied to endorse a product. LANCE data are provided 'as is'. AI training and resale are not mentioned.

freshness.typical_age: Minutes to about 3 hours after the latest overpass
freshness.notes: The API also serves standard-processing (SP) data for past dates; irlpls lists FIRMS for its near-real-time detections.

auth.how_to_get: The 24h/48h/7d CSV, KML and shapefile files under /data/active_fire/ download without a key.
Sign up for a free MAP_KEY with an email address at https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/map_key/; the key is emailed and goes in the URL path.

endpoints.params: SOURCE: VIIRS_SNPP_NRT, VIIRS_NOAA20_NRT, VIIRS_NOAA21_NRT, MODIS_NRT, LANDSAT_NRT (US/Canada), or *_SP for standard processing; AREA_COORDINATES: west,south,east,north or world; DAY_RANGE 1-5
endpoints.notes: Most recent detections from today back DAY_RANGE-1 days. A /{DATE} suffix returns DATE to DATE+DAY_RANGE-1 instead. An invalid key returns HTTP 400 'Invalid MAP_KEY.'

endpoints.params: e.g. /data/active_fire/noaa-20-viirs-c2/csv/J1_VIIRS_C2_Global_24h.csv, /data/active_fire/noaa-21-viirs-c2/csv/J2_VIIRS_C2_Global_24h.csv, /data/active_fire/modis-c6.1/csv/MODIS_C6_1_Global_24h.csv; regions include Global, USA_contiguous_and_Hawaii, Canada, Europe, South_America and others
endpoints.notes: No key. Refreshed every 60 minutes. KML and shapefile versions exist alongside.

cards.name: NATIX Network
cards.summary: Crowdsourced multi-camera (4-6 camera) driving video from Tesla owners who plug in NATIX's VX360 device, sold to Physical AI and autonomous-driving teams as raw footage with GPS, IMU and vehicle telemetry, VLM- and telemetry-mined edge cases, OpenSCENARIO/OpenDRIVE scenarios and map features. cards.name: NOAA NDBC buoys
cards.summary: NOAA's National Data Buoy Center publishes real-time observations from moored offshore buoys, coastal C-MAN stations and partner stations (wind speed, direction and gust, significant wave height and period, air and sea temperature, pressure) as plain-text files over HTTPS, free and with no key. Most stations report hourly; the real-time directory holds the last 45 days. About 90 buoys also carry BuoyCAMs that take daylight photos of the sea surface.

tasks: latest offshore buoy observation: wind speed, direction and gust
significant wave height, dominant and average wave period, mean wave direction
air temperature, sea surface temperature, dew point, pressure and pressure tendency
spectral wave summaries (.spec) for buoys; oceanographic, current (ADCP), continuous-wind, solar radiation, rain and DART files where a station has them
latest observation from every reporting station in one file (latest_obs.txt, with coordinates)
latest BuoyCAM photo from a buoy (panoramic JPEG, daylight hours, UTC time stamped on the image)
last 45 days of real-time history per station

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: No fee and no key. NDBC asks users to 'limit your retrievals to a minimal level'.

latency.typical: Most stations report hourly, with most data available by about 25 minutes after the hour
latency.notes: From the NDBC real-time data access FAQ. Some stations report more often (46026 reports every 10 minutes); check the station page for its interval. A fetch at about 04:59 UTC on 2026-10-27 (2026-10-26 US time) returned a 46026 row stamped 04:30 UTC. The BuoyCAM map refreshes every 15 minutes; BuoyCAM images seen were stamped 04:10 UTC.

regions: United States coastal and offshore waters, including the Great Lakes, Gulf of Mexico, Atlantic, Pacific, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam and American Samoa
Partner stations relayed by NDBC: Canada, UK and Irish/French shelf waters, Korea, and tropical moored arrays in the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans

Data from partner stations are the partners'. Not every station reports every variable (MM marks missing values), and buoys can go adrift or offline. BuoyCAMs: 90 stations listed, 75 with a current image.

licensing.summary: NDBC's footer 'Disclaimer' link goes to the NWS disclaimer, which says information on NWS web pages is in the public domain unless specifically noted otherwise and may be used without charge for any lawful purpose, so long as you do not claim it as your own, imply NOAA/NWS endorsement, or modify it and present it as official. Third-party information is used under licence from its provider; partner-station data (e.g. Canada, UK, Korea) may carry the partner's terms. The terms do not mention AI training or resale.

cards.name: NOAA tide and current stations
cards.summary: NOAA's Center for Operational Oceanographic Products and Services (CO-OPS) runs fixed coastal, Great Lakes and Pacific-island stations reporting 6-minute water levels plus, at many sites, wind, air/water temperature, pressure, visibility and real-time currents (PORTS). A free, keyless Data Retrieval API returns the latest reading per station; a Metadata API lists stations with coordinates, sensor status and nearby stations so an agent can find the closest one.

tasks: latest observed water level at a coastal or Great Lakes station (6-minute interval, relative to a chosen datum such as MLLW)
wind speed, direction and gust
air temperature, water temperature, air pressure, humidity, visibility, conductivity, salinity (where the station has the sensor)
observed currents at real-time PORTS current-meter stations
air gap (clearance between a bridge and the water surface) at air-gap stations
1-minute water level at a subset of stations
last 72 hours of preliminary data (date=recent)
find stations by type (waterlevels, met, currents, watertemp, 1minute, airgap, visibility, ...) with lat/lng, or stations near a given station within a radius

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: No fee, no account and no API key appear in the documented parameters. Keyless calls returned live data on 2026-10-25 and again on 2026-10-26.

latency.typical: Minutes: date=latest returns the last data point available within the last 18 minutes
latency.notes: Live tests on 2026-10-26 (04:59 UTC on 27 Oct): San Francisco (9414290) water level and wind were timestamped 04:54 UTC (5 minutes old); Kwajalein, Bermuda, Midway and San Juan were timestamped 04:48 UTC (11 minutes old). A 2004 CO-OPS technical report says routine transmission is every six minutes for some stations, every hour for others and every three hours for others, relayed via GOES satellite, so lag can vary by station.

regions: United States coasts (Atlantic, Gulf, Pacific, Alaska, Hawaii)
Puerto Rico and US Virgin Islands
US Pacific territories and possessions (American Samoa, Guam, Midway, Wake)
coverage.notes: Fixed stations only; you cannot request a new one. A live Metadata API call on 2026-10-26 listed 302 stations of type waterlevels (most in TX, MI, AK, FL, CA, NY, WA, LA, PR), 314 of type met, 257 of type 1minute and 85 of type currents (all at PORTS harbors). Non-state stations: Apra Harbor and Pago Bay (Guam), Pago Pago (American Samoa), Midway, Wake, Kwajalein (Marshall Islands), four in the US Virgin Islands and two in Bermuda; Guam, American Samoa, Midway, Wake, Kwajalein, Bermuda and Virgin Islands stations all returned same-day water levels on 2026-10-26. Not every product exists at every station, and sensors go offline: water_temperature at San Francisco 9414290 returned 'No data was found', and its sensors resource marks that sensor status 0 with 'Suspect Data - Data failed to meet QC standards - under review.'

licensing.summary: Per the Tides & Currents disclaimer, information on government servers is in the public domain unless specifically annotated otherwise and may be used freely by the public. It must not be modified in content and then presented as official government material, and NOS requests attribution when its material is reproduced and re-disseminated. Raw (preliminary) data have not passed NOS quality control or quality assurance and are to be used with appropriate caution. Data are provided as-is; the user assumes the entire risk and NOS disclaims liability. The terms do not mention AI training or resale.

freshness.typical_age: Typically minutes for the latest preliminary point; verified data after the following month; history back years
freshness.notes: date=latest (last point within 18 min), date=recent (72 h) and date=today apply only to preliminary water level, meteorological data and predictions. Water level responses carry q = 'p' (preliminary) or 'v' (verified). The API docs say water level data are verified monthly for the past month (January data verified in February), with no fixed date per station. Per-request length limits: 1-minute data 4 days, 6-minute data 1 month, hourly and high/low 1 year.

delivery.basis: API docs: date=latest retrieves the last data point available within the last 18 minutes; a live test on 2026-10-26 returned a 5-minute-old reading.

auth.how_to_get: No key. Docs ask callers to pass application=<your org or app name> so CO-OPS can find your queries in its logs (not required).

endpoints.params: type (waterlevels, met, waterlevelsandmet, currents, watertemp, 1minute, airgap, visibility, ...); expand (details, sensors, products, datums, floodlevels, ...); units
endpoints.notes: Returns count and stations[] with id, name, lat, lng, state, timezone, tidal, greatlakes, affiliations (currents stations carry project, e.g. 'Boston Harbor PORTS'). No bbox filter on the list; filter by distance client-side. Per-station resources at /mdapi/prod/webapi/stations/{id}/details.json, sensors.json (status and outage messages), datums.json, floodlevels.json.

endpoints.params: radius (nautical miles; default 2)
endpoints.notes: Stations near a known station, with stationType and distance.

endpoints.params: station (7-char ID, e.g. 9414290, or a currents ID like cb0102); product=water_level; date=latest|recent|today or begin_date/end_date/range; datum (mandatory for water level, e.g. MLLW, MSL, STND); units=metric|english; time_zone=gmt|lst|lst_ldt; format=json|xml|csv; application=irlpls
endpoints.notes: Live response: {metadata:{id,name,lat,lon}, data:[{t,v,s,f,q}]} where v = height, s = sigma of 1-second samples, f = flags O,F,R,L (outlier count, flat, rate-of-change, min/max limit), q = p preliminary / v verified. Missing product returns {error:{message}}.

endpoints.params: same as above with product=wind | air_temperature | water_temperature | air_pressure | humidity | visibility | conductivity | salinity | air_gap | currents (bin needed at non-PORTS stations) | one_minute_water_level
endpoints.notes: Wind returns t, s (speed), d (degrees), dr (text direction), g (gust), f (X max speed exceeded, R rate of change). Also available but not observations: predictions and currents_predictions (tide/current forecasts) and ofs_water_level (model nowcast/forecast guidance).

api.rate_limits: No numbers published. Docs say CO-OPS throttles heavy volume from a single customer and recommends sleep statements between successive calls and downloading only the data needed. Per-request length limits apply (e.g. 1 month of 6-minute data). A keyless response on 2026-10-26 carried no rate-limit headers.

mcp.community: No NOAA-run MCP server in the official MCP Registry. Third-party servers wrapping this API are listed, e.g. io.github.RyanCardin15/noaa-tides-and-currents-mcp, io.github.pipeworx-io/noaa-tides, io.github.cyanheads/noaa-marine-mcp-server, io.github.mrfentmen/tides-mcp.

human.unknown: Not applicable: readings come from automated government-operated instruments, not individual contributors

application.unknown: No documented signing or attestation of data from station to API; integrity rests on NOAA operating the network over HTTPS

camera.unknown: Not applicable; no imagery is collected

time.method: Each value has an observation timestamp (t). CO-OPS sensor specifications say each water level value is the average of 181 one-second samples centered on each tenth of an hour, and wind speed and direction are 2-minute averages collected before each tenth of an hour.
time.unknown: How station clocks are set or checked was not found in the documents read; nothing is signed or time-stamped by a third party.

location.method: Fixed stations with published lat/lng in the Metadata API and in each data response; stations also publish surveyed benchmarks through the benchmarks resource.
location.unknown: Coordinates are agency-entered; their positional accuracy was not reviewed.

content.method: Every preliminary water level value carries automated QC flags (outlier count, flat, rate-of-change and min/max tolerance) and a preliminary/verified level; verified data are reviewed monthly and may be marked inferred. CO-OPS specifies estimated accuracy of ±0.02 m per individual water level measurement relative to datum, and a three-standard-deviation outlier rejection test in each 6-minute average. Sensor outages and suspect data are reported per station in the sensors resource.
content.unknown: The flags and accuracy figures are NOAA's own statements, not independently checkable per value. The latest (preliminary) values have not passed NOS QC/QA per the disclaimer, and the full verification procedure was not read.

corroboration.unknown: No cross-check between stations or independent instruments is documented in the API; sigma (s) gives within-sample spread only, and monthly verification is NOAA's own review.

Response fields t, v, s, f, q; q p = preliminary, v = verified; preliminary flags O,F,R,L and verified flags I,F,R,T; wind fields s, d, dr, g and flags X, R

Metadata API stations endpoint, type values (waterlevels, met, currents, watertemp, 1minute, airgap, visibility, ...), expand options, details/sensors/datums/benchmarks resources, nearby resource with radius in nautical miles (default 2)

Public domain unless annotated, may be used freely; not to be modified and presented as official; attribution requested; raw data not QC'd, use with caution; as-is, user assumes risk, no NOS liability; no mention of AI training or resale

2004 technical report: NWLON data relayed via GOES satellite in near real time; routine transmission every six minutes for some stations, hourly for others, every three hours for others

cards.name: NWS weather stations (NOAA)
cards.summary: Free, keyless US government API (api.weather.gov) that serves live surface observations from fixed weather stations ingested through NOAA's MADIS system: NWS-maintained ASOS airport stations plus many networks NWS does not maintain (e.g. MesoWest, APRSWXNET, HADS, RAWS). Find the stations nearest a US lat/lon, then read the latest observation or up to 7 days of history; each value carries a MADIS quality-control flag.

tasks: current temperature / dewpoint / relative humidity
wind speed, direction and gusts
barometric and sea-level pressure
visibility, present weather and sky text description
precipitation over the last 1, 3 and 6 hours
raw METAR message (METAR stations)
recent observation history for a station (7 days retained, up to 500 per request)
nearest stations for a US lat/lon

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: No charge and no account. NWS docs say all API information is intended to be open data, free to use for any purpose.

latency.typical: Minutes after the station reports; observations may lag the upstream MADIS source by up to about 20 minutes
latency.notes: NWS docs say observations may be delayed up to 20 minutes from MADIS, the upstream source, because of QC processing (and since 4 Aug 2025 should no longer routinely be delayed more than that). Live check 2026-10-26: KNYC (Central Park, ASOS) latest observation was 03:51Z when fetched at about 04:58Z (the 04:51 report was not yet in), with Cache-Control max-age=87, s-maxage=300. Its last eight records were hourly at :51 with three hours missing. Single sample, not a spec. Nothing new is captured on request: stations report on their own schedule.

coverage.notes: Coverage is the fixed station network NWS ingests through MADIS; you cannot place a station. Live tests 2026-10-26: /stations lists stations for PR (149), GU (16), VI (13), AS (12) and MP (7), and stations in PR, GU, VI and MP returned observations from that day; none of the 12 American Samoa stations returned an observation and /points for Pago Pago lists no observation stations, so AS is left out. /points for London returns 404 'Data Unavailable For Requested Point'. Density varies: the nearest station to lower Manhattan was KNYC at 8.6 km; Vermont lists 199 stations, most from non-NWS networks (MesoWest 66, APRSWXNET 74), only one tagged ASOS. NWS says data quality can vary by provider. Rural density was not measured.

licensing.summary: NWS says information on its web pages is in the public domain unless specifically noted otherwise and may be used without charge for any lawful purpose, as long as you do not claim it as your own (e.g. claim copyright), imply NOAA/NWS endorsement or affiliation, or modify it and present it as official. The NWS name and visual identifier are trademarked. Under 17 U.S.C. 403, works consisting predominantly of NWS material must say that material is not subject to copyright. Third-party information is used under the third party's licence. Provided as-is with no warranty. The API docs say all API information is intended to be open data, free to use for any purpose. Neither page mentions AI training or resale explicitly, and neither says which station networks in the API count as third-party data.

human.unknown: Not applicable: readings are from automated or staffed stations, not crowd contributors; no human identity claim is made per observation

application.unknown: No documented signing or attestation of the data chain from instrument to API; integrity rests on a government-operated service over HTTPS. Most stations are not maintained by NWS (only ASOS is, per the API docs), and the instruments and software of other networks are not described in the API

camera.unknown: Not applicable; no imagery is collected

time.method: Each observation carries an instrument report timestamp (e.g. METAR time group '270351Z' matching timestamp 2026-10-27T03:51:00+00:00 in a live response).
time.unknown: How station clocks are disciplined is not documented in the API docs; no time-integrity method was found

location.method: Observations come from fixed, registered stations with published coordinates and elevation (/stations/{id}); the observation geometry is the station's location.
location.unknown: NWS does not maintain most stations (only ASOS); siting audits for other networks and whether coordinates are rounded (KNYC returned -73.98, 40.77) are not documented in the API. The value describes the station point, not the user's exact location

content.method: Each measured value carries a MADIS qualityControl flag: Z preliminary, no QC; C passed level 1 (validity); S passed levels 1 and 2 (internal, temporal, statistical spatial consistency); V passed levels 1-3 (incl. spatial buddy check); X failed level 1; Q passed 1, failed 2 or 3; G/B subjective good/bad; T virtual temperature not computed, QC-passing air temperature returned. MADIS publishes its tolerance limits and its reject/accept intervention lists. The latest endpoint accepts require_qc=true.
content.unknown: QC is automated range and consistency checking: it can miss slowly drifting or locally biased sensors, and it does not confirm the value is right. Flags are per value, so some fields in a record are unchecked (e.g. windGust and precipitation were 'Z' in a live KNYC record). NWS says data quality varies by provider and most stations are not NWS-maintained

corroboration.method: MADIS level 3 QC compares each observation with neighbouring stations (nearest in each of eight sectors) using an Optimal Interpolation analysis ('buddy' check); a 'V' flag means it passed. MADIS keeps hourly QC failure statistics per network.
corroboration.unknown: Buddy checks are weak where stations are sparse; the API does not expose which neighbours were used or the residuals

freshness.typical_age: Typically under about an hour for hourly METAR stations; up to about 20 minutes QC delay on top of the reporting cycle
freshness.notes: /observations/latest returns the newest record; /observations supports start/end for history, and NWS keeps only 7 days of station observations. Reporting interval varies by station and network and is not documented in the API docs; KNYC reported hourly at :51 in a live check. Known upstream issue: 24h max/min temperatures are always null for stations outside the central time zone (MADIS ingest bug).

auth.how_to_get: No signup. A User-Agent identifying your application is required (ideally with a website or email). NWS says this will be replaced with an API key in the future.

endpoints.params: latitude, longitude
endpoints.notes: Returns grid metadata including properties.observationStations, a URL like /gridpoints/{wfo}/{x},{y}/stations. 404 InvalidPoint outside coverage.

endpoints.params: limit
endpoints.notes: Stations for that grid point, sorted by distance from the forecast gridpoint, closest first, with distance in metres. /points/{lat},{lon}/stations is marked deprecated in the OpenAPI spec.

endpoints.params: id (list), state (state, territory or marine area codes), limit (1-500), cursor
endpoints.notes: Station catalogue

endpoints.params: stationId
endpoints.notes: Station metadata: coordinates, elevation, name, time zone; with Feature-Flags: obs_station_provider also provider and subProvider

endpoints.params: require_qc (boolean)
endpoints.notes: Latest observation as GeoJSON; each value has unitCode, value, qualityControl

endpoints.params: start, end, limit (1-500), cursor
endpoints.notes: Observation list for a station, newest first; 7 days retained

endpoints.params: time (ISO 8601)
endpoints.notes: Single observation at a given time

api.rate_limits: Not public; 'a generous amount for typical use'. Over-limit requests return an error and may be retried after the limit clears, typically within 5 seconds; proxies are more likely to hit it. The disclaimer's abuse guidelines ask clients to match request cycles to the data refresh rate, retry failed services at 1-minute intervals, and say abusive IPs or query types may be blocked. Responses carry Cache-Control headers.
api.notes: The OpenAPI spec also declares an apiKeyAuth scheme (header 'API-Key'; its description says X-Api-Key) that NWS is 'testing on certain endpoints' and says imposes no limits; no observation endpoint lists it and no way to get a key is published. The obs_station_provider Feature-Flags header adds each station's provider and subProvider (e.g. ASOS, MesoWest, APRSWXNET).

mcp.community: No NWS-run MCP server in the official MCP Registry. Third-party servers wrap api.weather.gov, e.g. io.github.cyanheads/nws-weather-mcp-server (https://nws.caseyjhand.com/mcp), io.github.pipeworx-io/nws (https://gateway.pipeworx.io/nws/mcp), ai.smithery/smithery-ai-national-weather-service.

sources.claim: Base URL api.weather.gov; User-Agent required, to be replaced with an API key; no fees, open data free to use for any purpose; rate limit not public but generous, retry after ~5 s; GeoJSON default; cache-friendly; observationStations sorted by distance; most stations not maintained by NWS except ASOS, data quality varies by provider; 7 days of observations retained; observations may be delayed up to 20 minutes from MADIS for QC; null 24h max/min upstream issue

Endpoint paths and parameters (require_qc on latest; start/end/limit 1-500/cursor on observations; id/state on /stations; /points/{lat},{lon}/stations deprecated); userAgent and apiKeyAuth security schemes; qualityControl enum Z,C,S,V,X,Q,G,B,T referring to MADIS; land/marine region codes

MADIS QC levels and flag meanings including T; tolerance limits; Optimal Interpolation buddy check with eight-sector neighbour search; reject/accept subjective intervention lists; per-network QC statistics

NWS information public domain unless noted, free for any lawful purpose; no copyright claims, no implied endorsement, no presenting modified content as official; name and visual identifier trademarked; 17 U.S.C. 403 notice; third-party data under its own licence; as-is, no warranty; abuse guidelines and possible IP blocking

Live test: KNYC hourly records at :51, with some hours missing

delivery.basis: NWS API docs: 'Observations may be delayed up to 20 minutes from MADIS, the upstream source, due to QC processing.'
