cards.name: OpenAQ
cards.summary: Nonprofit aggregator of openly licensed, ground-level air-quality data from hundreds of sources worldwide (government reference monitors since 2015, low-cost air sensors since 2021), harmonized into one free REST API (api.openaq.org/v3) with near-real-time and historical measurements. It reports what existing stations publish; it cannot deploy new sensors.
cards.short: Air-quality readings from government monitors and low-cost sensors in over 100 countries.

tasks: find air-quality stations near a point (radius up to 25 km), in a bounding box, or by country
latest PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, O3 and BC readings at a location, plus relative humidity and temperature where reported
PM1, PM4, CO2, NO, NOx, CH4 and ultrafine particles at a limited set of locations
raw, hourly, daily and yearly measurements per sensor, with summary statistics and coverage counts
filter reference-grade monitors from other sensors
look up the data licence, provider and owner of each location
list data-quality flags raised on a location or sensor

pricing.model: free within rate limits; custom plans by quote
pricing.notes: OpenAQ FAQ: data are provided for free within rate limits. The rate-limits page lists 'General use: Free' and 'Custom use: Contact us for pricing' for higher limits under a jointly agreed Custom Use Agreement. The terms say higher rates need OpenAQ's payment terms and API License and Services Agreement. No public price for custom plans.

latency.typical: Near real time; source reporting frequency 10 minutes to 24 hours
latency.notes: OpenAQ says it hosts 'near real-time and historical data' and that acceptable source data frequency is between 10 minutes and 24 hours. No end-to-end ingestion delay is published. The 'latest' value is the last point in a sensor's series, and some providers report out of order, so polling /latest does not guarantee complete coverage. Technical issues upstream or at OpenAQ can interrupt data flow. No new capture: you only get what existing stations report.

regions: Global (wherever upstream government agencies and sensor networks publish open data; uneven)
coverage.notes: OpenAQ says it aggregates 'hundreds of sources worldwide' and that its data 'do not represent all air quality monitoring data in the world.' An OpenAQ slide deck from August 2024 cites 56,000 locations in 153 countries and 43 billion data points. Only stationary, ground-level data are ingested (no satellite or airborne data). Country labels come from Natural Earth boundaries and may mislabel some stations.

licensing.summary: Varies by source. OpenAQ ingests only openly licensed data (e.g. CC0, CC BY 4.0) that it believes is available for redistribution, but gives no assurance the data are free of third-party claims; users must review and follow each source's terms (Creative Commons, open government or bespoke). Attribution to the original source where required, and to OpenAQ always, is required. Each location lists its licences, and the licences resource exposes commercialUseAllowed, attributionRequired, shareAlikeRequired, modificationAllowed and redistributionAllowed. Using the hosted API to build products that substantially duplicate or compete with OpenAQ is prohibited. Data are offered as-is without warranty. The terms do not mention AI training, resale or ownership of the data.

human.unknown: Not applicable in a person sense; data come from upstream agencies and sensor networks. OpenAQ names the provider and owner of each location (owner may be 'Unknown Governmental Organization') but does not document vetting who operates each station.

application.unknown: No attestation or signing of upstream data is documented. OpenAQ names the instrument and manufacturer per location but ingests what providers publish and harmonizes the format.

camera.unknown: Not applicable; no imagery is collected.

time.unknown: OpenAQ requires complete datetimes on ingested data but documents no check of upstream clocks; some providers report out of order.

location.unknown: OpenAQ requires complete coordinates but does not document verifying them. Country labels are approximate (Natural Earth boundaries). For mobile locations the coordinates are the first point measured.

content.unknown: Raw measurements are the values as reported upstream, offered as-is with no accuracy guarantee. The API exposes data-quality flags per location and sensor (label, level, time range), but the docs do not explain how flags are raised or what they cover.

corroboration.method: The API lets you filter for reference monitors (monitor=true), so an agent can compare low-cost sensors against nearby reference stations itself; OpenAQ documents no cross-check of its own.
corroboration.unknown: Whether upstream providers apply QA before publishing, and how OpenAQ's flags are produced, is not documented.

freshness.typical_age: Minutes to hours for latest readings (source frequency 10 min to 24 h); archive back years
freshness.notes: Live-ish 'latest' endpoints plus historical raw, hourly, daily and yearly series, and a bulk archive on AWS Open Data. Nothing is captured on demand.

delivery.basis: OpenAQ hosts 'near real-time and historical data'; acceptable source data frequency is between 10 minutes and 24 hours.

auth.how_to_get: Register at https://explore.openaq.org/register (valid name and non-disposable email; one key per individual) and copy the key from https://explore.openaq.org/account, where it can also be rotated.

endpoints.params: coordinates=lat,lon + radius (meters, default 1000, max 25000) OR bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat; iso (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), countries_id, monitor (bool, reference monitor), mobile (bool), providers_id, parameters_id, owner_contacts_id, manufacturers_id, instruments_id, licenses_id, order_by, sort_order, limit (default 100), page
endpoints.notes: Point+radius and bbox cannot be combined (422). Coordinates truncated to 4 decimals. coordinates without radius, or radius without coordinates, returns 422.

endpoints.params: locations_id
endpoints.notes: Location details: provider, owner, instruments, sensors, coordinates, mobile/monitor flags, and licences with attribution and date range.

endpoints.params: locations_id, datetime_min, limit, page
endpoints.notes: Latest value per sensor at a location; the last point in the series, not necessarily the most recently ingested.

endpoints.params: parameters_id (e.g. 2 = PM2.5), datetime_min, limit, page
endpoints.notes: Latest measurements across all sensors for one parameter.

endpoints.params: sensors_id, datetime_from, datetime_to, limit, page
endpoints.notes: Raw values as reported upstream. Hourly means at /v3/sensors/{sensors_id}/hours (datetime_from, datetime_to); daily means at /v3/sensors/{sensors_id}/days and yearly at /years (date_from, date_to). Aggregating over large ranges can time out (408); keep ranges small.

endpoints.params: locations_id, datetime_from, datetime_to, limit, page
endpoints.notes: Data-quality flags (type label, level, time range, sensor ids). Per sensor at /v3/sensors/{sensor_id}/flags.

endpoints.params: licenses_id
endpoints.notes: Licence flags: commercialUseAllowed, attributionRequired, shareAlikeRequired, modificationAllowed, redistributionAllowed, sourceUrl. Each location lists its licence ids under licenses[].

api.sdk: Official Python SDK (https://python.openaq.org/) and R package (https://openaq.github.io/openaq-r/).
api.rate_limits: Free tier: 60 requests/minute and 2,000/hour per API key. 429 on exceed; headers x-ratelimit-used/limit/remaining/reset. Repeated overruns can lead to a temporary or permanent ban (403, lifted only by contacting OpenAQ). Higher limits via a custom plan (quote).

mcp.community: Third-party wrappers in the official MCP Registry, not run by OpenAQ: io.github.cyanheads/openaq-mcp-server (npm @cyanheads/openaq-mcp-server, needs OPENAQ_API_KEY), io.github.pipeworx-io/openaq (https://gateway.pipeworx.io/openaq/mcp), io.github.malamutemayhem/openaq.
mcp.notes: No first-party OpenAQ MCP server found.

api.notes: v1 and v2 were retired on 31 January 2025 and return 410. Browser (CORS) calls are blocked; call from a server. The OpenAPI document is at https://api.openaq.org/openapi.json. Bulk historical files are on AWS Open Data (s3://openaq-data-archive) without a key.

payment.notes: Free tier needs no payment. Custom higher-limit plans are priced by contacting OpenAQ under a Custom Use Agreement; no payment methods are published.

cards.name: PEGELONLINE (German Federal Waterways)
cards.short: Live water levels from 786 gauges on German federal waterways, every 1–15 minutes, no key.
cards.summary: Germany's Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration (WSV) publishes raw readings from 786 gauges on federal waterways and coasts, mostly water level, plus discharge, water temperature and other parameters at some gauges, and water-level forecasts at a few. Readings are taken every 1 to 15 minutes and served through a free, keyless REST API with the last 31 days of data.

tasks: gauges near a point
gauges on a named river or waterway
current water level at a gauge
current discharge, water temperature or other parameter where the gauge has it
time series of the last 31 days
water-level forecast at selected gauges

delivery.basis: ITZBund: "Aktuell veröffentlicht PEGELONLINE neue Pegelwerte mit einer Verzögerung von ein bis fünf Minuten." Series intervals (equidistance) are 1, 5, 10 or 15 minutes.

latency.typical: 1–15 minute readings, published 1–5 minutes after measurement
latency.notes: ITZBund says new values appear with a 1–5 minute delay; coastal gauges measure every minute and inland gauges every 15 minutes. In the live check, 502 water-level series were at 15-minute intervals, 224 at 1 minute, 10 at 10 minutes and 1 at 5 minutes. The median current reading was 16 minutes old; 3 of 737 were over 25 hours old (flagged out-dated by the API).

freshness.typical_age: about 15–30 minutes
freshness.notes: Live check: median age of the current water-level reading 16 minutes, 90th percentile 31 minutes. The API marks a current value 'out-dated' when it is older than 25 hours and 'commented' when the gauge reports a fault.

regions: Germany (federal waterways and North Sea and Baltic coasts)
A few cross-border gauges in the Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland and the Czech Republic
coverage.notes: 786 stations, 737 with a water-level series. Gauges sit on federal waterways (Rhine, Elbe, Danube, Main, Weser, Oder, canals, coasts), not on smaller state-run rivers. The Dict-API tags 719 stations Germany, 5 Netherlands, 1 Austria and 1 Switzerland. Other foreign gauges come from Rijkswaterstaat (10), viadonau (9) and Povodí Labe (6); 57 stations, including most of these, have no coordinates and cannot be found by a point search.

pricing.model: free
pricing.notes: Free (FAQ: "kostenlos und frei verfügbar"). No registration or key.

licensing.summary: Data are under Datenlizenz Deutschland Zero 2.0 (DL-DE->Zero-2.0): "Any use is permitted without restrictions or conditions." The terms add that data may be used commercially and non-commercially, passed to third parties, combined with other data and built into products. They are unchecked raw data with no liability or warranty for accuracy, timeliness or completeness, and the same disclaimer covers third-party data from other national and international agencies. The terms do not mention AI training or resale by name.

human.unknown: Automated gauges; no person takes or confirms individual readings.

application.unknown: No signing or device attestation of readings is documented.

camera.unknown: Not a camera source.

time.method: Each reading carries an ISO 8601 timestamp in German legal time with an explicit UTC offset.
time.unknown: Timestamps come from the operator's own system and are not signed; how gauge clocks are kept is not documented.

location.method: Each station has published WGS84 coordinates, a river kilometre and a gauge datum.
location.unknown: Coordinates are the operator's own; 57 stations have none, and nothing independent checks them.

content.method: Values are raw sensor readings; the API flags faults ('commented') and stale values ('out-dated', over 25 hours).
content.unknown: The operator calls the data unchecked raw data and gives no warranty that values are correct or complete.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms individual readings. Checked daily values (Terminwerte) exist at shipping gauges, but they are the operator's own check.

auth.how_to_get: No authentication or registration is needed.

endpoints.params: latitude, longitude, radius (WGS84; radius unit not documented, results consistent with km); waters (e.g. RHEIN,MAIN); fuzzyId; ids; hasTimeseries; includeTimeseries; includeCurrentMeasurement; includeCharacteristicValues; includeForecastTimeseries; limit, offset
endpoints.notes: Stations with uuid, number, name, river km, agency, coordinates and water; with includeTimeseries&includeCurrentMeasurement each series carries its current value. Refer to stations by uuid; numbers and names can change.

endpoints.params: timeseries: W (water level), Q (discharge), WT (water temperature), etc.
endpoints.notes: Returns timestamp, value and, for water level, stateMnwMhw and stateNswHsw (low, normal, high, unknown, commented, out-dated).

endpoints.params: start (ISO 8601 time or period such as P8D; default last 10 days), end
endpoints.notes: Raw readings for up to the last 31 days. Also .csv, and .png for a chart. Forecasts use timeseries WV; checked daily values use TRM.

endpoints.params: includeStations, includeTimeseries, includeCurrentMeasurement, ids
endpoints.notes: All waters, optionally with their stations and series.

api.rate_limits: None published. Responses carry Cache-Control max-age (1–60 s) and an ETag for conditional GET; the docs ask clients to cache and use gzip.
api.sdk: @52north/edis-lib (npm, TypeScript) wraps the REST API, the Dict-API and the EDIS MQTT stream.
api.notes: Other keyless services: the Dict-API (https://dict-api.pegelonline.wsv.de/search, filters by station, water, state, country, bbox, parameter) and the HyDAS API (https://pegelonline.wsv.de/api/v1, beta, may change incompatibly), plus WMS, WFS and SOS. Push delivery over MQTT (EDIS, edis.pegelonline.wsv.de) is in a pilot phase and needs basic-auth credentials requested from ITZBund.

cards.name: Planet (Planet Labs)
cards.short: Satellite imagery of anywhere on Earth: near-daily PlanetScope, and new 50 cm SkySat captures from $12 per km2.
cards.summary: Operator of the PlanetScope (near-daily, ~3-4 m), SkySat (50 cm class), Pelican (30-50 cm class) and Tanager (hyperspectral) satellite constellations. New SkySat captures can be bought pay-as-you-go through Planet Select (a self-service web portal run with SkyFi; published per-km2 prices, 25 km2 minimum) or under an annual tasking-credits contract, which also covers Pelican and Tanager and gives access to the Tasking API (key from Planet sales). Its Data and Orders APIs search and deliver the existing archive; PlanetScope scenes 30 days and older are self-serve with an Insights Flex plan.

tasks: search archive scenes by area, date range, cloud cover and item type (e.g. PSScene, SkySatCollect)
scene-count statistics over time for an area
order and deliver archive scenes or basemaps, with optional raster tools, to download or cloud storage
new SkySat tasking: point (25 km2 square), line, area, stereo, tri-stereo and video (30-120 s) collects
Flexible tasking (automated retries for a cloud-minimized capture over a time of interest of 14+ days) and Assured tasking (a chosen imaging window, collected regardless of weather)
Pelican (30-50 cm) and Tanager hyperspectral tasking, and Tanager methane estimates, under a tasking-credits contract
price estimate before placing a tasking order (Tasking API)

delivery.basis: Planet's Assured Tasking terms: imaging windows 'between ≤ 7 days and ≥ 6 hours prior to TOI'; orthorectified products '≤ 12 hours from capture'. Planet Select: 'New tasking is completed within your selected capture window.'

pricing.model: Published per-km2 prices for pay-as-you-go SkySat tasking and archive through Planet Select; monthly or annual Insights Flex plans for archive PlanetScope; annual contracts (tasking credits, committed use) through sales for the Tasking API, Pelican, Tanager and fresher PlanetScope data
pricing.unit: per km2 (SkySat Flexible Tasking via Planet Select; 25 km2 minimum order)
pricing.notes: Planet's pricing page lists SkySat Flexible Tasking at $12/km2, SkySat Assured Tasking at $40/km2 and SkySat archive (30 days and older) at $6/km2, via Planet Select, with a 25 km2 minimum order (so about $300 for the smallest Flexible order). Pelican, Tanager, stereo, line and area collects are quoted by sales. Insights Flex plans for PlanetScope archive data (30 days and older): Starter $110/month or $1,100/year (7,000 monitoring credits/month), Professional $550/month, Scale $1,200/month; ordering 30-day-and-older PlanetScope scenes costs 50 monitoring credits per km2. Next-day and near-real-time PlanetScope needs an enterprise or Planet Agriculture plan (Agriculture: $0.35-$1.80 per hectare by country tier, sold in 5 km2 increments on an annual contract). The Tasking API's POST /tasking/v2/pricing/ and GET /tasking/v2/orders/{id}/pricing return a quota cost for contract customers. A free 30-day trial (3,000 monitoring credits, no card) covers public and sandbox data only, not ordering over your own area.

latency.typical: New SkySat capture: Assured tasking collects in a chosen imaging window booked between 6 hours and 7 days before the time of interest (Express windows under 6 hours); Flexible tasking keeps trying over a time of interest of at least 14 days. Orthorectified products are delivered within about 12 hours of capture (L1A within about 4 hours for Assured). Archive search is immediate.
latency.notes: Planet's tasking terms call the latency figures estimates that may vary. Flexible orders must be placed at least 24 hours before the time of interest. Planet Select says archive data is delivered immediately and new tasking is completed within the selected capture window. The Tasking API distinguishes Standard delivery (per SLA) from Fast Track delivery (as soon as data is available) but gives no figures. Archive scenes in the Data API must be activated before download, or ordered through the Orders API.

regions: Global (PlanetScope: Earth's land surface near-daily; SkySat and Pelican: tasked anywhere not restricted)
coverage.notes: Planet's June 2026 product specifications say PlanetScope provides near-daily imagery of the entire land surface with hundreds of Dove satellites in orbit, and that about fifteen SkySat-C satellites are in orbit (4-5 day revisit per satellite). Planet says certain countries and areas are restricted for tasking for capacity and compliance reasons and that these change; Planet Select shows when an area is unavailable and may restrict sensitive areas. Insights Flex reserves the right to limit access within some regions. Area tasking orders are capped at an account-specific maximum km2.

licensing.summary: Licensed, not sold. Under Planet's Master Content License Agreement 2026.1 (effective June 24, 2026, current for all Order Schedules) Planet grants a limited, nontransferable, non-sublicensable, revocable licence scoped by the Order Schedule and retains all right, title and interest in the content. You may not distribute, sublicense or let third parties access the content, create derivative works except as authorized, use it to improve non-Planet imagery, or build a substitute for Planet's products. AI training is allowed if your Order Schedule's usage rights allow Derivative Products, unless the Order Schedule says otherwise: not to replicate Planet content or improve third-party imagery, only on isolated, encrypted systems, and the resulting model stays subject to Planet's rights and may not be commercialized or distributed unless the Order Schedule permits. The Terms of Use (September 1, 2026) let Insights Platform licensees build application and media derivative products for third parties' internal use only, without source imagery, and require a Planet credit. The MCLA lets Planet require agentic users to be identified.

human.unknown: Not applicable: captures come from automated satellites, with no human operator in the loop

application.unknown: No public documentation of signing, provenance attestation, or a tamper-evident chain from satellite downlink to delivered file

camera.method: Each scene is an item type tied to one constellation (e.g. PSScene, SkySatCollect), and Planet's product specifications document each constellation's sensors (e.g. SkySat: three 5.5 MP CMOS detectors behind a 3.6 m focal-length telescope)
camera.unknown: No signed provenance links a delivered file to a specific satellite and sensor; you rely on Planet's metadata

time.method: Scenes carry an 'acquired' timestamp that the Data API filters on (DateRangeFilter on 'acquired'); tasking captures are reported per order through /tasking/v2/captures/
time.unknown: How the acquisition time is derived and its accuracy are not documented on the pages read; timestamps are not signed

location.method: Ortho products are corrected with attitude telemetry and ephemeris, then orthorectified with ground control points and 30-90 m DEMs; Planet's product specifications state positional accuracy under 10 m RMSE (PlanetScope ortho: 'Less than 10 m RMSE at 90th percentile'; SkySat ortho: under 10 m RMSE). Raw SkySat geolocation knowledge is 30-50 m
location.unknown: These are specifications, not per-scene measurements; accuracy varies by region and terrain, and no per-scene error is published

content.unknown: No public method for detecting manipulated imagery. Cloud cover and quality_category are metadata, not authenticity checks. Orders API manifests carry per-file MD5 and SHA-256 digests, which show a file arrived intact but are unsigned and say nothing about what it shows

corroboration.unknown: Planet offers no per-capture independent cross-check. A NASA GSFC study (June 2022) measured PlanetScope offsets against WorldView imagery for a few sample sites (see attestations); it says nothing about any individual delivered scene or about SkySat

attestations.verifier: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (Tan, Lin, Wolfe)
attestations.scope: location (PlanetScope geolocation, relative to WorldView reference images)
attestations.result: Sample sites only: after filtering, mean offsets of 4.24 m east-west and -0.81 m north-south in New Mexico; about 3-8 m east-west and 4.7-6.4 m north-south in Singapore, where the two WorldView references disagreed by about 8 m

freshness.typical_age: Tasking: captured after you order. Archive: PlanetScope from near-daily to years old; self-serve Insights Flex gets PlanetScope 30 days and older; SkySat archive via Planet Select is 30 days and older.
freshness.notes: The Data API and Orders API serve existing scenes; the Tasking API and Planet Select order new captures. A tasking customer may buy an archive hold of up to 30 days before its captures join the shared SkySat archive. Buying archive imagery through the Tasking API is deprecated and ends November 1, 2026.

auth.how_to_get: Data and Orders APIs: the API key on your Planet Account page, My Settings tab (one active key at a time; needs an account with a paid plan to order your own areas). Send it as HTTP Basic with the key as username and an empty password (preferred). Planet's own examples use PL_API_KEY. Tasking API: the key comes from a Planet sales representative.
Same key, sent as 'Authorization: api-key <key>'. The Tasking API docs use this form.
Same key as the api_key query parameter, where an API supports it (meant for tile-streaming clients).

Authorization-code or device-code login at login.planet.com, giving a JWT sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Interactive client registration has not been released: the only supported interactive client is Planet's CLI and Python SDK ('planet auth login'), which planet-mcp also uses. Machine-to-machine client credentials work only on services.sentinel-hub.com so far. Planet intends to deprecate API keys eventually, with no date set. api.planet.com serves no RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata.

api.sdk: Planet Python SDK and 'planet' CLI (planetlabs/planet-client-python)
api.rate_limits: Data API: activation 2/s, download 5/s, search 5/s, other 10/s. Orders API (per key): create, get, list and cancel 3/s each, download 5/s, bulk cancel 5/s. Tasking API: 30/min unauthenticated, 40/s burst, 300/min sustained; HTTP 429 when exceeded.
api.notes: The Data and Orders APIs are self-serve once you buy an Insights Flex plan (archive PlanetScope 30 days and older); new captures by API need the Tasking API and a contract key, while self-serve new captures go through the Planet Select web portal. Orders can include metadata.stac (beta, scenes only) for a STAC catalog; manifest.json lists MD5 and SHA-256 digests per file. No /.well-known/ucp, /.well-known/agent-card.json or /.well-known/irlpls is served on planet.com or api.planet.com.

mcp.auth: Planet account via 'planet auth login' (OAuth2 through the Planet CLI)
mcp.notes: planet-mcp is Planet's experimental local (stdio) MCP server built on the Planet SDK, installed with 'pip install planet-mcp'. Planet warns it can create and modify orders and subscriptions, and says not to disable tool approvals. It is not in the official MCP Registry and has no hosted endpoint.

payment.notes: Insights Platform plans are paid monthly or annually with a stored payment method, and monitoring credits are bought up front with top-ups. Tasking credits are paid up front under an annual contract. Planet Select orders are placed and paid in the SkyFi-run portal. No agent payment method is documented.

requester.checks: Planet Select does not permit defence and intelligence use cases and may restrict sensitive areas; tasking-credits contracts do permit them. Tasking is restricted over certain countries and areas. Users must comply with export controls and sanctions and may not serve restricted parties or jurisdictions. The MCLA lets Planet require agentic users to be identified by user-agent headers or separate credentials and their purpose described.
requester.unknown: How Planet screens a new self-serve customer is not published.

cards.name: Premise
cards.short: Smartphone crowd in 140+ countries for photo, video and survey tasks; sold by contract, no public API.
cards.summary: Premise turns a customer's questions into paid tasks in its mobile app. Contributors in over 140 countries complete them by taking photos, videos and audio recordings, answering surveys or reporting what they see at a place. Submissions go through automatic and manual quality control, and results reach the customer in a dashboard or as a raw export. It is sold for retail audits, price and market monitoring, point-of-interest mapping and verification, and situation monitoring for development and humanitarian work.

tasks: location surveys
retail audits and store visits
price and product availability monitoring
location discovery and point-of-interest verification
mapping infrastructure, services and businesses
business hours and offerings
situation analysis and remote monitoring
video interviews (VideoAI)
asset and site inspections

pricing.model: per project (quote)
pricing.notes: No price published; the only route is Book a Demo. The SaaS Agreement bills in US dollars under an executed Order Document, with fees payable up front unless the Order Document says otherwise, auto-renewing terms (one year by default) and no refunds. Negotiated pricing is confidential. from_usd 0 means not published.

latency.typical: Same-day data once a campaign is running (company-stated).
latency.notes: The homepage says organisations 'can swiftly gather same-day data'. The 2019 brochure says a campaign 'can begin in as little as 24-48 hours' where a contributor network exists, and that recruiting and training a network in a new region takes 2-4 weeks. Contributor rejection appeals take 3-5 days.

coverage.notes: Company-stated: 'over 140 countries', '6M+ Contributors Worldwide', '25M+ Submissions per Year', '2.3M+ Unique Points of Interest', and over 120,000 traditional-trade store visits a month (December 2024). No country list or density is published. The contributor terms exclude people resident in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, Syria and Crimea. For new regions the 2019 brochure gives 2-4 weeks to recruit a network.

licensing.summary: Under the public SaaS Agreement, data 'collected specifically for Customer' under an Order Document (Collected Data) is owned by the customer, and Premise assigns 'all intellectual property rights it has' in it. Data Premise sells to other customers too (Licensed Data) comes with a non-exclusive, non-transferable, perpetual licence for internal business purposes only and 'may not be resold or otherwise directly commercialized'. A separately negotiated master agreement overrides these terms. Contributors keep their content but grant Premise a non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable licence to exploit it for any purpose, including by the customer and the customer's clients. The terms do not name AI training by buyers, or whether Premise trains on customer data.

human.method: One account and one device per person, with no account sharing (Community Guidelines). Premise may run background and security checks at its discretion (Terms of Use), and the 2019 brochure lists account-duplication checks.
human.unknown: No identity check is required for ordinary tasks; sign-up is by Google or Apple credentials or a username and password. KYC applies only to the Premise Wallet. Contributors reach customers only as anonymous IDs, so a buyer cannot check who captured an item.

application.method: Tasks are done only in the Premise mobile app. The guidelines ban access by any other means than a mobile device, and any 'auto' or 'macro' software. The app collects the names of installed apps to detect ones that 'doctor' location data or the clock.
application.unknown: No device or app attestation (such as Play Integrity or App Attest) is documented.

camera.method: Image Analysis in quality control checks that photos are 'not blurry or from a computer, and of the correct subject'.
camera.unknown: How screen or generated images are detected is not published. There is no C2PA or other signed capture, and Premise is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.method: Submissions carry timestamps (2019 brochure). The app checks installed apps to catch any that 'doctor' the clock.
time.unknown: Whether the timestamp comes from the device or the server, and whether the buyer receives a capture time for each item, is not documented.

location.method: The app records precise check-in and observation locations. Quality control includes location verification and machine-learning anti-spoofing. The guidelines ban mocking or spoofing location, and starting and finishing a task in different places.
location.unknown: How the coordinates are checked is undocumented, and no public proof is offered for any item.

content.method: Every submission goes through automatic (machine-learning) and manual quality control and fraud detection before it reaches the dashboard. The task brief defines the deliverable.
content.unknown: Rejection and error rates are not published.

corroboration.method: 'crowdsourced confirmation' on top of manual quality control (2019 brochure).
corroboration.unknown: Only the 2019 brochure mentions it, and current pages do not. How often items are confirmed, and by whom, is not stated.

api.notes: No public API docs. Customers use dashboards and raw data export (CSV, KMZ, PDF), and the 2019 brochure mentions a 'Data API for real-time data access' to results. api.premise.com answers every path, including /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, with HTTP 400 'authorization header missing or malformed', so a private API exists but is undocumented. Ordering is by sales contract; no tasking API is published.

mcp.notes: No Premise entry in the official MCP Registry (2026-10-26).

delivery.basis: 'If a network is already in place where your study is situated, your data acquisition campaign can begin in as little as 24-48 hours. For new regions, we can recruit and train a network in 2-4 weeks' (2019 brochure); 'swiftly gather same-day data' (homepage).

freshness.notes: Collected Data is captured for the customer's tasks. Licensed Data that Premise already holds is also sold, but it is not new capture.

payment.notes: No payment method is published. Fees follow an executed Order Document, are payable in US dollars at registration or renewal unless the Order Document says otherwise, are non-cancellable and non-refundable, and carry 1.5% a month on late payment.

requester.checks: No customer screening is published. Customers sign an Order Document, and the SaaS Agreement forbids unlawful use and material that violates third-party privacy. Contributors are told not to invade privacy or enter non-public spaces, and may leave any task where they feel unsafe.
requester.unknown: Whether Premise reviews task briefs, for example ones that target a specific person or private place, before contributors see them.

sources.claim: 140+ countries, 6M+ contributors, 25M+ submissions a year, 2.3M+ points of interest, same-day data, validation algorithms, Book a Demo only

cards.name: Prolific
cards.summary: Online platform that recruits ID-verified adult participants in about 50 countries for paid studies and human-data collection, run through a web app, REST API, CLI or a first-party MCP server. Its AI Task Builder Collections let participants upload their own photos, recordings and files. Prolific prohibits in-person studies, including asking participants to visit specific locations, so it cannot send anyone to a place, and it does not verify where or when an uploaded file was captured.
cards.short: ID-verified people in about 50 countries for paid online studies and uploads; no in-person or on-site tasks.

tasks: online surveys and experiments, hosted on Prolific or on an external survey tool
AI model evaluation, preference ranking and annotation (AI Task Builder Batches)

original data collection with AI Task Builder Collections: free text, multiple choice and file upload with set file types, sizes and counts (Prolific's examples: photos, documents, recordings, egocentric video, speech samples)
longitudinal and multi-wave studies with the same participants
targeting by 300+ audience filters, custom screeners and representative samples

pricing.model: pay as you go from a prepaid workspace balance: a participant reward you set plus a platform fee; managed services by custom quote
pricing.unit: per participant submission (the reward you set, plus platform fee)
pricing.notes: The pricing page states a platform fee of usually 42.8% for corporate customers and 33.3% for academic or non-profit customers. The minimum reward is £6.00 / $8.00 per hour, with £9.00 / $12.00 recommended. No subscription or contract is needed for the platform; managed services use a Statement of Work. A submission's price depends on its estimated time, so no price per capture is published, and from_usd is 0. POST /study-cost-calculator/ returns a study's total including VAT and fees. Final cost can exceed a quote (underpaying adjustments, extra approvals, bonuses). Minimum top-up £0.51 / $0.51.

latency.typical: Prolific says self-serve studies typically launch in minutes and return first responses in hours. Most studies start recruiting quickly; contact support if recruitment has not started within two hours.
latency.notes: Speed depends on time of day, filters, reward and the eligible pool. Prolific gives no guaranteed timeframe and says it cannot currently support time-sensitive studies. Webhooks (response.submitted, study.completed) allow incremental ingest. Funding by bank transfer can take up to 7 days; card top-ups are instant.

regions: 49 supported countries, mostly OECD members, including the US, UK, Canada, EU countries, Japan, Korea, Australia and New Zealand, plus Brazil, Mexico, Chile, South Africa, the Gulf states, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Singapore
Small participant populations in Algeria, Argentina, Colombia, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Malawi, Malaysia, Morocco, the Philippines and Vietnam
coverage.notes: Country means where a participant lives, filtered by screener; it says nothing about where a capture is made. Prolific describes particularly strong representation in the US, UK and Europe. Pool size: 300,000+ active participants (pricing page; 'our participant pool in numbers' page says 300k+ and 43 represented countries, 86 languages). The participant help page lists Egypt, India and Indonesia as supported, while the researcher page lists them as small populations. No city-level availability is published, and in-person tasks are prohibited, so coverage of a specific place is not offered.

licensing.summary: Researcher Terms (full version, last updated 14 Aug 2026), section M: Prolific claims no rights in Studies or Submissions, and the Participant Terms ask participants to waive proprietary rights in a Submission to the Researcher and, where needed, assign them 'for their sole use'. Section B forbids researchers to 'sell, distribute, publish, sublicense, loan or copy any of the Submissions if not expressly permitted by the Terms', and the terms grant no such permission. The researcher is data controller and must give participants a privacy notice. Media (audio, video, images) must be flagged in the study description, must not include direct identifiers, and must not be used to re-identify anyone. The terms do not mention AI or machine-learning training by the buyer. For AI Task Builder studies Prolific holds Submissions as processor and says it 'will not use Study data or Submissions for our own purposes', but it may review them for compliance, safeguarding, troubleshooting and improving the platform. It also runs authenticity checks and deletes Submissions 6 months after the study completes. The terms do not mention model training by Prolific.

human.method: Waitlist entry, then identity verification with a live video selfie matched to a government-issued ID (Onfido/Entrust; vendor-reported fraud rate under 0.1%, false acceptance 0.01%), phone and email verification, IP validation and deduplication, VPN detection, an onboarding quality screen, surprise identity re-checks with new selfies, bi-monthly pool audits and behavioural monitoring. Prolific describes 110+ checks in its Protocol system. Optional bot authenticity checks, on by default in AI Task Builder; a '100% Human Guarantee' refunds double for bot-flagged submissions in eligible Qualtrics studies.
human.unknown: All figures are Prolific's or its ID vendor's; no independent audit is published. Prolific's pages disagree on the number of checks (40+, 50+, 110+). Whether the verified person is the one who made a given uploaded photo or recording is not checked.

application.unknown: AI Task Builder Collections take files through a browser file-upload field with allowed types and sizes. No controlled capture app or app attestation is documented.

camera.unknown: No method confirms an upload came from a live camera rather than an existing file, a screen recording or a generator. Prolific is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.unknown: Exports carry a submission created_at timestamp; nothing establishes when an uploaded file was actually captured.

location.unknown: No location verification. IP validation and the country filter concern where a participant lives and duplicate accounts, not where a file was captured, and studies asking participants to visit specific locations are prohibited.

content.method: Protocol quality checks, LLM and bot authenticity checks (behavioural signals such as copy-paste, tab switching, mouse movement and pacing; Prolific reports 98.7% precision and 78.9% recall in its own testing), flags for exceptionally fast submissions, participant quality scores from researcher approvals and rejections, and manual review by a data-quality team. The researcher approves or rejects each submission.
content.unknown: These target bots, AI-written text and low effort in surveys. No public method checks whether an uploaded photo, video or audio file shows what it claims, or detects staged, reused or AI-generated media.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-checking of a submission against other sources or second captures. A researcher can collect several participants per task and compare them.

cards.name: ProxyPics
cards.summary: Marketplace that sends nearby 'Proxies' (independent-contractor data collectors) to a US address to take photos and answer questions in the ProxyPics app, ordered through a public, self-serve REST API with a sandbox and webhooks. A 'Direct' mode instead texts a point of contact (such as the homeowner or property staff) a link so they capture the photos themselves.
cards.short: A nearby person goes to a US address and takes photos in the ProxyPics app.

tasks: exterior property photos, address verification and street scenes

pricing.model: per request; the Client pays a platform fee per request, with an optional price_boost
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published, not free. No price list on proxypics.com or in the API docs. The Participation Agreement says Clients are charged a fee for each request, in USD, that fees may vary, and that Clients should check the fees each time they use the Platform; the Client is billed as soon as the Proxy submits. Each API photo request carries a `cost` in cents (including any `price_boost`), so the price is visible after the request is created, and a PhotoRequestCostUpdated webhook reports fee changes. A 2018 BuiltIn Chicago article reported a flat $5 per photo with the photographer keeping $3.25; that is eight years old and not used as the price.

latency.typical: Under 24 hours (provider marketing); often under two hours in high-volume markets (HousingWire profile)
latency.notes: Crowdsource page advertises 'Delivered Under 24 Hours'; the About page says Proxies 'often deliver results within hours if not minutes'. HousingWire's company profile says 96% of assignments are completed in under 24 hours. No contractual SLA found. Requests can be scheduled (`scheduled_at`) or given an expiry (`expires_at`); expired requests can be extended through the API. After submission the Client has 120 hours to reject.

coverage.notes: Advertised as nationwide US, 24/7 with no blackout dates, day or night. Network size claims vary by source: 180K+ data collectors (Crowdsource and Real Estate pages), 395,000-plus Proxy panel and 415,000+ assignments fulfilled in 2025 (HousingWire profile). Rural density and fill rates are not published.

licensing.summary: ProxyPics owns the deliverables, not the buyer. Under the Participation Agreement (which covers Clients and Proxies) Proxy work product is a work made for hire for ProxyPics and all rights vest in ProxyPics; ProxyPics 'may grant Clients and its Affiliates the right to use, reproduce, distribute, display, and otherwise exploit such work product in connection with Client requests and ProxyPics's business'. The Platform Provider terms also assign all Submissions to ProxyPics. No public client licence states the scope of that grant, resale or AI training. ProxyPics processes work product and metadata for quality assurance, fraud prevention, support, product improvement and service delivery, and may use de-identified, aggregated data for analytics; AI or model training is not named.

human.method: Proxies register with true identity details (business name, address, phone, email, tax ID), may hold only one account, may not share it, and must personally perform each order; ProxyPics may require identity verification. Background checks by a third party are optional, paid by the Proxy, and needed only for interior-access and appointment orders. Marketing says 'Tiered Proxies (Licensed and Background Checked)'.
human.unknown: Most Proxies may not be background-checked: the check is voluntary and only gates interior and appointment orders, and the Participation Agreement says ProxyPics does 'not conduct any screening or other verification with respect to Clients or Proxies'. How identity is confirmed, and how account sharing is detected, is not published. Orders that need no licence go to all nearby Proxies.

application.method: Photos must be taken inside the ProxyPics app; the FAQ says outside-app photos are not accepted because of anti-fraud technology. Proxies may not spoof location, timestamps or device information.
application.unknown: Whether the app attests its own integrity or detects emulators or modified clients. In Direct mode the photo taker is the point of contact (often the owner), who gets an SMS link to the app or a web app.

camera.method: 'Camera Roll Locked' feature so photos cannot be imported from the gallery
camera.unknown: Whether a live camera pointed at a screen or printout is detected. No C2PA or other signed capture.

time.method: 'Time Stamped Photos ... validate the exact date and time the photo was taken'; terms require capture at or near the time of the visit
time.unknown: Whether the timestamp is device clock or server-side, and whether it is signed. The public API schema gives only order-level times (`completed_at`), not per-photo capture times. The FAQ says some clients 'require us to time stamp or geo-code the photos', suggesting it may not apply to every order.

location.method: Georeference: photos get GPS coordinates and are pinned to a map; the app prevents taking photos outside a set radius of the subject; the FAQ says all photos are geo-tagged; GPS spoofing is banned in the Participation Agreement
location.unknown: Radius size and GPS-spoofing resistance are not published. The public API schema exposes only the request's latitude and longitude, not per-photo coordinates (they may appear in the PDF report).

content.method: AI plus a ProxyPics quality-control team review submissions for quality, order requirements and fraud, including orders the AI did not flag; the client can approve or reject each completed request through the API within 120 hours, for wrong property or work not requested, and rejected jobs are redone or reposted

cards.name: PurpleAir
cards.summary: Network of over 35,000 consumer-owned optical particulate sensors that report every two minutes, read through a points-metered REST API (api.purpleair.com) with real-time and historical data back to 2016.
cards.short: Crowd-hosted air-quality sensors reporting every 2 minutes, read through a prepaid points API.

tasks: PM1.0 / PM2.5 / PM10 air quality
temperature
humidity
latest readings for all public sensors in a bounding box
historical sensor data retrieval (real-time to yearly averages)

pricing.model: prepaid API points, charged per call and per field per data row
pricing.unit: minimum points purchase ($10 buys 1,000,000 points at 100,000 points per USD)
pricing.notes: New users get 1,000,000 points on sign-up. Live tier table (minimum purchase $10): $10-$49 at 100,000 points/USD, $50-$249 at 150,000, $250-$499 at 200,000, $500-$999 at 300,000, $1,000-$4,999 at 500,000, $5,000+ at 1,000,000. Cost per call = endpoint base cost + (cost of all fields x data rows); base cost is at most 5 points (get_sensor 1, get_sensor_history 2); fields cost 1-2 points per row in the published examples. Example: one sensor's pm2.5 every 10 minutes costs 432 points a day. The full per-field table is on the Developer Dashboard (login, not read). Sensor owners still spend points on their own sensors' data, but PurpleAir gives free points on request by email and plans to automate that. Values are subject to change. A points subscription also exists in the account area (terms not public).

latency.typical: Sensors report every 2 minutes; the real-time endpoints return each sensor's latest report
latency.notes: PurpleAir's API guidelines say sensors report every two minutes and real-time data is held in memory, so querying more often than once a minute is unnecessary. Repeated calls return the same data until the sensor next reports; request last_seen to see when. No service level: the Fair Use Policy says availability and response times are not guaranteed. No new deployments to order: data comes only from sensors owners have already installed.

regions: Global (wherever owners have installed sensors; distribution uneven)
coverage.notes: PurpleAir says over 35,000 sensors worldwide. Coverage is wherever owners have installed and registered sensors, and only public sensors are readable without the owner's read key. You cannot request a new placement. No per-country list or density figures are published.

licensing.summary: PurpleAir's Terms (updated 18 July 2022) say PurpleAir owns all PurpleAir Data and any derivatives' underlying data. The licence is non-exclusive, non-transferable and non-sublicensable. You may use the data internally to test and develop your own product, and distribute that product commercially only to end users for their internal, non-commercial, non-public use, after written notice to PurpleAir. No raw data to third parties, no reselling the data or an API modelled on it, and no competing air-quality database without written permission. API calls must be made only by you, and keys must not be shared. A grantback licence gives PurpleAir rights in your derivatives, explicitly including AI algorithms trained on PurpleAir data and their outputs. You may not combine the data with open-source-licensed materials. Attribution is required: 'Data from PurpleAir' for direct use, 'Powered by PurpleAir' for derived data, with a link for APIs and ML models. Health or emergency uses need a disclaimer. The terms do not explicitly allow or forbid AI training; they attach the grantback to it.

human.unknown: Whether a sensor owner is a real, distinct person; owners register sensors themselves and API keys are tied to a developer account, not to sensor hosts

application.unknown: Whether readings come from unmodified PurpleAir firmware or hardware; the terms forbid modifying sensors, but no attestation or signing is documented

camera.unknown: Not applicable: this is a particulate sensor network and collects no imagery

time.unknown: How sensor clocks are set or checked; the API exposes last_seen and time stamps, but no timing-integrity method is documented

location.method: The Terms say each sensor's location is extrapolated from Google's Wi-Fi-based location services together with the location the owner enters, calculated on the sensor or on PurpleAir's servers. The owner sets the inside/outside label.
location.unknown: How the Wi-Fi fix and the owner's entry are reconciled, and whether a moved or misregistered sensor is detected; the Terms call the location 'likely' and publish no per-sensor check

content.unknown: Whether a sensor is exposed to staged or local sources (smoke, cooking, indoor placement); the provider disclaims accuracy and documents no tamper checks. The dual laser counters (A and B channels) are exposed as fields, but no provider-side flagging method is documented

corroboration.unknown: PurpleAir documents no per-sensor cross-check against reference monitors. The only independent check recorded here (AQ-SPEC) tested three units of one model near Los Angeles in 2016-2017 and says nothing about current models, other climates or any individual sensor in the network

attestations.scope: Accuracy of the PurpleAir PA-II model against reference instruments (content/corroboration), three units

auth.how_to_get: Log in to the Developer Dashboard (https://develop.purpleair.com) with a Google or Google-associated email (otherwise email contact@purpleair.com) and create a READ key. WRITE keys are only for creating and deleting groups and members. Private sensors also need each sensor's read_key.
The same key may be sent as the api_key query-string parameter (or in a POST JSON body); the docs prefer the header.

endpoints.notes: Latest data from many sensors, by default every public sensor; no limit on the number of sensors per call. Use modified_since for repeated polling. Default rate limit 500 ms.

endpoints.notes: Also /history/csv. Default rate limit 1000 ms. Supply both timestamps to save points.

api.rate_limits: Per-endpoint default rate limits (100 ms for /keys, single sensor and most group calls; 400 ms for /groups; 500 ms for /sensors and group members; 1 s for history and /organization). Exceeding one returns RateLimitExceededError; PurpleAir can adjust limits per key on request. Every call also spends prepaid points; with too few points the API returns PaymentRequiredError. The Fair Use Policy lets PurpleAir throttle or disable keys used for scraping or unusually heavy use, and asks bulk historical requests (thousands of sensors) to go by email instead.

Owners on the same network can also read a sensor locally at its IP address /json without the API.

payment.notes: Points are prepaid and bought in the PurpleAir store (minimum $10), which uses Shopify. cards.name: Quest
cards.summary: Singapore-based local-task marketplace (Quest Hyphen Inc Pte. Ltd., also branded "Quest: Hire a Human") where a person, business or their AI agent posts a paid quest and nearby workers ("Heroes") send offers. It targets quick in-person tasks of under about 30 minutes: queue, collect or drop off, check whether a place is open or an item is in stock, photograph a shelf or location, mystery shop, run a short survey. An agent can post quests and browse open quests over a first-party remote MCP server with a Bearer API key; viewing offers, hiring, paying and approving completion are done by the person in the Quest app or on the website. Works in Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines, with San Francisco as an early US market.
cards.short: A local-task marketplace in Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines and San Francisco; agents post tasks over MCP.

tasks: check whether a place is open or an item is in stock
photograph a shelf or a location
verify a listing or a business address on site
mystery shopping with photos and a receipt
short in-person surveys and user tests
queue, collect or drop off an item, file paperwork
event and business help (flyers, display checks, booth slots)

pricing.model: the poster sets a budget in local currency and workers send offers; Quest takes 10% from the worker; a customer fee is described inconsistently (see notes)
pricing.unit: quest (price set by the poster, one-time or per hour)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published: each quest's price is set by the poster (whole units of SGD, MYR, PHP or USD; scopeOfReach global posts in USD) and can be negotiated. The agent pages say 'No fee to post or hire. Quest takes 10% from the human after each completed hire.' But the Terms charge the Citizen a Connection Fee on top of the Agreed Price when an offer is accepted, the FAQ says Quest charges 'a fixed booking fee + processing fees to customer upon payment', and the home page says the customer pays 'a small, transparent service fee shown before you confirm'. The fee amount is not published. postQuest can return 'maximum price exceeded' with a maxPrice ceiling. Boost and Priority (Highlights/Notifications Blast) are optional paid upgrades; the FAQ says premium features are available on quests from $30. Cancellation: the party responsible pays a cancellation fee (10% of the quest price for a Hero; the Citizen forfeits the service fee).

latency.typical: Not published; offers usually arrive within hours, and the work happens at the date and time window the poster sets
latency.notes: Quest's blog says that over the last 180 days every one of 25,741 posts got at least one offer (2.5 on average) and that 'most tasks start receiving offers within hours of posting'. That is time to an offer, not to delivery. The person must then pick an offer and pay in the app or on the website, since the MCP server cannot hire yet. postQuest takes dueDate (exact, before or range) and a timeRange, plus an optional urgent flag; new posts are moderated ('pending: posted, being checked, then shown to humans').

coverage.notes: Provider: 'Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines, with San Francisco as our early US market. Availability varies by area.' The home page claims 750k+ humans and '10+ countries', and the Terms carry country terms for further markets (AU, CA, HK, ID, JP, KR, PK, TH), but the agent docs name only these four markets. Worker counts are sign-ups, not verified local availability. San Francisco is coded as US-CA because ISO 3166 has no city codes.

licensing.summary: Terms (last updated April 2026) contain no assignment of rights in a Hero's work to the Citizen, and the Model Quest Contract is silent on ownership. Users grant Quest an unrestricted, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, reproduce, modify and adapt content posted on the platform for publishing it, providing the service and promoting Quest. The Terms also say: 'any content (whether provided by Quest, a User or a third party) on the Quest Platform may not be used on third party sites or for other business purposes without Quest's prior written permission.' Proof photos are sent in Quest chat, so whether that clause covers them is not stated. Neither the Terms nor the Privacy Policy mention AI or machine-learning training or resale.

human.method: Guidelines require real names matching an official identification document; optional account verification on the profile page (Singapore only, per the FAQ); Identity Verification Services include phone verification, payment-information verification, social-media links and badges; ratings and reviews. Marketing pages say sensitive work is background-checked.
human.unknown: The Terms say Quest 'does not undertake any investigation' of Heroes (no criminal, licence or character checks), that its verification 'may not be fully accurate', and that badges are point-in-time checks. Outside Singapore account verification is not available. What 'background-checked' covers and who does it is not stated.

application.unknown: Proof is sent through Quest chat in the app or website; no app or device attestation is documented.

camera.unknown: Nothing says proof photos must be taken live with the device camera; gallery uploads, edited images or photos of a screen are not addressed.

time.unknown: No trusted capture time is documented for proof; the chat message time is all a poster sees.

location.unknown: The Privacy Policy says the app may collect precise device location, but no check that proof was captured at the quest address is documented.

content.method: The poster states what done looks like (a photo, a receipt, a short message), reviews it and releases the held payment; Quest support mediates disputes and cancellations.
content.unknown: Quest disclaims the truth and accuracy of user information; staged or fabricated proof is caught only by the poster's own review.

corroboration.unknown: No platform cross-check. A poster can ask for up to 20 humans per quest (numOffers), but independent captures would be buyer-arranged, not a provider guarantee.

auth.how_to_get: Sign in at hireahuman.quest, open https://hireahuman.quest/profile/api-keys, click Generate new key and copy it (shown once; registry example prefix qmcp_). Send as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. Revocable on the same page. OAuth is not supported yet.

endpoints.params: title, desc, startingCountry, dueDate, dueDateType [exact|before|range], timeRange, numberOfHours, numOffers (1-20), paymentRecurrence [one time payment|per hour], price (whole currency units), scopeOfReach [local|global]; optional startingAddress (required unless online), endingCountry, endingAddress, dateRangeEnd, requirements, screeningQuestions, additionalPurchasesPrice, priceNegotiable, urgent, portfolioLinkRequired
endpoints.notes: Posts a quest; returns {status, questID} with status pending, duplicate, maximum price exceeded (with maxPrice and currency), illegal-content, auto-delete, admin-delete or user-banned. Account and country come from the key. Nothing is paid: the person picks an offer and pays in the app or on the website.

endpoints.params: countryCode, category, subCategory, location [in-person|online], chosenLocations, lat, lng, radius (metres), sortOrder [nearby|price-min|price-max], minAmount, maxAmount (smallest currency unit), offset, currentPage
endpoints.notes: Browse open quests to check going rates; returns questID, title, price, district, countryCode, startingCountry, startingLocation, datePosted, dueDate and offerCount, with no poster personal details.

Returns userID, idMcpApiKey and calledAt for the key; a connection test, not order status. There is no MCP tool for offers, hiring, order status or fetching proof yet ('A hire tool is in development').

mcp.notes: Streamable HTTP only. Registry entry v1.0.0, published 2026-10-21, requires an Authorization header. Coming soon per the provider: hireHuman (pick an offer and fund the quest), manageQuest (chat, approve completion, rate) and OAuth for OAuth-only clients such as ChatGPT.

api.notes: Quest asks agents to confirm task, location, time and budget with their person before calling postQuest ('Real people will travel to do it') and to keep contact details out of descriptions. An agent operating a browser may also post, review offers, hire and pay on hireahuman.quest while signed in as its user, with the user's approval.

payment.notes: Credit or debit card (Visa or Mastercard) through Stripe, in the Quest app or on the website; PayNow is 'coming soon'. When the person accepts an offer, the Agreed Price is paid into Quest's Payment Account and held until they release it on completion. Over MCP an agent cannot hire or pay: 'Your user picks an offer and approves the payment.' Refunds go to the original card or as Stored Value.

requester.checks: Posters must be natural persons over 16 with a Quest account; the API key ties every quest to that account. Posts are moderated (postQuest can return illegal-content, auto-delete, admin-delete or user-banned). User Guidelines ban quests 'that may result in the invasion of personal privacy', including 'investigating and/or gathering personal information without the concerned individual's consent or knowledge', plus illegal, deceptive and cash-based quests.
requester.unknown: No identity check of posters is documented outside optional Singapore verification; whether moderation blocks a request to photograph or follow a specific person, as opposed to gathering their personal information, is not stated.

freshness.typical_age: Captured when the hired worker does the task, at the date and time window the poster sets
freshness.notes: No archive; proof is whatever the poster asks for in the quest description.

delivery.basis: No delivery time is published. Blog: 'Most tasks start receiving offers within hours of posting' (time to an offer, not to delivery); the poster sets the due date and time window.

sources.claim: What Quest is, task types (be there, go and look, show up for business), under about 30 minutes, MCP URL, Bearer key, no OAuth, three tools, hire/pay not over MCP, browser agents may hire with approval, no fee to post or hire, 10% from the human, Boost and Priority, coverage SG/MY/PH plus San Francisco

Ltd.

FAQ: account verification only in Singapore, card-only payment, 10% commission from heroes plus a fixed booking fee and processing fees to the customer, premium features from $30, cancellation and refund rules
Payments: Stripe card payments held until released by the Citizen, PayNow coming soon, dispute support

Cancellation policy: responsible Hero pays 10% of the quest price; responsible Citizen forfeits the service fee
Home page: 750k+ humans, 10+ countries, service fee shown before you confirm, sensitive work is background-checked, field-data examples (photograph store shelves, verify a business address)

cards.name: RentAHuman
cards.summary: Agent-first marketplace (launched February 2026) where an AI agent posts a paid bounty, picks or auto-accepts applicants, and pays from a prepaid wallet once the worker submits photo, video, text or link evidence. Callable through a REST API, a local MCP server (rentahuman-mcp) or a remote OAuth MCP server; an agent can sign up for a key over the API without a browser.

tasks: local inspection with photo evidence
physical field data collection
errands, pickups and deliveries
attend a place or event with timed selfie check-ins
photo/video/document upload collection
line standing (NYC, LA, SF, Toronto, Vancouver)
remote microtasks, research participation, human QA

pricing.model: poster sets the worker's pay (fixed or hourly) plus an 18% service fee
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 because there is no fixed price: the poster chooses the pay, and RentAHuman adds 18% on top (a $100 task costs $118). In-person bounties may have a location-specific minimum hourly pay (GET /api/bounties/location-minimum). Optional per-seat bonuses. Wallet top-ups $1-$10,000. Line standing is listed at $23.60/hour fees included (NYC, LA, SF, Toronto, Vancouver; book 12+ hours ahead).

latency.typical: Not guaranteed; set by the bounty's deadline and completion window
latency.notes: The provider states that 'a posted task is a request, not a booking. Local coverage and response times aren't guaranteed.' Posters can set deadline, completionWindowHours, startWindowMinutes, scheduledStartAt and a ghost response window. After submission the poster has a four-day review window; if they don't review, payment is not auto-released; RentAHuman's team reviews the proof. A rejection opens a 48-hour worker appeal.

coverage.notes: Public stats endpoint reported 872,945 humans available, 32,664 agents connected and 17,446 bounties total (2026-10-26); the public bounty list showed 49 live bounties that day, 17 of them in person (14 US, 1 each IN, JP, PH). Worker counts are self-registered sign-ups, not verified availability; the provider states local coverage and response times aren't guaranteed. Search by city/country is free via GET /api/humans. Users in countries under comprehensive US sanctions are excluded by the Terms.

licensing.summary: Terms (updated 2026-07-20): each user retains ownership of their User Content (bounties, uploaded photos, submissions) but grants RentAHuman a worldwide, perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable, transferable licence, including to develop, train and fine-tune AI/ML models and to build aggregated or de-identified datasets; no opt-out is stated. RentAHuman does not endorse, verify or guarantee User Content. The Terms do not say whether the poster receives ownership, exclusive rights, resale rights or AI-training rights in a worker's evidence.

human.method: Optional per bounty: identityRequired (account-level government ID verification) and linkedinVerifiedRequired; poster reviews applicant profiles and reviews
human.unknown: Off by default. ID-check vendor, pass rates and multi-account detection are not documented. Trade licences and insurance are explicitly not verified.

application.unknown: A mobile app exists (attendance tracking, per the Terms), but no app or device attestation is documented

camera.method: liveCaptureRequirement ('photo' or 'video') requires completion evidence captured live with the device camera; live video up to 60 s / 250 MiB
camera.unknown: Off by default. Whether browser camera capture can be fed by a virtual camera, or a screen be photographed, is not addressed.

time.method: Optional live selfie check-ins every 5-240 minutes during in-person shifts; poster sees each photo with server time
time.unknown: Whether the main completion evidence carries a trusted capture time, and whether timestamps are signed

location.method: Optional location-stamped check-ins with server-computed distance and flags, an attendance radius of 50-2000 m around the job site (default 150 m), and opt-in requirePreciseLocation, which lets the poster see each hired worker on a map after the worker accepts the notice in the app. The attendance list itself excludes worker coordinates.
location.unknown: Uses phone/browser location; GPS-spoofing resistance is not documented. Off by default, and completion evidence itself is not documented as location-stamped.

content.method: The poster (or the agent) reviews submitted evidence against completionCriteria and can request up to three rounds of changes; RentAHuman staff review only disputes
content.unknown: The platform says it does not verify User Content; staged or fabricated evidence is caught only by the poster's own review

corroboration.unknown: No platform cross-check. A poster could fund several seats (spotsAvailable) to get independent captures, but that is buyer-side, not a provider guarantee.

auth.how_to_get: Headless: POST https://rentahuman.ai/api/agents/signup with email, acceptTerms: true, country and city sends a 6-digit code; POST /api/agents/signup/verify with the code returns a rah_ key once. Or create keys (up to 25) at https://rentahuman.ai/account/api-keys, or sign up over x402 for $10 USDC (early access). Searching humans and listing bounties need no key.
The same rah_ account key sent as Authorization: Bearer (OpenAPI BearerAuth also accepts a Firebase ID token for a signed-in user); accepted on the REST API and the remote MCP endpoint.

Remote MCP at https://rentahuman.ai/api/mcp: OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE S256, dynamic client registration at /api/mcp/oauth/register, public clients (token auth none). mcp:tools is the full marketplace scope (smaller tool set than the local server); mcp:read is a read-only workspace (seven reading tools, no posting or payments).

endpoints.notes: Search public worker profiles; free, no key needed.
List public open bounties; no key needed.

Minimum hourly pay for an in-person location (no key; returns null when no configured area applies). POST /bounties with dryRun: true returns a preview with the funding total; GET /bounties/{id}/funding-quote prices a pending bounty.

endpoints.params: title, description, price, estimatedHours (required); completionCriteria, evidenceTypes [text|photo|video|link], liveCaptureRequirement, checkIns {enabled, intervalMinutes}, location {country, isRemoteAllowed, ...}, deadline, spotsAvailable, attendanceRadiusMeters, requirePreciseLocation, identityRequired, autoAccept, submissionMode, bonuses, dryRun, idempotencyKey
endpoints.notes: Docs require showing the dryRun preview and posting only after the account owner approves. Unfunded bounties come back as pending_deposit with a deposit_url.

Fetch one bounty. GET /bounties/{id}/applications lists applicants; PATCH /bounties/{id}/applications/{appId} accepts or rejects. Signed webhooks cover applications, submissions, messages, escrow and payments.
Evidence submitted by workers. PATCH /bounties/{id}/submissions/{submissionId} reviews it; GET /bounties/{id}/applications/dataset downloads all accepted uploads as a zip with manifest.json.
Attendance sessions (check-ins) for hired workers on in-person bounties.

api.notes: Terms allow AI agents through the API and MCP, provided automation does not pose as a human. Docs require showing the dryRun preview and posting only after an explicit yes, with an Idempotency-Key on writes.

freshness.notes: No archive. Live camera capture and check-ins are opt-in per bounty.
