cards.name: Umbra
cards.summary: Operator of a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation that images through clouds and at night. Its Canopy web app and REST API let you check feasibility, task a new Spotlight (5x5 km, 0.25-2 m) or Scan capture in a time window you set, track it, and download the delivered collect via STAC. Collects generally arrive 1-4 hours after the window closes. List prices start at $675 per 5x5 km scene at 1 m. Every Canopy registration goes through Umbra's regulatory review. Umbra also runs a public CC BY 4.0 open-data archive, but that is context only: here it is listed for new captures.

tasks: task a new SAR Spotlight capture centred on a point (default 5x5 km scene; 4x4 km, 10x10 km and Natural Footprint scene sizes if enabled for your organization; range resolution 0.25, 0.35, 0.5, 1 or 2 m; multilook 1/2/4/8 via the API)
task a new SAR Scan strip between two points 25-100 km apart (8 km swath; 2 m up to 100 km, 1 m up to 75 km, 0.5 m up to 50 km)
Extended Dwell collects (list-priced on umbra.space; not an imaging mode in the Canopy API, which offers SPOTLIGHT and SCAN)
feasibility check: get imaging opportunities for a location and time window before ordering
track task and collect status; cancel tasks that are still SCHEDULED, SUBMITTED, ACCEPTED or ACTIVE
deliver products: GEC (always), SICD, SIDD, CPHD, CRSD, DI_GIF, DI_TIF, plus STAC metadata; CSI products for 5x5 km Spotlight
push deliveries to a configured cloud destination (AWS S3 or Google Cloud Storage delivery configs)

pricing.model: per tasked collect, list price by imaging mode, scene size, resolution and number of looks
pricing.unit: per 5x5 km Spotlight scene (1 m, 1 look)
pricing.notes: From umbra.space/pricing and the Umbra Product Guide. Spotlight 5x5 km, 1 look: 1.0 m $675, 0.5 m $950, 0.35 m $1,750, 0.25 m $3,250; more looks raise it (e.g. 1.0 m 10-look $2,200; 0.25 m 3-look $4,900). Natural Footprint, 1 look: $1,500 (1 m) to $3,750 (0.25 m); processed to 10x10 km at no extra charge on request if the scene is large enough. Extended Dwell 5x5 km $4,750; CSI and SAR video +40% on list price. Scan by strip length: 2 m $1,250-$2,250, 1 m $2,500-$3,500, 0.5 m $4,000 (25-50 km). GEC, SICD, SIDD and JSON metadata are included; CPHD or CRSD add $250 each and switch a 5x5 km Spotlight to Natural Footprint pricing. Bistatic/multistatic: +100%. A 30-day Archive Withhold (keeps the new collect out of Umbra's archive) costs 200% of list price. Pricing is per collect; no minimum order was stated. The Canopy API has no price-quote endpoint. Fees are non-refundable under the Tasking Terms.

latency.typical: Delivered 1-4 hours after the end of your tasking window
latency.notes: Task Lifecycle Tutorial: the scheduler processes the task queue every 10 minutes, and collect delivery 'will generally happen 1-4 hours after the associated Task's windowEndAt has passed.' Capture happens inside the window you set (windowStartAt/windowEndAt); the scheduler biases to the earliest feasible time in the window. In the UI the window end is limited to 7 days ahead, and scheduling reaches about 7-8 days ahead (state vectors). Umbra says it is 'generally safe to submit Tasks up to three hours before the desired collection time'. Product Guide mean revisit: 4.71 h at the equator, 3.75 h at ±30°, 2.32 h at ±50°, 0.88 h at ±67°. If feasibility returns no opportunities, the docs say to resubmit with a longer window.

regions: Global (subject to orbit passes and restricted access areas)
coverage.notes: SAR sees through cloud and works at night. Any point or line can be requested; actual availability comes from the feasibility endpoint. Polar orbit (97.4°), ground range 170-1,100 km either side of the flight path. Restricted Access Areas (an API endpoint and a published GeoJSON list) block tasking: some areas need screening beyond standard KYC (ongoing conflict), some conflict with Umbra priorities, and some are limited by US regulation (e.g. resolution limits over Israel). Spotlight is 5x5 km by default; Natural Footprint is larger (commonly 7.5x11 to 16x10 km) if enabled. Scan swath is 8 km wide.

licensing.summary: The Satellite Tasking Services Terms and Conditions license all delivered Content under CC BY 4.0: content is 'licensed, not sold', and Umbra keeps all right, title and interest. Attribution is required, with the notice 'SAR-derived data © [YEAR] Umbra Lab, Inc.' on adapted material. Umbra's Licensing & Attribution page says customers may publish, resell at a profit without royalty, and sell derivative works. The Terms override CC BY where they conflict, e.g. US export controls and sanctions (no resale to embargoed countries). The Terms do not mention AI or machine-learning training. Per the Product Guide, new tasked collects enter Umbra's Archive Catalog (which Umbra sells) unless you buy a 30-day Archive Withhold at 200% of list price. Delivered content can be downloaded for 90 days after notice. The separate open-data archive on AWS is also CC BY 4.0.

human.unknown: Not applicable in the usual sense: captures are made by Umbra's own satellites, not individual people

application.unknown: No public description of signing or checksums that would prove delivered files are unmodified Umbra products; the STAC metadata documented has no checksum fields. Downloads come from pre-signed URLs on Umbra's STAC endpoint.

camera.method: Collects carry SAR metadata (platform/satelliteId, range resolution, looks, polarization, grazing, azimuth and squint angles); Umbra publishes satellite IDs with NORAD numbers. SICD/CPHD are standard NGA sensor-model formats.
camera.unknown: Sensor identity and parameters are operator-asserted metadata; no independent check documented. Not on the C2PA Conforming Products List.

time.method: STAC datetime is the centre of aperture; start_datetime and end_datetime are the first and last radar pulse, in UTC, inside the tasked window
time.unknown: How pulse times are measured and checked is not publicly documented, and nothing timestamps them independently

location.method: Collects carry footprint geometry (WGS 84); GEC is geocoded and ellipsoid-corrected; SICD includes sensor geometry. Umbra states 8 m CE90 absolute geolocation accuracy, and its automated QA includes a geolocation calibration check when calibration sites are collected.
location.unknown: The 8 m CE90 figure is a system specification, not a per-collect measurement; no public per-collect geolocation report

content.method: Limited warranty in the Tasking Terms that delivered Content will 'reasonably be of the area of interest as requested' and meet the Product Guide specs (replace or credit, claims within 30 days). Automated QA before delivery rejects blank, eclipsed or mispointed collects (status CORRUPT, task ANOMALY).
content.unknown: No public method for detecting manipulated or synthetic SAR imagery; QA checks image quality, not authenticity. Raw CPHD/CRSD lets an expert reprocess, but that is not an integrity guarantee.

corroboration.unknown: No documented cross-check against other sensors; a buyer could compare against other SAR or optical providers themselves

freshness.typical_age: Captured inside the window you set after ordering, delivered 1-4 hours after the window ends
freshness.notes: IRLpls lists Umbra for new tasked captures. For context only: Canopy also has a STAC archive catalog and archive-task ordering (priced at the equivalent list price), and Umbra publishes a CC BY 4.0 open-data archive on AWS (s3 umbra-open-data-catalog, us-west-2). Those are not the offering listed here.

auth.how_to_get: OAuth2 client credentials for scripts and services: an organization admin creates one shared client_id/client_secret on the Canopy Organization page (Authentication tab), then POSTs them to https://auth.canopy.umbra.space/oauth/token with audience https://api.canopy.umbra.space and grant_type client_credentials. Tokens last 86,400 s; token requests are limited to 50 per 24 h per client, so cache them. Use audience https://api.canopy.prod.umbra-sandbox.space for the sandbox. Needs an approved Canopy account.

Copy an access token from https://canopy.umbra.space/account (expires after 24 hours). For a sandbox token, switch on 'Test Mode' in the app header and call api.canopy.prod.umbra-sandbox.space; sandbox collects are not billable. No public account sign-up flow was found: the docs point to umbra.space/contact, and every registration is subject to Umbra's regulatory review.

endpoints.notes: Feasibility rather than price: returns id and status (RECEIVED/COMPLETED/ERROR). Poll until COMPLETED to read opportunities. Rate limit 2/s, 120/min, 3600/h.

endpoints.notes: Creates a new capture (billable). New tasks should move to SUBMITTED or REJECTED within minutes. No idempotency key is documented (userOrderId is a free label, searchable on collects). Rate limit 2/s, 120/min, 300/h. Check organization settings (GET /admin/organizations/settings) for the resolutions and products your organization may use.

Task status (RECEIVED, SUBMITTED, ACCEPTED, ACTIVE, SCHEDULED, TASKED, TRANSMITTED, INCOMPLETE, PROCESSING, PROCESSED, DELIVERING; terminal DELIVERED, REJECTED, CANCELED, ERROR, ANOMALY) and collectIds

endpoints.notes: Your organization's collects
GeoJSON FeatureCollection of places where tasking is disallowed for your organization

api.rate_limits: Per organization, rolling window: 25 reads/s and 5 writes/s on standard endpoints. Create Task and Cancel Task 2/s, 120/min, 300/h. Create Feasibility 2/s, 120/min, 3600/h. Client-credentials token requests 50 per 24 h per client. Limits may change.
api.notes: No RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata: api.canopy.umbra.space returns 401 on /.well-known paths. auth.canopy.umbra.space publishes RFC 8414 metadata with no registration endpoint.

delivery.basis: Canopy Task Lifecycle Tutorial: collect delivery 'will generally happen 1-4 hours after the associated Task's windowEndAt has passed'. Total time also depends on the tasking window you set and on feasibility; Umbra says tasks can generally be submitted up to three hours before the desired collection time.

payment.notes: Billing Terms: self-service Snapshot orders put a hold on a credit card or ACH account at checkout and charge it on delivery; Subscriptions are billed monthly for collects delivered. Enterprise accounts pre-commit to a volume, draw down a shared credit and are invoiced monthly, net 30. The Tasking Terms also allow check or wire transfer, in USD. Fees are non-refundable. No agent payment rail is documented.

requester.checks: Tasking Terms: every Canopy registration is subject to regulatory review by Umbra or a third party, and Umbra may refuse anyone. Customers must represent they are not on US sanctions or export-control lists and must provide compliance documents on request. Restricted Access Areas need screening beyond standard KYC.
requester.unknown: What the regulatory review and KYC check in practice, and how long approval takes, is not published

cards.name: UP42
cards.short: One business account to order new satellite, aerial and drone captures from about 20 operators.
cards.summary: Geospatial marketplace for registered businesses. 25 tasking collections are integrated in the API (Vantor WorldView, Airbus Pléiades/Pléiades Neo/SPOT/TerraSAR-X, BlackSky Gen-2/Gen-3, Planet, Satellogic, Pixxel, Wyvern, Umbra, Capella, ICEYE, KOMPSAT, EROS-C, GEOSAT, GÖKTÜRK-1, Beijing-3, AxelGlobe), with validate, estimate, opportunities, feasibility and quotation steps; SatVu, Globhe drones and some others are non-integrated and ordered through the Operations team. Paid in prepaid credits (100 = €1).

tasks: list collections (keyless) and order-form JSON schemas
validate and estimate a catalog or tasking order before buying
list tasking opportunities (sensor passes) for an AOI
check whether a tasking order needs a feasibility study
place tasking orders; choose feasibility options and accept quotations
track order status and coverage; request acquisition window extensions
search delivered assets via STAC and create download URLs

pricing.model: prepaid credits, 100 credits = €1, minimum purchase 10,000 credits (€100); credits expire after 24 months
pricing.notes: Not published in USD. Priced by AOI size, resolution, collection, acquisition mode, tasking priority and cloud cover; an estimate is given before purchase and a high-difficulty acquisition may carry a price uplift. Floors: BlackSky tasking from 17,500 credits (€175)/scene; minimum charges 1 scene (BlackSky, Planet, Satellogic, SatVu, Umbra, Capella, ICEYE, KOMPSAT-5, StriX, TerraSAR-X), 25 km² (Vantor VNIR, GEOSAT 2), 100 km² (Pléiades, Pléiades Neo, SPOT, Pixxel, Dragonette-1), 1 km² (Globhe drone). 5% bonus credits on purchases of 1,000,000+ credits. Credits are non-refundable; tasking shortfalls past the window are refunded pro rata on request.

latency.typical: days; depends on collection, feasibility study and priority
latency.notes: Minimum lead time 0 days (BlackSky, Umbra) or 1-3 days, and minimum acquisition window 1 day (BlackSky, Capella, ICEYE, Umbra, Vantor) up to 30 days (Dragonette-1). Where a feasibility study is needed it takes 1-5 business days (Sep-May) or 3-10 (Jun-Aug). Collection access requests are reviewed in up to 3 working days; the initial compliance check usually takes 1 business day. UP42 can't say when a capture attempt will be made.

regions: Global (per collection coverage and restriction maps)
coverage.notes: Collections are described as acquired worldwide, subject to each collection's coverage and restriction maps; many tasking collections need an access request that the data provider can reject based on the organisation or use case.

licensing.summary: Data is licensed, not sold: the buyer does not acquire ownership (Terms of Purchase 5.1-5.2; Platform Services Agreement 13.2). Use is set by each provider's EULA, accepted before the first order and downloadable only after login; UP42 says most are non-transferable, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive and revocable. Original data is for internal use; external use and redistribution are usually not allowed, while derivative products can usually be shared. UP42's docs answer 'Can I resell the data I ordered?' with 'No'. AI or ML training is not addressed in the public terms or docs.

human.unknown: Satellite, aircraft and drone operators capture; no person is attested.

application.unknown: No signing, checksum or provenance scheme for delivered files is documented.

camera.method: Each delivery is tied to a named collection, sensor and data product in its order and STAC metadata.
camera.unknown: The sensor is named in operator metadata; nothing lets a buyer check it independently.

time.method: STAC items carry the acquisition datetime from the operator's metadata.
time.unknown: Acquisition time comes from operator metadata and is not signed or independently time-stamped.

location.method: Positional accuracy is published per collection (e.g. BlackSky Gen-3 tasking < 10 m CE90 absolute); deliveries are AOI-georeferenced.
location.unknown: Accuracy is the operator's specification and is not checked per delivery; some collections list it as unknown.

content.unknown: No manipulation detection is documented; buyers can report quality issues within 7 days of delivery for investigation with the provider.

corroboration.unknown: No independent confirmation of deliveries is documented.

freshness.typical_age: Tasking: captured inside your acquisition window
freshness.notes: The same account also buys archive (catalog) imagery, which irlpls does not match.

delivery.basis: Acquisition time frames page: minimum lead time 0-3 days and minimum acquisition window 1-30 days by collection; actual time frames are set by the feasibility study, and UP42 can't give a specific capture date.

auth.how_to_get: Free sign-up at up42.com, upgraded to the free Professional plan with your organisation's details. Tokens come from the OAuth2 password grant (client_id up42-api) with your console email and password, last 5 minutes, and are sent as 'Authorization: Bearer'. To order: add tax info and a company card, buy credits (first purchase triggers a compliance check), request access to restricted collections and accept each EULA.

cards.name: USGS earthquake feed
cards.summary: The U.S. Geological Survey's real-time earthquake feeds list new seismic events worldwide (magnitude, location, depth, time, automatic or reviewed status, tsunami flag, PAGER alert) as GeoJSON updated every minute, free and with no key. Events come from the ANSS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat), which merges solutions from seismic networks around the world. The FDSN event web service filters by time, place, radius, magnitude, alert level and review status.

tasks: earthquakes in the past hour, day, week or 30 days, by magnitude threshold (significant, 4.5+, 2.5+, 1.0+, all)
query earthquake events near a point (latitude, longitude, maxradiuskm) or in a box since a given time, above a magnitude
filter by PAGER alert level (green, yellow, orange, red), review status (automatic or reviewed), significance, felt reports or depth
event detail: magnitude, depth, place, time, status automatic/reviewed, felt reports, tsunami flag, PAGER alert level, and associated products such as ShakeMap, DYFI and moment tensors
watch for new or revised earthquakes by polling a feed, or the query service with updatedafter

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: No fee and no key.

latency.typical: USGS FAQ: about 2.5 minutes on average after an earthquake in California, typically within 8 minutes elsewhere in the US, about 20 minutes on average outside the US
latency.notes: The GeoJSON summary feeds are labelled 'Updated every minute'. Per the same FAQ, GeoJSON feeds of 7 days or less are cached for 1 minute, other 7-day-or-less feeds for 5 minutes, and 30-day feeds and searches for 15 minutes, which adds to the delay. A query response on 2026-10-26 carried Cache-Control: public, max-age=60.

coverage.notes: Worldwide. ComCat merges solutions from seismic networks around the world (contributors include US regional networks and agencies in many other countries). USGS says the network is densest in California and sparse in some areas outside the US, so small events abroad are less complete and slower to post.

licensing.summary: USGS says USGS-authored or produced data and information are in the U.S. Public Domain and asks for credit (e.g. 'Credit: U.S. Geological Survey'); not everything on USGS sites is public domain, and copyrighted third-party material needs the holder's permission. USGS gives no warranty of accuracy, completeness or usefulness. Events and products contributed to ComCat by non-USGS networks were not checked separately. The terms do not mention AI training or resale.

freshness.typical_age: Minutes after an event for the real-time feeds; the query service also reaches back through the catalog
freshness.notes: Early values are automatic and are revised as networks and analysts refine them; the 'updated' field changes when they do. Events can also be deleted (the query service returns HTTP 409 for a deleted event unless includedeleted is set).

auth.how_to_get: No key needed.

endpoints.params: level: significant, 4.5, 2.5, 1.0, all; period: hour, day, week, month
endpoints.notes: GeoJSON FeatureCollection, 'Updated every minute'; properties include mag, place, time, updated, status, tsunami, alert, felt, sig, net, ids, sources, nst, dmin, rms, gap, magType, url, detail. USGS recommends these feeds for automated applications.

endpoints.params: eventid, e.g. aka2026vgpxtq (the 'detail' URL in each summary feature)
endpoints.notes: One event with its associated products (origin, phase-data, and where available shakemap, losspager, dyfi, moment-tensor).

endpoints.params: format=geojson (default quakeml; also csv, kml, text, xml); starttime (default now - 30 days), endtime, updatedafter; minlatitude/maxlatitude/minlongitude/maxlongitude or latitude, longitude, maxradiuskm; minmagnitude, maxmagnitude; mindepth, maxdepth; alertlevel, minalertlevel; reviewstatus (automatic, reviewed); eventtype; orderby (time, time-asc, magnitude, magnitude-asc); limit (1-20000); offset; eventid
endpoints.notes: FDSN Event Web Service. Queries over 20,000 events return HTTP 400. Keyless radius query near Ridgecrest, CA returned automatic 'ci' events on 2026-10-26.

endpoints.params: same parameters as query; format=geojson or text or xml
endpoints.notes: Counts matching events; returned {"count":459,"maxAllowed":20000} for starttime=2026-10-25 on 2026-10-26.

endpoints.params: none
endpoints.notes: Contributing networks; /fdsnws/event/1/catalogs lists catalogs, /fdsnws/event/1/application.json lists enumerated parameter values.

api.rate_limits: None published. The query service caps a request at 20,000 events. USGS asks automated applications to use the real-time GeoJSON feeds rather than the query service whenever possible.
api.sdk: USGS lists libcomcat (Python), matcomcat (Matlab) and an R comcat package on its ANSS Developer's Corner.

application.unknown: No signing of feed contents; integrity rests on USGS and contributing-network operations

camera.unknown: No imagery

time.unknown: Origin time is an estimate that can be revised; per-event timing uncertainty is not in the summary feed

location.method: Each event carries an estimated epicentre and depth, with solution-quality fields (nst stations used, gap azimuthal gap, dmin distance to nearest station, rms residual)

content.unknown: Automatic magnitudes and locations can change substantially after review, and events can be deleted

corroboration.method: The 'ids' and 'sources' fields list every contributing network whose solution was associated with the event. Where networks disagree, ComCat picks a preferred product by weight, favouring the network authoritative for the region; the other solutions stay available in the detail feed.

cards.name: USGS stream gauges
cards.summary: U.S. Geological Survey network of automated stream gauges reporting gage height, discharge and other water parameters, served free through the modernized Water Data OGC API (api.waterdata.usgs.gov). It supersedes the legacy WaterServices APIs, which USGS will retire during its final decommission campaign (November 2026 to February 2027, completing in Q1 2027). About 1,400 USGS river cameras at gauge sites also publish still images every few minutes to every hour through the public NIMS API.

tasks: gage height / stage (parameter 00065)
streamflow discharge (parameter 00060)
water temperature (parameter 00010)
latest observation per time series
historical continuous and daily values
field and channel measurements used to check the sensors
find gauges near a point or in a bounding box
river camera stills (USGS NIMS / HIVIS; capture interval set per camera, from 2 to 60 minutes, some daylight only)

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: No fee is charged. The API key is free (managed by api.data.gov, emailed on sign-up) and only raises rate limits. USGS says anyone making more than a few queries per hour needs a key. Keyless requests returned data on 2026-10-26.

latency.typical: About 15-60 minutes behind real time for typical gauges (15-minute recording, roughly hourly transmission)
latency.notes: USGS FAQ: real-time streamflow is typically recorded at 15-minute intervals, stored on site and transmitted to USGS once an hour, depending on the relay technique. Live checks on 2026-10-26 at 04:55 UTC (27 Oct): USGS-01646500 (Potomac) had its newest discharge value at 03:50 UTC, last modified 03:57 UTC, about 65 minutes old. USGS-01650800 had a value at 04:45 UTC, about 10 minutes old.

regions: United States, including Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands
coverage.notes: Only existing fixed gauges; you cannot request a new gauge. The monitoring-locations collection also includes non-USGS agency sites (e.g. a USEPA site in a Washington DC bbox query), not all of which have continuous data. Some sites are discontinued and return null values with a DISCONTINUED qualifier. Live checks on 2026-10-26 found same-day readings in Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands; American Samoa's newest continuous reading was from 2008. River cameras: 1,394 listed in the NIMS API (1,152 not hidden) across most states plus Puerto Rico and Guam. Total gauge count not verified.

licensing.summary: The API's OpenAPI description gives its licence as 'US Government work in the public domain', linking to CC0 1.0. It also links CC0 as the terms of service. USGS says USGS-authored data are U.S. Public Domain and asks for credit (e.g. 'Credit: U.S. Geological Survey'). Not every item on USGS sites is public domain: some third-party images are copyrighted and need the holder's permission. Recent data are provisional and provided on the condition that neither USGS nor the U.S. Government is liable for damages. The terms do not mention AI training or resale. Licensing of non-USGS agency data in the API was not checked.

freshness.notes: latest-continuous returns the most recent value per time series; continuous returns full sensor history. Each value carries approval_status: recent values are 'Provisional' and may be substantially revised after field inspections and measurements.

auth.how_to_get: No key needed for light use. USGS says you need a key for more than a few queries per hour.
Optional and free: sign up at https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov/signup (an api.data.gov key, sent by email) for higher rate limits.
The same free key, passed as the api_key query parameter.

Properties: time_series_id, monitoring_location_id, parameter_code, statistic_id, time, value (string), unit_of_measure, approval_status, qualifier, last_modified. Any response property is queryable (see /queryables). Paginate via the 'next' link.

endpoints.notes: Manual discharge and gage-height measurements USGS uses to check and correct automated records; latest-field-measurements and channel-measurements also exist.

endpoints.notes: LEGACY Instantaneous Values service, no key; still answered on 2026-10-26. USGS is retiring WaterServices in its final decommission campaign (November 2026 to February 2027, Q1 2027), which may include intentional degradation and blackouts. Use the OGC API. IP blocks (403) for excessive use.

api.rate_limits: No numbers published for keyless use. USGS says more than a few queries per hour needs a key. Keys give higher limits; going over returns HTTP 429. The X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining response headers report the limit (the docs example shows 1000), but a keyless response on 2026-10-26 carried no such headers. The legacy service blocks IPs (403) for excessive use.

camera.unknown: River camera stills come from fixed USGS-installed cameras at gauge sites; no capture signing or tamper evidence is documented, so whether a frame is unaltered rests on trust in USGS operations.

time.unknown: Each value has an observation time and last_modified timestamp, but how logger clocks are set or checked was not found in docs read

location.method: Fixed sites with published coordinates plus horizontal positional accuracy and method fields in monitoring-locations (e.g. 'Interpolated from map', 'Mapping grade GPS unit')
location.unknown: Accuracy varies by site and many coordinates are interpolated from maps; the fields are agency-entered, not independently attested

content.method: Improbable values relayed by telemetry are automatically screened until verified. Values carry approval_status (Provisional or Approved) and qualifiers. USGS states provisional data may be inaccurate due to instrument malfunctions or site changes and may be substantially revised after field inspections and measurements.
content.unknown: Provisional values (the freshest ones) can be substantially wrong; the screening rules and review procedure were not read in detail

corroboration.method: Field measurements and channel measurements collections expose the manual readings USGS uses to check and correct automated records
corroboration.unknown: How often a given gauge is field-checked, and how far provisional values drift before correction, was not established

cards.name: Vangrid
cards.short: Pay a USDC bounty by x402 and a contributor films a place; you get the video and a 3D model.
cards.summary: Vangrid runs a bounty board for ground-level video captures of real places. An agent posts a bounty in one HTTP call, paying the amount in USDC on Base or Arc through x402 with no account or API key; contributors with the Vangrid capture app film it, the agent reviews watermarked previews and accepts one, and receives the full capture plus a textured 3D model (GLB). Every capture is fingerprinted (content sha256, coarse geohash, timestamp) and the fingerprints are committed in Merkle trees whose roots are attested on Base through EAS, so anyone can check that a capture's hash existed by the end of its window. Faces, plates and bodies are blurred on the device. Pay-per-request endpoints also return metadata for captures already anchored.

tasks: walk-around video capture of a specific place (loading dock, forecourt, junction, building, stock room)
3D reconstruction of the accepted capture as a textured GLB mesh
ground-level spatial data for robotics, mapping and world models
lookup of already-anchored captures by area and time window (metadata only)
free provenance check of a capture's sha256 against its Base anchor

delivery.basis: Agent bounty docs: 'A person has to go and film, so this takes hours or days.' Deadline 1 to 30 days (default 7); reconstruction after acceptance 'typically takes 30 minutes or more'.

latency.typical: Hours to days for a contributor to film; then 30+ minutes of reconstruction after you accept
latency.notes: The bounty is posted to the board within a minute of payment. Submissions arrive when a contributor goes and films; nothing guarantees anyone will. The deadline is 1 to 30 days (default 7); after it, or on cancel while open, the full amount is refunded on the network it was paid on. Accepting is final.

freshness.typical_age: Usually filmed after the bounty is posted, but a contributor may submit a clip captured earlier
freshness.notes: The bounties guide says a contributor can 'Record a new one, or use a clip you have already captured.' Submissions show submitted_at, not capture time; the capture time is in the anchored fingerprint, checkable with the free provenance endpoint. The pay-per-request index returns metadata (sha256, geohash, capture time, anchor) of existing captures, not media.

pricing.model: bounty (escrowed USDC, set by the buyer)
pricing.notes: The buyer sets amount_usdc in whole USDC; the server's default minimum and maximum are 50 and 5,000 (quoted in the discovery metadata). The amount is escrowed on chain and released on acceptance: Vangrid keeps a 10% platform fee and about $5 for reconstruction and pays the rest to the contributor (a $50 reward pays $40). Reconstruction is included; no second payment. Full refund on cancel while open or on expiry. Pay-per-request data: $0.01 per spatial query, $0.005 per observation, provenance check free; prices are quoted per request and can change. Enterprise API pricing is by quote.

payment.notes: Agents pay through x402 v2 (exact scheme) in USDC on Base (eip155:8453) or Arc (eip155:5042); the 402 quote lists both and the transfer settles before the bounty is created. No gas needed on Base. People post on the web board by funding the escrow from a wallet. The amount is escrowed up front and refunded to the paying wallet on cancel or expiry. Enterprise pilots are priced by contract.

coverage.notes: Coverage follows contributors: densest in metro areas, sparser elsewhere. The Terms say the service is not offered to residents of Illinois, Texas and Washington (USA), Germany, France, Italy, mainland China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba and Crimea, and uploads are blocked in some regions by capture location and network region. Contributors may not capture private property, home or vehicle interiors, schools, playgrounds, healthcare, places of worship, military or critical-infrastructure perimeters, or identifiable minors. A public explorer tree from 2026-09-24 listed captures from cities on several continents (e.g. Istanbul, Atlanta, Amsterdam, Nairobi, Sydney, Jakarta, Tokyo).

licensing.summary: The Terms say contributors keep ownership of their captures and grant Vangrid a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, sublicensable, transferable licence to process, distribute and commercialise them and their derivatives. What licence the bounty buyer receives is not stated. The Privacy Policy says Vangrid processes captures to train spatial models and may license filtered datasets to defense, robotics, world-model and AI labs, and infrastructure operators, so a commissioned capture is not exclusive.

requester.checks: None documented for buyers: there is no account and no API key; an agent pays from any wallet, gets a one-time agent_token, and Vangrid posts the title and brief to the board from its operator wallet within a minute. The rules sit with contributors: the Terms forbid capturing private spaces, identifiable minors and sensitive sites, and ban harassing or stalking any person.
requester.unknown: Whether briefs are screened before posting, and how a request to film a specific person would be refused, is not stated.

auth.how_to_get: x402 v2: call without payment, read the 402 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header, sign an exact USDC authorization on Base or Arc and retry. No account or key; needs a wallet holding USDC.
The agent_token (vgb_...) returned once by POST /bounties; it is the only credential for that bounty's status, accept and cancel calls.
GET /provenance/{hash} is free and needs no payment or token.

endpoints.params: title (3-200 chars), brief (20-4000 chars), amount_usdc (integer; default range 50-5000), deadline_days (1-30, default 7)
endpoints.notes: Paid by x402: the price is exactly amount_usdc, settled before processing. Returns bounty_id, agent_token (once), poll_url.

endpoints.params: Authorization: Bearer <agent_token>
endpoints.notes: Free. Status (paid, open, accepting, accepted, cancelling, cancelled, expired, expired_refunded, failed), onchain_id, board_url, transactions, and submissions with watermarked preview_url (15 min) and quality_status pass/fail.

endpoints.params: Authorization: Bearer <agent_token>
endpoints.notes: After POST /bounties/{id}/accept {submission_id} (free, final, releases the escrow), the accepted submission carries full_capture_url, model_glb_url and model_zip_url as signed links valid 15 minutes. POST /bounties/{id}/cancel refunds while open.

endpoints.params: aoi (GeoJSON Point with radius_m 1-5000, or Polygon up to 100 km2), from, to, limit (1-1000)
endpoints.notes: $0.01 by x402. Returns already-anchored captures: sha256, 6-character geohash, captured_at and Base anchor. No media.

endpoints.params: id = capture sha256
endpoints.notes: $0.005 by x402. One anchored observation. GET /provenance/{hash} answers the same check for free.

mcp.auth: x402 from a local wallet (EVM_PRIVATE_KEY), with MAX_USD_PER_CALL and MAX_USD_PER_BOUNTY caps
mcp.notes: Open-source (MIT) stdio server github.com/vangrid-labs/bounty-mcp, run with npx -y github:vangrid-labs/bounty-mcp. Tools: vangrid_post_bounty, vangrid_bounty_status, vangrid_accept_submission, vangrid_cancel_bounty, vangrid_coverage_query, vangrid_observation, vangrid_verify_provenance. Accept and cancel are free and irreversible and not covered by the spend caps. Not in the official MCP Registry.

api.notes: Discovery: an x402 manifest at https://data.vangrid.io/.well-known/x402 lists the paid resources, networks and payTo address. A separate Enterprise Spatial API (api.vangrid.io/v1, bearer API keys, spatial query, ingest, streaming) is granted per pilot by contacting sales.

human.unknown: Contributors sign in with a wallet and need an invite code to upload; no identity check is documented, and buyers see no contributor identity.

application.method: Captures are recorded in the Vangrid capture app (browser or Android) and checked at ingest for quality, length, camera/location consistency and duplicates.
application.unknown: Vangrid says hardware-backed device attestation is 'not live yet' and that the fingerprint 'says nothing about the device that produced it'.

camera.method: Recorded through the app's camera; the Terms ban fabricated, manipulated, staged or AI-generated content; ingest rejects duplicates.
camera.unknown: No signed capture or C2PA; Vangrid is not on the C2PA conforming products list, so nothing proves the video came from a real sensor rather than a screen or generator.

time.method: Each capture's fingerprint (content sha256, coarse geohash, timestamp) is a leaf in a Merkle tree whose root is attested on Base through EAS when its window closes. Anyone can recompute the root from the leaf's published proof and compare it with the on-chain attestation, with no call to Vangrid; a free endpoint also answers per sha256.
time.unknown: This proves the capture's hash existed no later than the anchor (windows of about 15 to 35 minutes); the capture time inside the fingerprint is device-reported. A bounty submission may be a clip filmed before the bounty was posted, and the bounty API does not state that full_capture_url hashes to the anchored sha256, so the buyer must hash it and check.

location.method: Location is optional; when given it is checked for consistency with camera signals at ingest, and a 6-character geohash (about 1.2 km by 0.6 km) is anchored in the fingerprint.
location.unknown: The anchored location is device-reported and coarse; GPS/motion cross-correlation against spoofing is 'not live yet', and some bounties may receive captures with no location at all.

content.method: Automated quality check per submission (quality_status pending/pass/fail); the buyer reviews a watermarked preview against the brief before accepting one.
content.unknown: The automated check covers quality and length, not whether the clip shows the place in the brief; that judgment is the buyer's.

corroboration.unknown: A bounty delivers one contributor's capture. Independent verifiers under collateral are 'not live yet'; the multi-view ground_truth_score described for the enterprise query API is not part of bounty delivery.

sources.claim: Tagline 'Sovereign data rail for real-time ground truth, enabling world models and autonomous systems'

Agent bounty API: no account or key; x402 on Base or Arc; POST /bounties fields and ranges (default 50-5000 USDC, deadline 1-30 days); agent_token bearer; statuses; preview and model links valid 15 min; quality_status; accept/cancel; full refund; 'hours or days'; MCP tools

Bounties: 10% platform fee and ~$5 reconstruction from the reward; GLB mesh; reconstruction 30+ min; escrow in USDC on Base; full refund; contributors may submit a previously captured clip; only a dataset hash goes on chain
Pay-per-request: $0.01 spatial query, $0.005 observation, free provenance; 6-character geohash (~1.2 x 0.6 km); EAS anchor fields; OpenAPI and x402 manifest; MCP server setup
OpenAPI 1.0.0: seven endpoints, x402 PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and agentToken bearer security schemes, server data.vangrid.io
x402 manifest: paid resources (spatial query, observation, bounties), networks eip155:8453 and eip155:5042

Verification: live ingest checks (quality, camera/location consistency, duplicates), capture fingerprint, Merkle root anchored on Base; device attestation, sensor cross-correlation and independent verification not live
Public explorer of anchored Merkle trees, leaves and inclusion proofs (latest tree attested 2026-10-27 UTC)
Sample check: provenance endpoint returned verified=true for capture cf9642...4a48 (tree 4145, captured 2026-09-24T06:31:34Z)
Sample tree 4145 leaves and proofs; the leaf's 11-node proof recomputes (keccak256, sorted pairs) to the attested root

cards.name: WeGoLook
cards.summary: On-demand field workers ('Lookers') who go to a vehicle, property or site and capture photos, video and checklist answers in the WeGoLook app. A public order portal sells fixed-price vehicle inspections (auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft) from $99; insurers and other enterprises buy custom workflows by contract. WeGoLook is a Crawford & Company subsidiary (Crawford bought 85 percent in January 2017) and also powers Crawford's alternative claims inspections.
cards.short: Sends a local inspector to photograph and video a vehicle or property; online vehicle inspections from $99.

tasks: vehicle inspection ordered online: auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft
VIN and damage verification
working demonstration and walk-around video
auto and fleet claims inspection
non-complex property inspection
roof and interior/exterior property inspection (Crawford AIS network)
vacant land inspection
underwriting and real estate portfolio inspection
notice delivery and product recall checks
notarized document looks
self-service looks (customer or employee collected)
custom workflow integrations

pricing.model: fixed price per online inspection; enterprise by quote
pricing.notes: The public order portal lists Instant Inspection - Auto at a base price of $99, with add-ons: working demonstration and exterior walk-around videos $35, three-day rush delivery $35, two-day rush delivery $50. The same five vehicle products (auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft) are listed. Enterprise and claims work (Standard, Self-Service and Custom Looks) has no public price. Looker pay, per the app store listings, is mostly $15-$25 per Look.

latency.typical: About 1.6 days to first inspection on average, against a two-day SLA (2022 claims brochure); rush delivery in two or three days can be bought online
latency.notes: The 2022 brochure also gives 38 minutes average time to first contact and 11.2 miles average Looker distance. The order portal sells three-day and two-day rush delivery as paid add-ons, so standard online delivery is slower than three days, but the standard window is not stated. Crawford says many of its services can be delivered 'as rapidly as same day'. App store listings say most Looks take under an hour on site.

coverage.notes: Over 45,000 Lookers claimed. cards.name: Windy Webcams
cards.short: A directory of public webcams worldwide, with current images through an API.
cards.summary: Large global directory of public webcams run by third-party operators, with a REST API (v3) to find webcams near a point or in a bounding box and get current image URLs, live/timelapse player embeds and location metadata.

tasks: current still image of a place from a fixed public webcam
find webcams within a radius (up to 250 km) or bounding box
live stream / daily, monthly, yearly timelapse player embeds
visual check of weather, snow, sea state, crowds or traffic at a camera's view

pricing.model: freemium (free tier plus annual professional subscription)
pricing.unit: free tier; Professional 9,990 EUR per year
pricing.notes: Free tier: limited image size, image URLs valid for a short time (15 minutes on the pricing page, 10 minutes in the docs), pagination offset capped at 1000; images must be linked to windy.com or shown via the embeddable timelapse player, which may carry Windy ads. Professional: 9,990 EUR per year, paid annually in advance and auto-renewing; full-size images, image URLs valid 24 hours, offset up to 10,000, no ads in the timelapse player, and an all-webcams export in one call. No USD price published. The free tier may not be offered only inside the paid part of a user's app.

latency.typical: Returned on request; the image is the camera's most recent upload, its age shown by lastUpdatedOn
latency.notes: No per-camera refresh interval is published. Windy defines an Active Webcam as one updated within the last 24 hours, so an active camera's image can still be hours old. Docs recommend calling the webcams endpoint on every page load because image URL tokens expire (10 minutes free per the docs, 15 minutes per the pricing page; 24 hours professional). Windy does not guarantee the number of active webcams, the availability of any webcam, or image quality.

regions: Global (wherever webcams are registered; dense in Europe and tourist/ski/coastal areas, uneven elsewhere)
coverage.notes: Only existing webcams with fixed views; you cannot point or add a camera on request. Windy calls it 'the largest collection of webcams worldwide'; Windy staff: '70 000+' webcams (2026-05-28). Filters by country, region, city, continent and 18 categories (airport, beach, building, city, coast, forest, indoor, lake, landscape, meteo, mountain, observatory, port, river, sportArea, square, traffic, village). Terms describe webcams as mounted outdoors to monitor the general natural environment.

licensing.summary: Specific Terms of Use of the Windy Webcams API (effective 1 Sept 2023) govern and prevail over the general terms. They forbid redistributing any part of the API or its data to third parties, further redistributing the Content, giving third parties access to the API or your key, letting third parties build services on it, publishing any graphics displaying webcam images, stretching images, using image URLs other than those the API returns, continuous scanning of many webcams or downloading significant parts of image history, intensive automated use of any endpoint, and trying to identify people in the images. Users must visibly credit 'Webcams provided by windy.com - add new webcam' with links. Copyright stays with Windy and its suppliers (the webcam operators). General Windy terms add: no selling, renting or sublicensing Content, use for your own internal purposes only, and webcam images are excluded from the general permission to reuse Windy visuals. AI or ML training and caching are not mentioned.

human.unknown: Who operates each camera. Terms define webcams as owned or operated by third-party Webcam Operators; no operator identity check is documented.

application.unknown: Whether images come straight from the camera or are re-uploaded or edited; terms say images 'may be further processed' by Windy. No signing or capture attestation is documented.

camera.unknown: Whether the feed is a real camera view or a looped or replaced image; no checks documented, and Windy says it has 'absolutely no control over the images'.

time.method: API returns lastUpdatedOn (ISO 8601) per webcam
time.unknown: How the timestamp is set (camera clock or upload time) and whether stale or frozen images are detected. 'Active' only means updated within 24 hours.

location.method: API returns WGS84 latitude/longitude plus city, region and country for each webcam
location.unknown: Whether coordinates are operator-entered or checked, and where the camera actually points.

content.unknown: Whether images are staged, overlaid or heavily compressed. Windy gives no guarantee and takes no responsibility for webcam content. Status values (unapproved, rejected, duplicate) suggest listings are reviewed, but no review process is documented.

corroboration.unknown: No cross-checking between cameras or against other sources documented; each webcam has an edit URL for public feedback.

auth.how_to_get: Register a Windy account and create a Webcams API key at https://api.windy.com/keys (sign-in required); a new key may take a few minutes to become active worldwide. The key must not be published or shared with third parties.

endpoints.params: nearby={lat},{lon},{radius_km} (max 250 km); bbox={north_lat},{east_lon},{south_lat},{west_lon}; categories (max 10), categoryOperation (and|or), continents (max 2), countries, regions, cities, webcamIds (max 50, overrides other filters); include=categories,images,location,player,urls; limit (0-50, default 10); offset (max 1000 free, 10000 professional); sortKey (popularity|createdOn), sortDirection; lang
endpoints.notes: Use include=images to get current/daylight image URLs and sizes; include=player for live and timelapse embed URLs. Image URLs carry expiring tokens and return HTTP 401 once expired.

endpoints.params: include=categories,images,location,player,urls; lang
endpoints.notes: Single webcam with fresh image URLs; response has status (active, inactive, ...), lastUpdatedOn, viewCount, location, player URLs and provider URL.

endpoints.params: northLat, southLat, eastLon, westLon, zoom (4-18), include, lang
endpoints.notes: Webcams spread for map display in a bounding box; maximum box size depends on zoom level.

endpoints.params: lang
endpoints.notes: Also /continents, /countries, /regions, /cities return geo codes usable as filters.
Basic info for all webcams in one file; professional tier only.

api.rate_limits: No numeric rate limit published. Terms forbid intensive use of any endpoint by automated software, continuous scanning of a significant number of webcams, downloading significant portions of image history, and placing inappropriate load on the API. Tier limits: pagination offset 1000 (free) vs 10000 (professional), limit max 50 per call.

mcp.notes: No Windy or Windy webcams server in the official MCP Registry (searches 'windy', 'windyty', 'webcam' on 2026-10-26).

api.notes: No OAuth: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and oauth-authorization-server return 404 on api.windy.com and windy.com. The all-webcams export returns 403 without a key.

freshness.typical_age: Most recent image uploaded by each camera; varies per camera (see lastUpdatedOn)
freshness.notes: Current and daylight images plus a live player for streaming cameras. Timelapse players (day/month/year/lifetime) show past imagery but irlpls uses only the current image. An Active Webcam is one updated within the last 24 hours. No on-demand capture.

delivery.basis: Docs: call /webcams/api/v3/webcams or /webcams/api/v3/webcams/{webcamId} every time the page is loaded to get current image URLs, whose tokens expire after 10 minutes (free) or 24 hours (professional).

payment.notes: Free tier needs no payment. Professional is an annual subscription paid in advance through a third party when upgrading on api.windy.com, renewing automatically until cancelled. No agent payment rail is documented; the payment processor and accepted methods are not named.

requester.checks: A Windy account is needed to create an API key; requests are identified by key and Windy may log API use.
requester.unknown: No identity or use-case check beyond account registration is documented.

sources.claim: Auth header x-windy-api-key; keys at api.windy.com/keys, may take minutes to activate; image URL tokens expire after 10 minutes (free) or 24 hours (professional) and then return HTTP 401; call /webcams or /webcams/{webcamId} on every page load

OpenAPI 3.0 spec (decoded from the docs page's SvelteKit data file): endpoints /webcams/api/v3/webcams, /webcams/{webcamId}, /map/clusters (zoom 4-18), /categories, /continents, /countries, /regions, /cities, /webcams/export/all-webcams.json (professional only); nearby max radius 250 km, bbox format, limit 0-50, offset max 1000 free / 10000 professional, categories max 10 of 18, continents max 2, webcamIds max 50; include values; response fields status (active, inactive, unapproved, disabled, rejected, duplicate, merged), lastUpdatedOn, WGS84 location, player live/day/month/year/lifetime URLs, urls detail/edit/provider; securityScheme apiKey header x-windy-api-key
Unauthenticated GET returned HTTP 403 {"message":"Missing Header 'x-windy-api-key' with API key"} on 2026-10-26

Pricing (api.windy.com/webcams redirects here): 'largest repository of webcams worldwide'; Free: link images to windy.com or embed timelapse player, image size limited, image URL valid 15 minutes, offset 1000; Professional 9 990 EUR/year: ad-free player, full-size images, URL valid 24 hours, offset 10 000, list all webcams via a single call

Webcams API terms summary: use images only at original or smaller size and only via API URLs; link every image to the webcam page or player; credit 'Webcams provided by windy.com - add a webcam'; no inappropriate bandwidth load; data used 'as is'; links to the full specific terms

Specific Terms of Use of the Windy Webcams API (effective 1 Sept 2023): webcams owned/operated by third-party Webcam Operators, may be further processed by Windy; Active Webcam = updated within 24 hours; no guarantee of active webcam count, availability or image quality, no control over content; key created at registration; access logged; Professional fees paid as in-advance annual subscription through a third party, auto-renewing; free tier not only in paid part of an app; misuse includes continuous scanning, intensive automated use, identifying individuals, stretching images, non-API image URLs; no API access or key sharing with third parties; no publishing graphics displaying webcam images; redistribution of API data and Content forbidden; mandatory attribution; ads may run in free version; IP stays with Windy and suppliers

General Windy terms (effective 1 Sept 2023): own internal use only, no redistribution; no selling, renting, sublicensing Content; no crawling or automated collection; Windy and suppliers retain ownership of Content; webcam images excluded from the Visualizations permission and governed by the webcam specific terms; Content may be removed without notice. No AI-training clause
Windy staff (forum, 2024-04-19): free webcam API has only low-resolution images; use is fine if Windy is credited as image provider
Windy staff (forum, 2026-05-28): '70 000+' webcams; paid API offers the fullest size received from the source
No Windy or Windy webcams MCP server in the official registry (only unrelated 'windy-word-mcp')

No OAuth metadata or discovery files: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, oauth-authorization-server, ucp, agent-card.json and irlpls all return 404 on api.windy.com (and www.windy.com, webcams.windy.com, account.windy.com)

cards.name: WSDOT highway cameras
cards.summary: Washington State DOT publishes about 1,700 camera feeds (state highways, mountain passes, airports, ferry terminals, and some partner cameras such as Oregon DOT's around Portland), each a still JPEG that refreshes about every 5 minutes with the date and time printed on it. The full camera list with image links is free and keyless as RSS, KML or an ArcGIS feature service, and the images themselves need no key. The Traveler Information REST API adds road, milepost, owner and active-status fields and needs a free access code sent by email.
cards.short: Live still images from about 1,700 Washington State highway, pass, airport and ferry cameras; free, no key needed.

tasks: list every camera with title, coordinates and current image URL, keyless (RSS, KML or ArcGIS FeatureServer)
query cameras by area or attribute through the keyless ArcGIS FeatureServer
list highway cameras with coordinates, road name, milepost, direction, region, owner and active status (REST API, access code)
search cameras by state route, region and milepost range (REST API, access code)
fetch a camera's current still image, stamped with date and time
see traffic, snow and road conditions on Washington highways and mountain passes, and conditions at airports and ferry terminals

pricing.model: free public government service
pricing.notes: No charge. The camera list (RSS, KML, ArcGIS) and the images need no key; the REST API needs a free access code sent by email.

latency.typical: Images refresh about every 5 minutes (WSDOT); in a 28-image sample on 2026-10-26, 26 were under 10 minutes old and most under 2 minutes.
latency.notes: In the same sample one listed image (I-5 at MP 139.2: Emerald St) had not changed since 2026-07-02 and one airport image returned 404, so check the time printed on each image or its Last-Modified header.

coverage.notes: 1,706 cameras listed on 2026-10-26 across WSDOT regions ER, NC, NW, OL, OS, SC, SW and WA: mostly Washington state highways and passes, plus about 100 airport cameras, about 45 ferry-terminal cameras, and 65 Oregon cameras in the Portland area (region OS, many served from Oregon DOT's tripcheck.com). Some cameras belong to other agencies (CameraOwner, OwnerURL fields), and the REST IsActive field can be false.

licensing.summary: WSDOT provides travel information 'as-is' and 'as available' and disclaims all warranties of accuracy and timeliness. Images carry a '© WSDOT' overlay and the website footer says 'All Rights Reserved'. The ArcGIS camera service's licence says the feed is intended for 'low volume' use and that WSDOT may cancel or restrict access for any reason. No reuse licence for camera images was found, and nothing names AI training or resale. Some images come from other agencies (e.g. Oregon DOT).

freshness.typical_age: About 5 minutes or less
freshness.notes: Only the current image is served; no archive of past frames is offered. Each image has its date and time printed in the corner.

auth.how_to_get: The RSS, KML and ArcGIS camera lists and the image URLs on images.wsdot.wa.gov need no key.
Enter your email address on https://wsdot.wa.gov/traffic/api/ to be sent an Access Code; pass it as the AccessCode query parameter. Needed for the REST and WSDL services only.

endpoints.notes: Keyless. RSS 2.0 of all cameras: guid (camera ID), title, link (image URL), image width and height. The item date is the feed date, not the image time.
Keyless. KML of all cameras grouped by region folder, with coordinates and image URL.

endpoints.notes: Keyless ArcGIS query. Fields: OBJECTID (CameraID), CameraTitle, ImageURL, CompassDirection; point geometry in Web Mercator unless outSR is set. Licence: 'low volume' use.

endpoints.notes: All cameras: CameraID, CameraLocation (Description, Direction, Latitude, Longitude, MilePost, RoadName), CameraOwner, OwnerURL, Description, DisplayLatitude, DisplayLongitude, ImageURL, ImageWidth, ImageHeight, IsActive, Region, SortOrder, Title. Returns HTTP 401 'The supplied access code was missing or invalid' without a code. JSONP via callback.

endpoints.params: AccessCode, StateRoute, Region, StartingMilepost, EndingMilepost
AccessCode, CameraID

endpoints.notes: Keyless current JPEG, as given in each camera's ImageURL; Last-Modified header gives the image time. Some ImageURLs point to other hosts (e.g. tripcheck.com).

time.unknown: The timestamp is an unsigned overlay. Some listed cameras serve stale images (one sampled image was months old), so a recent time must be checked on every image.

location.method: Cameras have published coordinates, road name, milepost and view direction; WSDOT says images include state route and milepost
location.unknown: Pan-tilt cameras may point elsewhere than the listed direction

cards.name: XDOF
cards.short: Robot training data to order: teleoperation, egocentric capture and real-robot policy evaluations.

tasks: custom robot data collection to client specifications, with annotation
bespoke teleoperation data recorded on the specific robot being trained
generalized teleoperation data on bimanual YAM stations (pick and place, folding, insertion, tool use, assembly, tying)
egocentric data from collectors wearing body sensors while doing everyday tasks
collection at partner venues: retail, logistics, industrial and urban sites
DAgger-style data collection
real-world policy evaluations on XDOF's robot fleet, returning success rates, failure modes and every trial episode with language annotations

pricing.model: Quote after contact

latency.typical: Not published for data collection; evaluations: initial results within 24 hours
latency.notes: XDOF states no turnaround for collection projects. For its Evaluations service it says: 'We can turn around initial results within 24 hours.'

freshness.typical_age: Captured after the project is scoped with the client

regions: Latin America (Mexico and Brazil, being built out)
coverage.notes: No coverage list is published. licensing.summary: No commercial or data terms are published. The site Terms of Service (updated 9 Sep 2026) govern only use of the website: users keep ownership of content they submit, and XDOF gets a licence to use it 'solely in connection with operating and providing the Site and our services'. cards.name: Zeitview
cards.summary: Asset intelligence company (formerly DroneBase) whose pilots collect drone, fixed-wing and robotic-crawler data for energy, utility and property assets, then add AI analysis and expert review. It also sells fixed-price drone photo and video packages for US commercial real estate, and has a contact-gated Partners API for bulk mission orders.
cards.short: Drone inspections of energy, utility and property assets; fixed-price US real estate drone photo packages.

tasks: solar inspection (visual and thermal)
wind turbine inspection (onshore and offshore; external and internal blades, towers, nacelles; lightning protection testing)
electric utility circuit patrol, vegetation encroachment, thermal hotspot and substation inspection
aerial methane detection and quantification for oil and gas
roof, facade, pavement and landscaping property assessments with 1-100 condition scores
drone aerial photos, HD video clips and edited marketing videos for US commercial real estate

pricing.model: quote (enterprise inspections); published packages for US commercial real estate
pricing.unit: per listing (commercial real estate Images Package)
pricing.notes: Commercial real estate, per listing: Images $379, Starter $479, Pro $649. Strip, convenience, neighborhood and community centers (up to 400,000 sq ft), per center: Images $409, Starter $579, Pro $769. Each package includes up to one hour of flight time on site and image hosting. Volume and enterprise pricing by contact. Enterprise terms: fees in USD, quotes valid 90 days, fees non-cancellable and non-refundable.

latency.typical: Real estate: flight within a few days (weather permitting); images 2 business days after the flight, edited videos 3-5 business days
latency.notes: Real estate buyers choose between faster turnaround and clearer skies. Partners API: scheduled missions must be booked at least 24 hours ahead, and the availability preview covers the next four days. No turnaround published for enterprise inspections. Terms treat severe weather as force majeure.

delivery.basis: Commercial real estate page: "Zeitview will visit and fly the site within a few days (subject to weather). After the flight, allow two additional business days for aerial marketing packages, and three to five business days for edited marketing videos." Other services: not published.

freshness.typical_age: Captured after the order; delivered days after the flight
freshness.notes: Each image in the Partners API carries a taken_at timestamp. Zeitview also analyses data that customers collect themselves (bring your own data).

coverage.notes: The About page claims coverage in 80+ countries and "the largest drone pilot network in the industry". Other pages give lower, segment-specific figures: properties 20+ countries, solar 70+, wind 40. The properties and solar pages claim 80,000 pilots; the utilities page says 11K+. Real estate packages cover "anywhere in the continental United States". No country list is published. The Partners API rejects missions in FAA-protected airspace. Per-country density and lead times are not published.

licensing.summary: General Terms and Conditions (dated October 8, 2025): Zeitview owns its services and "related technology and deliverables", and the customer acquires no IP in them (8.1). The customer owns its Confidential Information and Customer Data, defined as data about the customer (2.3, 8.2). Services are for the customer's "own internal or personal purposes" (5.1). The customer grants Zeitview a perpetual, worldwide, sublicensable licence to Customer Data to provide services, optimise them and create anonymised data sets (8.3). Zeitview may use service data, including AI-generated annotations and anonymised data sets, to improve and develop its services, and may disclose it in aggregate or de-identified form (8.6). The commercial real estate page instead says "All drone aerial photography is yours to own and use as you like". Neither document mentions AI or model training rights for the buyer, or resale.

human.method: "Certified pilots" capture the data. Real estate pilots are "vetted and tested", and Zeitview says it is FAA-permitted for commercial flight and insured at every job site. Partners API missions record pilot_accepted, pilot_arrived and pilot_departed timestamps.
human.unknown: How pilot identity and certification are checked, and whether the delivered files were captured by that pilot. Customers may also upload their own data.

application.unknown: No claim that capture goes through a controlled or attested app. The Partners API lets some integrations use a third-party flight app and upload tool, and nothing says imagery cannot be replaced before upload.

camera.method: RGB, thermal, lidar and methane sensors on drones, fixed-wing aircraft and robotic crawlers
camera.unknown: Sensor output is not signed or tamper-evident, and there is no C2PA support. Nothing rules out edited images or photos of a screen.

time.method: Each image from the Partners API carries a taken_at timestamp, and missions carry status timestamps. Each methane detection includes a timestamp.
time.unknown: The source of taken_at (likely camera metadata) is not documented, and it is not signed or checked against an independent clock.

location.method: Data is geotagged to the asset or component. Each image from the Partners API carries GPS latitude, longitude and altitude. Methane detections include a precise GPS location.
location.unknown: Positional accuracy, where the geotag comes from, and resistance to GPS spoofing or substituted files are not documented.

content.method: AI models flag anomalies, then certified analysts or domain experts review and validate each finding before delivery
content.unknown: Review error rates are not published, and nothing says a fabricated or staged capture would be caught. The terms say Zeitview "does not review the information collected during performance" of its services (6.5).

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms a capture. Repeat surveys and the portfolio view are Zeitview's own data. The FAQ calls its methane measurement EPA-approved, but Zeitview is not named on EPA's alternative test methods page.

auth.how_to_get: The docs say: "In order to access this API, please contact our team." Mission packages (package_id) are also defined with Zeitview's team.

endpoints.notes: Dry run that saves nothing. Checks FAA airspace and returns four days of hourly timeslots with pilot availability and weather. No price. V1 at /v1/partners/missions/preview checks airspace only.

endpoints.params: external_id (required, unique; prevents duplicates), package.id, location (name, coordinate, address, GeoJSON annotations), instructions, reference_id, portfolio, scheduled_at_start/end (same day, at least 24h ahead)
endpoints.notes: Airspace is checked asynchronously; a rejection arrives by email or webhook. Cancel with DELETE /v1/partners/missions/{mission_id}. Re-shoot and reschedule at /reshoot and /schedule.
Status and activity log. Optional HMAC-SHA256-signed webhooks (X-Dronebase-Signature), enabled by support.

endpoints.params: reference_id
endpoints.notes: Up to 50 missions matching the reference id

endpoints.params: page, per_page (default 100, max 1000)
endpoints.notes: Signed image URLs that expire after about 6 hours, with taken_at, GPS and shot type for each image

mcp.notes: Searches of the official MCP Registry for "zeitview" and "dronebase" returned no servers (2026-10-26).

api.notes: The Zeitview Partners API (formerly the DroneBase API) creates missions in bulk, server to server. The docs list only a sandbox host, https://sandbox-api.dronebase.com, which did not resolve on 2026-10-26. The production host is not published. Download URLs are signed and time-limited since May 1, 2026. The marketing pages say Asset Insights is "built as an API", but no public docs for it were found. Real estate packages can also be ordered in the web Client Dashboard (clients.zeitview.com).

payment.notes: Enterprise terms: Zeitview invoices by email, payment is due within 30 days by electronic transfer in USD, and orders are subject to credit approval. Payment methods for online real estate orders are not stated on public pages.

requester.checks: All orders are subject to approval by Zeitview, including credit approval (terms 1.7). Users must be 18 or older and not barred by US sanctions (OFAC), and must provide payment information (Terms of Service 3). Missions in FAA-protected airspace are rejected (Partners API).
requester.unknown: Whether Zeitview checks the requester's authority over the property, or the purpose of a capture, is not documented.
